docs.title: What OpenDepot serves
docs.text:
OpenDepot is an open source artifact registry that runs in your Kubernetes cluster. It serves:

  • Agent Skills and Agents published from Git repositories and installed with the opendepot CLI.
    • Signed when published and checked before install. Agent hooks run opendepot verify before each tool call and block the call until an edited skill or agent is restored. See verifying with agent hooks.
  • Modules and providers for OpenTofu and Terraform, through the registry protocol.

MCP servers and OCI artifacts are planned. Registry clients read through the server. Kubernetes RBAC governs changes to artifacts. The server's only Kubernetes write path is ScanPolicy, which is off by default.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Install

    Deploy with the Helm chart, or run a local registry with kind. Start with the Modules and Providers quickstart or the Agents and Skills quickstart. See installation.

  • Publish Skills and Agents

    Publish Skills and Agents from Git tags or branches, either as standalone resources or through a Depot. See publishing Agents and Skills.

  • Consume Skills and Agents

    Install versioned Skills and Agents with the opendepot CLI, which verifies signed checksums before use. See consuming Agents and Skills.

  • Publish modules and providers

    Create a Depot that polls your module and provider sources, or manage them declaratively with GitOps. See the Depot workflow.

  • Consume modules and providers

    Point OpenTofu or Terraform at the registry. See consuming modules and consuming providers, or compose them into a validated root module with the Assembly Line.

  • Browse and secure

    Browse artifacts in the OpenDepot Workshop, manage Security Policies, and review vulnerability scanning.

For how the system fits together, see Architecture. For deployment options, see Configuration. For API and CLI details, see Reference.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: OpenDepot is a Kubernetes-native artifact registry. Kubernetes resources describe the modules, providers, skills, agents, versions, and discovery jobs that OpenDepot should manage. Controllers reconcile those resources, the server exposes them through the OpenTofu and Terraform registry protocols and the agents.v1 API, and a storage backend holds the artifacts.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'defaultRenderer': 'elk'}} }%%
graph TD
    CLI["OpenTofu / Terraform CLI"]
    OpenDepotCLI["opendepot CLI\nSkills and Agents"]

    Server["Server\nRegistry Protocol and agents.v1 API"]
    UI["OpenDepot Workshop"]
    Dex["Dex\nOIDC Identity Broker"]
    IdP["Upstream IdP"]

    Depot["Depot\nController"]
    Module["Module\nController"]
    Provider["Provider\nController"]
    Agent["Agent\nController\nSkills and Agents"]
    Version["Version\nController"]

    Storage[("Storage Backend\nS3 · Azure · GCS · Filesystem")]
    GitHub["GitHub\nReleases API"]
    ProviderRegistry["Upstream Provider Registry\nOpenTofu · Terraform"]
    Jev["TypeSafe Jev\nOptional assessment"]

    CLI -->|registry requests| Server
    OpenDepotCLI -->|agents.v1 requests| Server
    CLI -->|tofu login| Dex
    Dex -->|federates auth| IdP
    Server -.->|validates OIDC keys| Dex
    UI -->|browse API| Server

    Depot -->|discovers releases| GitHub
    Depot -->|discovers versions| ProviderRegistry
    Depot -->|creates or updates| Module
    Depot -->|creates or updates| Provider
    Depot -->|creates or updates| Agent
    Module -->|creates| Version
    Provider -->|creates| Version
    Agent -->|creates| Version
    Version -->|fetches archives| GitHub
    Version -->|fetches binaries| ProviderRegistry
    Version -->|uploads artifacts| Storage
    Version -.->|optional content assessment| Jev
    Server -->|reads metadata and artifacts| Storage

The diagram shows two cooperating paths:

  • Consumption: OpenTofu, Terraform, OpenDepot Workshop, and the opendepot CLI read metadata through the Server. The Server authenticates requests, reads Kubernetes resources, and serves or redirects artifacts from storage. The opendepot CLI uses the agents.v1 protocol to install Skills and Agents.
  • Reconciliation: Depot discovers upstream releases and creates declarative Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources. The Module, Provider, and Agent controllers turn those resources into Version resources, and the Version controller fetches, scans, checksums, and stores the artifacts.

docs.title: Reconciliation Flow
docs.text:
1. A user creates a Module, Provider, Skill, Agent, or Depot resource.
  2. The Depot controller polls GitHub and the configured provider registry when a Depot is present. It resolves version constraints and reconciles discovered modules, providers, skills, and agents.
  3. The Module controller creates one Version resource for each module version. The Provider controller creates one Version for each provider version and operating system/architecture combination. The Agent controller creates one Version for each Skill and Agent version.
  4. The Version controller downloads the upstream artifact, computes its checksum, runs configured scans, and uploads it to storage. For Skills and Agents, it packages the source repository into an archive, signs SHA256SUMS, and runs the optional Jev assessment.
  5. The Server reads the Kubernetes resources and exposes synced versions through the registry protocols and the agents.v1 protocol.
  6. Subsequent reconciliations repair drift, discover new releases, and preserve immutable artifact content according to the configured policy.

docs.title: Depot Controller
docs.text:
The Depot controller is the discovery layer. It polls:

  • GitHub Releases API for module releases
  • GitHub repositories for Skill and Agent tags, or branch heads when ref is set
  • registry.opentofu.org or registry.terraform.io for provider releases

It applies version constraints, creates or updates the corresponding Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources, and records the managed resource names in Depot status. Configure the polling interval with pollingIntervalMinutes.

See Depot Discovery for configuration examples.

docs.title: Module and Provider Controllers
docs.text:
These controllers translate high-level registry resources into individual version work items:

  • The Module controller creates a Version for each entry in Module.spec.versions.
  • The Provider controller creates a Version for each version and each requested operating system and architecture.
  • Both controllers track the latest version and garbage-collect Versions removed from spec.versions. When versionHistoryLimit is set, the Module and Provider controllers trim spec.versions to the newest N versions, and the removed Versions are garbage-collected.

A provider with two versions, two operating systems, and two architectures produces eight Version resources.

docs.title: Agent Controller
docs.text:
The Agent controller reconciles Skill and Agent resources. It runs in the agent deployment and is disabled by default. Set agent.enabled: true in the chart values to deploy it.

Like the Module and Provider controllers, it creates a Version for each entry in spec.versions, trims the list when versionHistoryLimit is set, and removes Versions that are no longer declared. Branch-sourced Skills and Agents create a Version for each new commit. See Branch sourcing.

docs.title: Version Controller
docs.text:
The Version controller performs the artifact work:

  • Downloads module archives from GitHub or provider binaries from the configured upstream registry.
  • Packages Skill and Agent source repositories into archives, signs their SHA256SUMS file, and runs deterministic checks before a Version is synced.
  • Assigns stable UUID7 storage filenames and computes SHA256 checksums.
  • Runs module IaC scans when scanning.enabled is true, and provider binary and source scans when scanning.providerScanning is also true.
  • Generates provider SHA256SUMS signatures when provider GPG signing is configured.
  • Runs the optional Jev assessment on Skill and Agent Versions. When Jev is enabled, the content of a Version is sent to the TypeSafe Jev endpoint. See Data handling.
  • Uploads artifacts to the configured storage backend and updates Version status.

UUID7 filenames prevent clients from guessing storage object names. When module immutability is enabled, reconciliation verifies that the stored checksum still matches the published version.

docs.title: Branch sourcing
docs.text: When branch sourcing is enabled, the Depot follows the branch head of a Skill or Agent source. Each new commit becomes a Version named for its commit and labeled with opendepot.defdev.io/commit. The version controller packages and signs it, then assigns a semver. The parent Skill or Agent records the commit, the discovery time, the state, and the Version name in versionRefs. The Server resolves a branch Version through the parent's versionRefs entry, and only when the Version's label matches the parent and its spec.version is set. Branch sources poll only when pollingIntervalMinutes is set on the Depot. For the full behavior, see Branch sourcing.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
The Server is the registry API. It:

  • Implements the Module Registry and Provider Registry protocols.
  • Implements the agents.v1 protocol for Skills and Agents.
  • Serves service discovery from /.well-known/terraform.json.
  • Reads Module, Provider, Skill, Agent, Version, and access-control resources from the Kubernetes API.
  • Serves artifacts directly or returns storage-native pre-signed redirects.
  • Writes ScanPolicy objects for the Workshop when server.policyManagement.enabled is true. Writes are off by default.
  • Records download events as Prometheus metrics for OpenDepot Workshop statistics.

Authentication can use OIDC, Kubernetes bearer tokens, or anonymous access for local evaluation. OIDC enables tofu login and applies GroupBinding rules to JWT group claims. See Authentication.

docs.title: Prometheus Monitoring
docs.text: The chart can deploy a kube-prometheus-stack installation, or use an existing Prometheus deployment through server.stats.prometheusURL. The server exposes /metrics on the metrics port of its Service, and the chart's ServiceMonitor discovers that endpoint for Prometheus Operator installations. Registry gauges expose resource counts, archive sizes, synchronization state, and security findings.

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop
docs.text:
The optional UI is a Next.js application fronted by NGINX. NGINX routes browser pages to the UI and registry paths such as /opendepot/* and /.well-known/terraform.json to the Server, keeping browser requests same-origin.

The UI reads the Server's browse API to display modules, providers, versions, scan findings, Depot relationships, and download statistics.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The chart supports S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage, and a shared filesystem. The Version controller writes artifacts and the Server reads or redirects downloads from the same backend.

Prometheus stores download counters and registry gauges used by the Registry Explorer. It is separate from registry state: Kubernetes stores the declarative resources and status used by the controllers and Server.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• Kubernetes is the control plane. Registry state, desired configuration, and reconciliation status are Kubernetes resources.
  • Kubernetes RBAC governs changes. Controllers reconcile artifact state, and clients consume the registry through standard protocols. The Server's only Kubernetes write path is ScanPolicy, which is off by default.
  • Discovery is declarative. A Depot expresses what upstream sources and version constraints to follow; reconciliation handles the resulting updates.
  • Artifacts are immutable by policy. Checksums, stable storage names, and optional immutability enforcement protect published versions.
  • Authentication is layered. OIDC, Kubernetes bearer tokens, and anonymous access support different deployment stages without changing the registry model.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Thank you for your interest in contributing to OpenDepot! Please read our CONTRIBUTING.md on GitHub for guidelines on opening issues, submitting pull requests, and the development workflow.

Pull requests that change service code run the e2e workflow. It builds the service images and fails on fixable CRITICAL or HIGH findings from trivy-action (.github/workflows/e2e.yaml). Suppressions for that scan go in .trivyignore.yaml.

docs.title: Security Scanning
docs.text:
The security-review agent (.github/agents/security-review.agent.md) runs these scans manually:

  • trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH against each service image and the Valkey subchart image.
  • trivy config --severity CRITICAL,HIGH chart/opendepot/ for Kubernetes misconfigurations.

The version-controller image bundles Trivy, downloaded from the TRIVY_VERSION release in services/version/Dockerfile and verified against its published SHA256 checksum. Upstream binaries are never built from source. If an upstream Trivy release has a HIGH CVE with no available fix, track it in a GitHub issue before adding a suppression. Include the issue URL as a comment in the ignore file. Chart-level suppressions go in chart/opendepot/.trivyignore.

Note

Resolve CVEs in the controller's own dependencies. Do not suppress them.

docs.title: Generating API Types
docs.text: make manifests in api/v1alpha1 runs controller-gen with crd:allowDangerousTypes=true. The flag is required because types.go has float64 fields, such as the Jev policy thresholds and assessment scores. Without it, controller-gen fails on those fields. Do not remove the flag. After changing types.go, run make manifests to regenerate the CRDs and make generate to regenerate zz_generated.deepcopy.go.

docs.title: Agent Presign E2E Testing
docs.text:
The agent presign e2e scenarios use an AWS emulator sidecar. The emulator is test-only. It is not part of the chart or the released images. The scenarios are skipped unless E2E_AWS_EMULATOR=true is set.

The run needs an isolated Kind cluster. The test fails when KIND_CLUSTER is unset or set to the shared opendepot cluster. Use a separate name, and keep the cluster with KEEP_KIND=1 if you want to inspect it.

The Agent presign scenarios cover two cases. Anonymous auth serves a public agent. OIDC auth serves a private agent, and it checks a 401 without a token and a 307 for a bound request.

The emulator port-forward uses local port 9297. Free that port before the run.

make build-aws-emulator builds the emulator image for PLATFORM, which defaults to linux/arm64. The emulator Dockerfile accepts only arm64.

kind create cluster --name opendepot-agent-presign
make build-aws-emulator load-aws-emulator KIND_CLUSTER=opendepot-agent-presign
cd services/server
make test-e2e KIND_CLUSTER=opendepot-agent-presign KEEP_KIND=1 E2E_AWS_EMULATOR=true E2E_FOCUS="Agent presign"
make cleanup-test-e2e KIND_CLUSTER=opendepot-agent-presign

The e2e values file, values-agent-presign-e2e.yaml, sets test-only values such as the emulator sidecar and path-style S3. Do not use it as a production reference.

docs.title: Local OIDC E2E Testing
docs.text:
The repository ships a set of make targets for end-to-end OIDC testing against a local Kind cluster. They wire together Kind, Helm, Dex v2.45.0, filesystem storage, mkcert TLS, and a static test user so that you can run tofu login without any cloud infrastructure.

Note

The make targets use opendepot.localtest.me as the default registry hostname. This hostname resolves to 127.0.0.1 via public DNS — no /etc/hosts editing required. You can override it with OIDC_REGISTRY_HOST=<hostname> if you need a custom local name, in which case make oidc-hosts will add the entry to /etc/hosts.

Target Purpose make oidc-hosts Adds $(OIDC_REGISTRY_HOST) → 127.0.0.1 to /etc/hosts (requires sudo). Only needed when using a custom OIDC_REGISTRY_HOST that does not resolve via public DNS make oidc-tls Generates a locally-trusted mkcert TLS cert for opendepot.localtest.me, localhost, and 127.0.0.1 and creates the opendepot-tls Kubernetes Secret make oidc-deploy PASS=<password> Deploys OpenDepot + Dex v2.45.0 with filesystem storage and a static OIDC test user make oidc-forward Port-forwards the server (localhost:8080) and Dex (localhost:5556) make oidc-login Runs tofu login opendepot.localtest.me:8080 make oidc-test-resources Creates a sample Module and a GroupBinding for the test user's group make oidc-verify-module Runs an authenticated request against the test module to verify the full auth flow make oidc-test-clean Removes the test Module and GroupBinding make oidc-stop Stops all port-forwards make oidc-setup PASS=<password> Runs all setup steps (deploy, oidc-tls, oidc-deploy, oidc-forward) in sequence

Prerequisites: kind, kubectl, Helm 3, mkcert, OpenTofu, and either htpasswd (from httpd) or the Python bcrypt package for hashing the test user password.

Full setup from a freshly created Kind cluster:

# One-time: install mkcert CA into the system trust store
mkcert -install

# Create a kind cluster (if you don't have one already)
kind create cluster --name opendepot

# Build and load images, generate TLS cert, deploy, and port-forward
make oidc-setup PASS=mysecretpassword

Login and test:

# Opens tofu login - authenticate in the browser
make oidc-login 

# Username: dev@example.com
# Password: Set during `make oidc-setup PASS=<PASSWORD>`

# Now create a test Module and GroupBinding for the static user's group
make oidc-test-resources

# Change to test/local in the OpenDepot project repo and run `tofu init`
cd test/local && tofu init

If successful you should see:

Initializing the backend...
Initializing modules...
Downloading opendepot.localtest.me:8080/opendepot-system/terraform-aws-key-pair/aws 2.0.3 for key_pair...
- key_pair in .terraform/modules/key_pair

Initializing provider plugins...

OpenTofu has been successfully initialized!

You may now begin working with OpenTofu. Try running "tofu plan" to see
any changes that are required for your infrastructure. All OpenTofu commands
should now work.

If you ever set or change modules or backend configuration for OpenTofu,
rerun this command to reinitialize your working directory. If you forget, other
commands will detect it and remind you to do so if necessary.

The oidc-deploy target configures server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true, so Dex is reverse-proxied through the server itself — the recommended setup. make oidc-forward port-forwards only the server (localhost:8080); Dex is reachable at /dex/* through that same port-forward, so there's no need to also forward Dex directly.

The ui-setup-oidc target configures the same dexProxy setup for the CLI login path, and additionally routes the UI's own browser login through the UI's nginx, which has a /dex location proxying to the server for environments without a real Ingress controller (local Kind has none). make ui-forward port-forwards only the UI (localhost:8080); both tofu login and the UI's own OIDC login work through that single port-forward.

ui-setup-oidc still writes ~/.tofurc (via make ui-tofurc), since this local registry is plain HTTP and OpenTofu's service discovery only works over HTTPS — a CLI config host block is required regardless of dexProxy. The login.v1 URLs in that block now point at Dex through the single UI port-forward instead of a separate Dex port-forward.

ui-setup-oidc also builds and loads the -assembly server and version-controller images (INCLUDE_TOFU=true), and ui-deploy sets server.image.tag and version.image.tag to $(TAG)-assembly so Assembly Line has the OpenTofu binary it needs. make ui-setup builds only the Trivy-enabled version-controller image and does not enable Assembly Line.

The older split-network pattern — where the server reaches Dex via the in-cluster service URL while authzUrl/tokenUrl overrides redirect the browser through a separately port-forwarded Dex — is still available and described in Split-Network OIDC, but is no longer used by the local Kind Make targets since dexProxy covers the common case with fewer port-forwards.

docs.title: Helm Chart
docs.text:
The chart is published to a GitHub Pages Helm repository at https://opendepot.defdev.io/index.yaml:

helm repo add opendepot https://opendepot.defdev.io
helm repo update

The source is in chart/opendepot/. For prerequisites and install steps, see Installation.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: Value Type Description global.namespace string Namespace for all resources. Default: opendepot-system global.imagePullPolicy string Image pull policy. Default: IfNotPresent global.image.tag string Image tag for all services. Defaults to Chart.AppVersion when blank.

docs.title: Extension Hooks
docs.text:
These values let operators add settings to the server pod. Each one defaults to an empty list ([]).

Value Type Description server.extraEnv list Extra environment variables for the server container. server.extraVolumes list Extra pod volumes. server.extraVolumeMounts list Extra volume mounts for the server container. server.extraContainers list Extra containers added to the server pod after the server container. server.extraInitContainers list Extra init containers added after the built-in init containers. Set restartPolicy: Always for a native sidecar.

extraEnv renders after the built-in environment variables. An entry with the same name as a built-in variable overrides it. If a name appears more than once, the last value wins.

server:
  extraEnv:
    - name: EXAMPLE_VAR
      value: "example"

docs.title: OIDC Authentication
docs.text:
The server.oidc section enables OIDC JWT validation. For setup, see Authentication.

Value Type Description server.oidc.enabled bool When true, enables OIDC JWT validation and advertises the login.v1 service discovery endpoint. Default: false server.oidc.issuerUrl string OIDC issuer URL (e.g., https://opendepot.example.com/dex). When blank and dex.enabled: true, auto-derives the in-cluster Dex service URL. server.oidc.clientId string OIDC client ID. Must match the Dex static client id. Default: "opendepot" server.oidc.clientSecretName string Name of an existing Secret with the OPENDEPOT_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET key. The chart does not create this Secret. When dex.enabled and server.oidc.enabled are true and a Dex static client uses secretEnv: OPENDEPOT_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, the value must match a dex.envFrom secretRef name, or the render fails. server.oidc.groupsClaim string JWT claim name containing the user's groups, used for GroupBinding evaluation. When blank, defaults to groups. Set to cognito:groups, roles, etc. for non-standard IdPs. server.oidc.allowServiceAccountFallback bool When true, Kubernetes ServiceAccount bearer tokens with a non-OIDC issuer are authenticated via the bearer-token path using the SA's own RBAC. GroupBinding is bypassed for SA tokens. Requires server.oidc.enabled: true. Default: false server.oidc.allowClientCredentials bool When true, Dex client credentials tokens whose aud is listed in clientCredentialsAudiences are accepted. The token's sub claim is mapped to a virtual group "client:<sub>" and evaluated against GroupBinding resources. Requires a Dex staticClient with grantTypes: ["client_credentials"]. Default: false server.oidc.clientCredentialsAudiences list Dex client IDs whose client credentials tokens are accepted (the token's aud must contain one of them). Passed to the server as --oidc-client-credentials-audiences. Required and non-empty when server.oidc.allowClientCredentials is true; the chart fails to render, and the server refuses to start, otherwise. Default: [] server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled bool When true and OIDC is enabled, the server reverse-proxies /dex/* requests to the bundled Dex service so Dex never needs its own public ingress or hostname. Requires dex.enabled: true and server.oidc.issuerUrl set to the external, path-based URL matching dex.config.issuer. Set to false for external OIDC providers; ignored when OIDC is disabled. Default: true server.oidc.authzUrl string Overrides the authorization URL advertised in login.v1 of /.well-known/terraform.json. Leave blank to use the URL from the OIDC provider discovery document. Not needed when server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true. Use this when the server discovers Dex via an in-cluster address but CLI clients must reach Dex at a different address (e.g. a port-forwarded URL during local Kind testing). server.oidc.tokenUrl string Overrides the token URL advertised in login.v1 of /.well-known/terraform.json. Same use-case as authzUrl. Not needed when server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true.

Example (recommended — Dex proxied through the server):

server:
  oidc:
    enabled: true
    issuerUrl: https://opendepot.example.com/dex
    clientId: opendepot
    clientSecretName: opendepot-dex-client-secret  # Existing Secret with the OPENDEPOT_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET key
    dexProxy:
      enabled: true

Warning

If dex.enabled and server.oidc.enabled are true and a Dex static client uses secretEnv: OPENDEPOT_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, the render fails unless server.oidc.clientSecretName is set and matches a dex.envFrom secretRef name. Set the same name in both places and create the Secret before installing.

docs.title: Dex Configuration
docs.text:
The dex section deploys Dex as an OIDC identity provider. Dex federates upstream IdPs (GitHub, Entra ID, Okta, LDAP, and others) and issues the JWTs that the server validates.

Value Type Description dex.enabled bool When true, deploys Dex as a subchart. Default: false dex.config.issuer string Public issuer URL. Recommended (server-proxied): same host as the server ingress, e.g. https://opendepot.example.com/dex. In-cluster (no proxy): http://opendepot-dex.opendepot-system.svc.cluster.local:5556/dex. Separately exposed: https://dex.example.com/dex dex.config.connectors array Array of upstream IdP connector configurations. See examples below. Default: [] dex.config.enablePasswordDB bool When true, enables local username/password authentication (testing only). Default: false dex.config.staticPasswords array Array of test users for local auth. Never enable in production. Default: []

Basic Example (GitHub):

dex:
  enabled: true
  config:
    issuer: https://opendepot.example.com/dex
    connectors:
      - type: github
        id: github
        name: GitHub
        config:
          clientID: <github-oauth-app-client-id>
          clientSecret: <github-oauth-app-secret>
          redirectURI: https://opendepot.example.com/dex/callback
          org: my-org  # (optional) restrict to an org

Entra ID (Azure AD) Example:

dex:
  enabled: true
  config:
    issuer: https://opendepot.example.com/dex
    connectors:
      - type: microsoft
        id: microsoft
        name: "Azure AD"
        config:
          clientID: <azure-app-id>
          clientSecret: <azure-app-secret>
          redirectURI: https://opendepot.example.com/dex/callback
          tenant: <azure-tenant-id>

For connector configuration details, refer to the Dex Connector Documentation.

Warning

Never set enablePasswordDB: true or staticPasswords in production. Use real IdP connectors instead.

docs.title: Controllers
docs.text:
These values apply to version, module, depot, and provider. Replace <service> with the controller name:

Value Type Description <service>.enabled bool Deploy the controller. Default: true (provider: false) <service>.replicaCount int Number of replicas. Default: 1 <service>.image.repository string Image repository. Default: ghcr.io/tonedefdev/opendepot/<service>-controller <service>.image.tag string Overrides global.image.tag when set. <service>.resources.requests.cpu string CPU request. Default: 100m <service>.resources.requests.memory string Memory request. Default: 512Mi for version, 128Mi for others <service>.resources.limits.memory string Memory limit. Default: 4Gi for version, 512Mi for others <service>.nodeSelector map Node selector. Default: {} <service>.tolerations list Tolerations. Default: [] <service>.affinity map Affinity rules. Default: {}

Note

provider is disabled by default because provider archives can be several hundred megabytes each. Enable it when you are ready to sync binaries.

The Version controller's init containers have fixed, bounded resources (requests 10m CPU and 16Mi memory; limits 100m CPU and 32Mi memory). The Version pod also runs a token-refresh-helper sidecar that refreshes the projected ServiceAccount token. The main controller does not mount a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token directly.

docs.title: Branch Sourcing
docs.text:
Branch sourcing lets Skill and Agent sources follow a Git branch with ref. It is off by default. The chart value below controls it for both the depot and version controllers:

Value Type Description branchSourcing.enabled bool Sets --branch-sourcing-enabled on the depot and version controllers. Default false. Both controllers read the same value.

Polling for new branch commits uses the existing pollingIntervalMinutes on the Depot. There is no separate poll-interval value. For the behavior, see Branch sourcing.

docs.title: Assembly Line
docs.text:
Assembly Line is disabled by default and requires OpenTofu. Default images do not include OpenTofu, so set server.image.tag and version.image.tag to a -assembly tag. ui.baseUrl must be an external HTTP(S) URL, because its host and port appear in generated module source addresses and the OpenTofu Provider Network Mirror URL. For provider eligibility, see Assembly Line.

Value Type Description assembly.enabled bool Enable contract/schema extraction and initialized exports. Default: false assembly.validationRegistryUrl string HTTPS registry and Provider Network Mirror origin used only by server-side OpenTofu initialization. Defaults to ui.baseUrl. assembly.validationCACertPath string Optional PEM CA bundle trusted only by the temporary OpenTofu initialization process. Default: "" assembly.tofuBinPath string OpenTofu binary path in the -assembly version and server images. Default: /usr/local/bin/tofu assembly.extractionTimeout duration Provider schema extraction timeout. Default: 5m assembly.initTimeout duration Export tofu init timeout. Default: 2m assembly.maxRequestBytes int Maximum export request body. Default: 2097152 assembly.maxNodes int Maximum total canvas nodes per export. Default: 100 assembly.maxOutputBytes int Maximum captured output per OpenTofu command. Default: 65536 assembly.workDir string Server validation workspace mount. Default: /var/lib/opendepot/assembly assembly.workspaceSizeLimit quantity Validation emptyDir size limit. Default: 1Gi

The server root filesystem is read-only. The chart mounts only assembly.workDir, as a size-limited emptyDir. For production, consider adding ephemeral-storage requests and limits under server.resources and version.resources.

For provider bindings, generated files, authentication, and validation, see Assembly Line.

docs.title: GPG Signing (Providers)
docs.text:
The server signs SHA256SUMS for provider packages with a GPG key you supply. OpenTofu and Terraform verify that signature under the Provider Registry Protocol. For setup, see GPG Signing for Providers.

Value Type Description server.gpg.secretName string Name of the Kubernetes Secret containing GPG signing credentials (OPENDEPOT_PROVIDER_GPG_KEY_ID, OPENDEPOT_PROVIDER_GPG_ASCII_ARMOR, OPENDEPOT_PROVIDER_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64). Default: ""

docs.title: Service Account & RBAC
docs.text: Value Type Description serviceAccount.create bool Create service accounts. Default: true serviceAccount.annotations map Annotations (use for IRSA/Workload Identity). Default: {} rbac.create bool Create RBAC roles and bindings. Default: true rbac.scopeToNamespace bool Use namespace-scoped Role/RoleBinding instead of ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding. Default: false

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Value Type Description storage.filesystem.enabled bool Enable shared volume for filesystem storage. Default: false storage.filesystem.mountPath string Mount path inside containers. Default: /data/modules storage.filesystem.hostPath string Use a hostPath volume (for local dev with kind). Default: "" storage.filesystem.storageClassName string StorageClass for PVC (requires ReadWriteMany). Default: "" storage.filesystem.size string PVC storage size. Default: 10Gi Value Type Description server.s3UsePathStyle bool Sets OPENDEPOT_S3_USE_PATH_STYLE on the server. Default: false

See Storage Backends for S3, Azure, and GCS configuration, which are set via environment variables rather than Helm values.

docs.title: UI Configuration
docs.text:
The ui section deploys the OpenDepot Workshop frontend. See OpenDepot Workshop for setup, OIDC login, and public visibility configuration.

Value Type Description ui.enabled bool When true, deploys the OpenDepot Workshop UI and NGINX proxy. Also suppresses server-ingress.yaml — migrate traffic to ui.ingress before enabling. Default: false ui.replicaCount int Number of UI pod replicas. Default: 1 ui.image.repository string UI container image repository. Default: ghcr.io/tonedefdev/opendepot/ui ui.image.tag string Image tag. Defaults to global.image.tag, then the chart appVersion. ui.serverHost string Upstream host:port that NGINX proxies registry requests to. Defaults to server.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:80 when blank. ui.serverCACertPath string Optional PEM CA path from the opendepot-tls Secret that Next.js trusts when connecting to a privately signed TLS server. Default: "" ui.sessionPasswordSecretName string Name of a Kubernetes Secret with a sessionPassword key (min 32 chars). Required when ui.enabled: true. ui.oidc.enabled bool Enables OIDC authorization code login in the UI. Default: false ui.oidc.issuerUrl string Public HTTPS OIDC issuer URL. Discovered endpoints must share this origin. HTTP is accepted only with global.developmentMode: true. ui.oidc.clientId string OIDC client ID for the UI. Default: "opendepot-ui". When ui.oidc.enabled: true and non-empty, the chart also passes --oidc-ui-client-id to the server so UI-issued tokens are accepted on browse and stats endpoints. See OpenDepot Workshop OIDC. ui.oidc.clientSecretName string Name of a Kubernetes Secret with a clientSecret key for the OIDC confidential client. ui.oidc.scopes string Space-separated OIDC scopes. Default: "openid profile email groups" ui.oidc.callbackPath string OIDC redirect URI path registered with the identity provider. Default: "/auth/callback" ui.auth.devTokenInput.enabled bool When true, shows a developer bearer-token input in the UI. Must be false in production. Default: false ui.ingress.enabled bool Creates a Kubernetes Ingress for the UI with split-path routing rules. Default: false ui.ingress.className string Ingress class name. ui.ingress.annotations map Annotations applied to the Ingress resource. ui.ingress.hosts list Host and path rules. ui.ingress.tls list TLS configuration for the Ingress.

docs.title: Prometheus Monitoring
docs.text:
The chart can install a minimal kube-prometheus-stack. The server Service exposes /metrics on the named metrics port (9090). The ServiceMonitor selects that Service by the app: server label and is enabled by default. It requires a Prometheus Operator. If your operator selects ServiceMonitors by label, set server.metrics.serviceMonitor.additionalLabels to match. Set server.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled: false if your monitoring discovers the endpoint another way.

The Stats page queries Prometheus over its HTTP API. To use an existing Prometheus, set server.stats.prometheusURL. This takes precedence over the in-cluster fallback:

server:
  stats:
    prometheusURL: https://prometheus.example.com

When prometheusURL is blank and monitoring.enabled: true, the server falls back to http://<release>-monitoring-prometheus.<release-namespace>.svc.cluster.local:9090. That address exists only when monitoring.bundled.enabled: true.

The bundled stack is disabled by default because the Prometheus Operator requires cluster-wide RBAC. Enable it only if that access is acceptable:

monitoring:
  bundled:
    enabled: true

Stats cover the server.stats.lookback window (default 90d), not an all-time total. For longer history, configure remoteWrite to Mimir or another Prometheus-compatible backend.

Value Type Description monitoring.enabled bool Enable OpenDepot monitoring resources, including the ServiceMonitor and the server's bundled-Prometheus fallback. Default: true monitoring.bundled.enabled bool Install the bundled kube-prometheus-stack. Default: false monitoring.prometheus.prometheusSpec.retention string Local Prometheus retention. Default: 90d monitoring.prometheus.prometheusSpec.remoteWrite list Optional remote-write targets such as Mimir for long-term storage. server.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled bool Create the OpenDepot ServiceMonitor. Default: true server.metrics.serviceMonitor.interval string ServiceMonitor scrape interval. Default: 15s server.metrics.serviceMonitor.scrapeTimeout string ServiceMonitor scrape timeout. Default: 10s server.metrics.serviceMonitor.additionalLabels map Additional labels for matching an external Prometheus Operator's ServiceMonitor selector. Default: {} server.stats.prometheusURL string Prometheus HTTP API URL. When blank, the server uses the bundled Prometheus service address only if monitoring.enabled: true; that service must be installed with monitoring.bundled.enabled: true. server.stats.lookback string Stats page query window. Default: 90d server.stats.queryTimeout duration Prometheus query timeout. Default: 5s

The bundled Prometheus stack requires cluster-wide Prometheus Operator RBAC and is disabled by default. Enable it only when that cluster-wide access is acceptable:

monitoring:
  bundled:
    enabled: true

The Stats page uses the configured lookback window, not an all-time total. For time series longer than local retention, configure remoteWrite to Mimir or another Prometheus-compatible backend and use Grafana to query the retained history.

docs.title: Source-built image dependencies
docs.text:
Trivy and OpenTofu are pinned release versions (TRIVY_VERSION and TOFU_VERSION in the Dockerfiles), verified against their published SHA256 checksums at build time. The standard Version image does not include Trivy or OpenTofu. Set INCLUDE_TRIVY=true to add Trivy, and set INCLUDE_TOFU=true to add OpenTofu. The -assembly server and Version images include OpenTofu. The -assembly Version image also includes Trivy.

See Download Tracking for details on how stats are recorded and surfaced in OpenDepot Workshop.

docs.title: Scanning Values
docs.text:
The scanning section controls Trivy-based vulnerability scanning for modules and providers. See Vulnerability Scanning for full details.

Value Type Description scanning.enabled bool Enable Trivy-based scanning. Requires a version-controller image that bundles Trivy, which the standard tag includes, and activates module IaC scanning. No PVC or CronJob is created at this level. Default: true scanning.providerScanning bool Enable provider binary and source scanning. Requires scanning.enabled: true. Creates the Trivy DB PVC and trivy-db-updater CronJob and mounts the cache volume. Default: true scanning.cacheMountPath string Mount path inside the version-controller container for the Trivy DB cache. Default: /var/cache/trivy scanning.offline bool Pass --offline-scan to Trivy, preventing network calls during scans. Only applies to provider scanning. Default: true scanning.blockOnCritical bool Halt reconciliation when CRITICAL findings are present (modules or providers). Default: false scanning.blockOnHigh bool Halt reconciliation when HIGH or CRITICAL findings are present (modules or providers). Default: false scanning.cache.storageClassName string StorageClass for the Trivy cache PVC (must support ReadWriteMany for multi-node). Omitted from the PVC manifest when blank, allowing the cluster default to apply stably across upgrades. Default: "" scanning.cache.accessMode string Access mode for the Trivy cache PVC. Default: ReadWriteMany scanning.cache.size string Size of the Trivy DB cache PVC. Default: 1Gi scanning.dbUpdater.schedule string Cron schedule for the Trivy DB update job. Default: "0 2 * * *" scanning.dbUpdater.image.repository string Trivy image repository for the db-updater CronJob. Default: aquasec/trivy scanning.dbUpdater.image.tag string Trivy image tag for the db-updater CronJob. Default: "0.70.0"

Note

blockOnCritical and blockOnHigh are cluster-wide floors. For per-finding exemptions without loosening enforcement everywhere, create a namespaced ScanPolicy resource instead of relaxing these flags. See Policy Enforcement. The chart installs the ScanPolicy CRD and grants the version controller get/list/watch on scanpolicies automatically — no additional values are required to use it.

The optional policy-management API is intentionally separate from controller enforcement. Enabling server.policyManagement.enabled adds write verbs to the server ServiceAccount and exposes the UI CRUD surface; it does not grant users access. Configure Kubernetes Role/RoleBinding permissions for kubeconfig or bearer-token callers, or create a least-privilege SecurityGroupBinding for OIDC callers. Keep the value false when policies are applied only through GitOps.

docs.title: Tilt and monitoring scope
docs.text:
The repository's Tilt profile (tilt/values.yaml) is for development only. It enables global.developmentMode, local TLS, Dex with password authentication, filesystem storage, Trivy scanning, the UI, the bundled Prometheus stack, and server.policyManagement.enabled. Do not copy these values into production.

The bundled monitoring stack scrapes OpenDepot metrics with one Prometheus and 90-day retention. Grafana, Alertmanager, node exporters, and Kubernetes component monitors are disabled. Policy audit evidence comes from server and Kubernetes logs, not Prometheus. For longer retention, configure monitoring.prometheus.prometheusSpec.remoteWrite and a durable audit-log sink.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Breaking changes and upgrade steps for each OpenDepot release. Check this page before running helm upgrade on an existing installation.

Tip

Helm does not update CRDs during helm upgrade. Always apply the latest CRDs before upgrading: 

helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -

docs.title: v0.12.0
docs.text: v0.12.0 updates the chart and application version to 0.12.0. This release adds the agents.v1 registry for Skills and Agents. The agent deployment sets a RuntimeDefault seccomp profile as part of this release.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: • Client credentials require an audience list. When server.oidc.allowClientCredentials is true, the server accepts only Dex client credentials tokens whose aud is listed in server.oidc.clientCredentialsAudiences. The chart fails to render when that list is empty. See Client credentials audiences.

docs.title: New CRDs and RBAC
docs.text:
The ScanPolicy CRD gains spec.jevExemptions and the activeJevExemptions and expiredJevExemptions status counts. The Version CRD gains the contentDigest and exemption fields on status.jevAssessment. Helm does not update CRDs during helm upgrade, so apply the chart CRDs before you upgrade.

The Version controller also needs a new RBAC rule that lets it create and patch Events in the events.k8s.io API group. The chart adds the rule. It records JevExemptionApplied and JevExemptionRevoked events.

docs.title: Critical Jev assessments set needsReview
docs.text: A Jev assessment with a Critical risk level now sets status.jevAssessment.needsReview to true, in addition to blocking the Version. Before this change, Critical blocked the Version without setting the field. A completed assessment from before this change is reused unchanged, so its needsReview value does not change until the Version is assessed again. See Thresholds.

docs.title: Client credentials audiences
docs.text:
Before this release, the server accepted a Dex client credentials token from any client ID. It now accepts only tokens whose aud is listed in clientCredentialsAudiences. Existing deployments that set server.oidc.allowClientCredentials: true must add the list before they upgrade. The chart fails to render, and the server refuses to start, when the list is empty.

server:
  oidc:
    allowClientCredentials: true
    clientCredentialsAudiences:
      - ci-pipeline

List every Dex client ID that uses the client_credentials grant. Tokens from other clients receive 401 Unauthorized after the upgrade.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. If server.oidc.allowClientCredentials is true, set server.oidc.clientCredentialsAudiences to the Dex client IDs that use the client_credentials grant. The chart fails to render without this list. For installs that do not use Helm, pass --oidc-client-credentials-audiences with a comma-separated list instead: 
    server:
  oidc:
    allowClientCredentials: true
    clientCredentialsAudiences:
      - ci-pipeline
  2. Apply the updated CRDs from the chart: 
    kubectl apply -f chart/opendepot/crds/
  3. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot chart/opendepot \
   -n opendepot-system \
   -f my-values.yaml

docs.title: New CRDs
docs.text:
The release adds the Skill and Agent CRDs. Helm does not update CRDs during helm upgrade, so apply them before you upgrade:

helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -

The agent service is disabled by default. The GroupBinding CRD gains the skillResources and agentResources fields. An empty list denies access to skills and agents, so add these fields to grant access. See agents for setup.

docs.title: Depot version history
docs.text:
The Depot CRD adds spec.global.providerConfig and spec.global.versionHistoryLimit. Depots trim spec.versions to the newest N matching versions, so trimmed versions no longer return on later polls.

Helm does not update CRDs in the crds/ directory on helm upgrade. Apply the new Depot CRD before you upgrade:

kubectl apply -f chart/opendepot/crds/opendepot.defdev.io_depots.yaml

The Depot GlobalConfig printer column now reads .spec.global, the JSON key. Before this release, the column was always blank in kubectl get depots.

docs.title: Depot global defaults
docs.text:
The global.moduleConfig and global.providerConfig blocks accept only default fields. Identity fields belong on each entry.

  • global.moduleConfig accepts fileFormat, immutable, githubClientConfig, storageConfig, and versionHistoryLimit.
  • global.providerConfig accepts operatingSystems, architectures, githubClientConfig, storageConfig, and versionHistoryLimit.
  • Neither block accepts name, namespace, sourceRepository, versionConstraints, provider, repoOwner, or repoUrl. Set these on each entry.
  • global.providerConfig.upstreamRegistry is removed. Set upstreamRegistry on each providerConfigs entry. Each entry already defaults to registry.opentofu.org, so the removed global field never applied to entries.

The API server removes fields that the restricted schema does not define when it decodes a Depot. It returns no error or warning. Existing Depots that set global.providerConfig.upstreamRegistry or an identity field in a global block have those fields pruned silently. The controller already ignored these fields, so pruning does not change what the Depot manages. Remove them from your manifests so that your source matches the stored object.

versionHistoryLimit in global, global.moduleConfig, and global.providerConfig now has minimum: 0. The API server rejects a negative value. Use 0 or remove the field to keep all versions.

Provider entries now inherit spec.global.githubClientConfig. Before this change, they did not. When the top-level block sets useAuthenticatedClient: true, source scans for provider Versions use the GitHub App token by default. This can read go.mod data from private repositories, and the Trivy findings are stored in Version status. This is intentional. To keep a provider unauthenticated, set githubClientConfig.useAuthenticatedClient: false on that provider entry. See Options for the precedence order.

Helm does not upgrade CRDs in the crds/ directory. If you use global defaults, apply the updated Depot CRD before you upgrade to 0.12.0. Run this from the root of the OpenDepot repository:

kubectl apply -f chart/opendepot/crds/opendepot.defdev.io_depots.yaml

Without the updated CRD, the API server keeps the old schema. The restrictions and minimum: 0 are not enforced until you apply it.

docs.title: Dex and OIDC client secret
docs.text:
When Dex and OIDC are enabled, the chart fails to render unless server.oidc.clientSecretName is set and matches a secretRef name in dex.envFrom. Before this release, a mismatch rendered successfully, and Dex started without the client secret.

Use any Secret name, but set the same name in both server.oidc.clientSecretName and dex.envFrom. The Secret must contain the OPENDEPOT_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET key.

docs.title: v0.11.0
docs.text: v0.11.0 updates the chart and application version to 0.11.0. Download statistics now use Prometheus instead of Valkey, and the Stats page queries Prometheus over a 90-day lookback by default.

docs.title: Vulnerability Blocking Thresholds
docs.text: scanning.blockOnHigh now blocks HIGH and CRITICAL findings. In 0.10.x, it blocked only HIGH, so CRITICAL findings did not block reconciliation. Before upgrading, review any Version that has CRITICAL findings. This release may block reconciliation for those versions. Add a ScanPolicy exemptions entry to allow a specific finding.

docs.title: Prometheus Statistics
docs.text:
Prometheus replaces Valkey as the statistics backend. The chart can optionally install a minimal kube-prometheus-stack. It is disabled by default. Enable it explicitly:

monitoring:
   bundled:
      enabled: true

The server exposes download counters and registry state gauges at /metrics on the metrics port of the server Service. The chart creates a ServiceMonitor for Prometheus Operator discovery. Existing Prometheus users should leave the bundled stack disabled, set server.stats.prometheusURL to the existing Prometheus HTTP API base URL, and ensure that Prometheus scrapes the OpenDepot Service. Set server.metrics.serviceMonitor.additionalLabels if the existing operator requires matching labels, or disable the ServiceMonitor when another scrape configuration is already in place. The URL must be absolute.

When server.stats.prometheusURL is empty and monitoring.enabled is true, the server uses the bundled Prometheus service address. That service exists only when monitoring.bundled.enabled is true. To keep time series beyond the local 90-day window, configure monitoring.prometheus.prometheusSpec.remoteWrite for Mimir or another Prometheus-compatible system.

docs.title: Security and Configuration Changes
docs.text:
• Assembly Line validation runs OpenTofu init only. Retained and streamed OpenTofu output is bounded by assembly.maxOutputBytes.
  • Provider schema extraction validates provider source, version, and path inputs, bounds subprocess output, and applies the configured extraction timeout.
  • The Version controller no longer exposes a directly mounted ServiceAccount token. It stages credentials in the pod through an init container and uses a token-refresh-helper sidecar to refresh the projected token. The chart grants only namespace-scoped Pod-delete and Secret-read permissions for this flow.
  • Init containers use bounded CPU and memory resources.
  • UI dependencies include security patches. No application configuration change is required for this update.
  • Production UI OIDC base URLs and discovered endpoints require HTTPS. HTTP is available only with global.developmentMode: true; UI state and session cookies use secure cookie settings in normal deployments.
  • The -assembly Server and Version controller images source-build pinned OpenTofu; the default images do not include it. The Trivy-enabled Version controller image source-builds pinned Trivy.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Remove Valkey values, ACL Secrets, and server.stats.valkeyPasswordSecretName overrides from custom values files. Choose one Prometheus setup. For the bundled stack, enable it: 
    monitoring:
   bundled:
      enabled: true
    For an existing Prometheus deployment, keep the bundled stack disabled and set its HTTP API URL instead: 
    server:
   stats:
      prometheusURL: https://prometheus.example.com
  3. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot \
   -n opendepot-system \
   -f my-values.yaml

Keep production UI OIDC URLs on HTTPS. Do not enable global.developmentMode to bypass that requirement outside local development.

docs.title: v0.10.0
docs.text: v0.10.0 enables Valkey ACL authentication and the bundled Dex reverse proxy by default. All existing installations must create a Valkey password Secret. Existing OIDC installations must also review their Dex configuration.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Valkey authentication is required outside development mode. The chart rejects valkey.auth.enabled: false unless global.developmentMode: true.
  • A pre-existing Secret is required. The default configuration expects an opendepot-valkey-auth Secret with a default key in the OpenDepot namespace. The chart does not create this Secret.
  • The Valkey and server Secret names must match. If you use a custom Secret name, set both valkey.auth.usersExistingSecret and server.stats.valkeyPasswordSecretName to that name.

docs.title: OIDC Default Change
docs.text:
server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled now defaults to true. This hardens bundled Dex deployments by proxying /dex/* through the existing server or UI ingress, so Dex no longer requires a separate public ingress or hostname.

This change does not affect installations with OIDC disabled. Existing OIDC installations require action in either of these cases:

  • Bundled Dex with an internal or auto-derived issuer: Set server.oidc.issuerUrl and dex.config.issuer to the same external, path-based URL served by the existing ingress, such as https://opendepot.example.com/dex.
  • External or separately exposed Dex: Set server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: false. The bundled proxy cannot target an externally managed issuer.

docs.title: Provider Upstream Registry Selection
docs.text:
v0.10.0 adds spec.providerConfig.upstreamRegistry to Provider resources and spec.providerConfigs[].upstreamRegistry to Depot resources. The field selects the canonical registry used for provider discovery, downloads, Network Mirror identity, and OpenDepot Workshop snippets.

Supported values are:

  • registry.opentofu.org (default)
  • registry.terraform.io

Existing resources require no changes. When the field is omitted, OpenDepot continues to use registry.opentofu.org, matching the behavior of earlier releases.

Set the field explicitly to mirror a provider from the Terraform Registry:

ProviderDepot 
apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: Provider
metadata:
   name: aws
   namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
   providerConfig:
      name: aws
      namespace: hashicorp
      upstreamRegistry: registry.terraform.io

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: Depot
metadata:
   name: upstream-providers
   namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
   providerConfigs:
      - name: aws
         namespace: hashicorp
         upstreamRegistry: registry.terraform.io

The provider retains its canonical source address, such as registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws. Configure the same hostname in the network_mirror.include and direct.exclude patterns in .tofurc or .terraformrc. See Consuming Providers for complete examples.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Create the Valkey ACL Secret before running helm upgrade: 
    kubectl create secret generic opendepot-valkey-auth \
  --namespace opendepot-system \
  --from-literal=default='<strong-random-password>'
  3. If you use a custom Secret name, add matching references to your values file: 
    valkey:
  auth:
    usersExistingSecret: my-valkey-auth

server:
  stats:
    valkeyPasswordSecretName: my-valkey-auth
  4. If OIDC is enabled, choose the appropriate Dex configuration:
Bundled DexExternal or separately exposed Dex

Set the same external, path-based issuer URL for the server and Dex:

dex:
  enabled: true
  config:
    issuer: https://opendepot.example.com/dex

server:
  oidc:
    enabled: true
    issuerUrl: https://opendepot.example.com/dex

Expose /dex through the existing server or UI ingress. A separate Dex ingress is no longer required.

Disable the bundled proxy explicitly:

server:
oidc:
   dexProxy:
      enabled: false
  1. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot -n opendepot-system -f my-values.yaml
  2. Confirm that Valkey and the server are ready: 
    kubectl rollout status deployment/valkey -n opendepot-system
kubectl rollout status deployment/server -n opendepot-system

Warning

Do not disable Valkey authentication in production. global.developmentMode: true permits unauthenticated Valkey only for local development environments.

docs.title: v0.9.0
docs.text:
v0.9.0 adds an opt-in reverse proxy so Dex never needs its own public ingress or hostname. See Proxying Dex Through the Server.

Set server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true to have the server reverse-proxy /dex/* requests to the bundled Dex service. This is fully backward compatible — the flag defaults to false, and existing dex.enabled: true deployments with a separately exposed Dex continue to work unchanged.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot -n opendepot-system -f my-values.yaml
  3. (Optional) To adopt the recommended proxy mode, set dex.config.issuer and server.oidc.issuerUrl to the same external, path-based URL and enable server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true. See Proxying Dex Through the Server for the full walkthrough.

No action is required to keep existing behavior — dexProxy.enabled defaults to false.

docs.title: v0.8.0
docs.text: v0.8.0 adds automatic README resolution for modules. See Module READMEs and the OpenDepot Workshop README rendering.

docs.title: New RBAC Permissions
docs.text: The version-controller ServiceAccount now requires configmaps (create, get, list, patch, update, watch) to store resolved READMEs, and the server ServiceAccount now requires configmaps (get, list, watch) to serve them through the browse API. Both rules are added automatically by the Helm chart — no values changes are required. See Controller Permissions.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot -n opendepot-system -f my-values.yaml

No manual action is required for existing Module and Version resources — the version controller resolves and stores READMEs automatically on each Version's next reconcile, or immediately when forceSync: true is set.

docs.title: v0.6.0
docs.text: v0.6.0 replaces the SQLite download-stats backend with a bundled Valkey instance.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• --stats-db-path is removed. The server flag no longer exists.
  • server.stats values block is removed. Remove server.stats.emptyDir, server.stats.persistence.*, or any other old server.stats key from your values.yaml. The chart does not validate values against a schema, so these keys are ignored rather than rejected.
  • Stats history is not migrated. Valkey starts with a clean slate — download counts accumulated in the previous SQLite database are not carried over. Historic data can be discarded or archived manually before upgrading.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Remove any server.stats keys from your values.yaml.
  3. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot -n opendepot-system -f my-values.yaml

Valkey is deployed automatically as part of the chart. Download tracking resumes immediately after the server pod becomes ready. For production clusters, valkey.dataStorage.enabled: true (the default) ensures stats survive pod restarts — no additional configuration is required.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: Change Affected field Action required Provider.status.sourceScans removed; per-version provider source scans moved to Version.status.sourceScan ProviderStatus, VersionStatus Update any automation or scripts that read .status.sourceScans on a Provider resource. Provider source scan results are now stored on each Version resource in status.sourceScan, alongside module IaC scan results. Provider.status.resolvedSourceRepository added (read-only, string) ProviderStatus No action required. The field is populated automatically by the Version controller after the first scan.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Apply the updated CRDs: 
    helm show crds opendepot/opendepot | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
  2. Update any scripts or automation reading Provider.status.sourceScans to read Version.status.sourceScan instead.
  3. Upgrade the chart: 
    helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot -n opendepot-system -f my-values.yaml

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OpenDepot supports several authentication paths for registry clients and the OpenDepot Workshop. Choose the workflow that matches the credentials your users or pipelines already have.

  • OIDC via Dex

    Recommended for production users and SSO. Authenticate with tofu login, federate an existing identity provider, and apply GroupBinding access rules.

  • Managed Cluster Tokens

    Use short-lived EKS, AKS, or GKE tokens when a pipeline already authenticates to the Kubernetes cluster.

  • Base64-Encoded Kubeconfig

    Use a kubeconfig credential for local development or environments where an environment token is not practical.

  • OpenDepot Workshop

    Configure browser sessions, UI OIDC, public visibility, and developer token input for OpenDepot Workshop.

docs.title: Choosing a Method
docs.text:
Feature Managed Cluster Token Kubeconfig File OIDC (Dex) OIDC + ServiceAccount Fallback Token lifetime Short-lived, auto-rotating Long-lived, manual rotation Short-lived, set by Dex Mixed: ServiceAccount token and JWT Security High Good Highest High Setup complexity Low Low Medium Medium Credential distribution Environment variable or shell Credentials file No distribution through SSO No distribution for human users tofu login support No No Yes Yes for human users Best for Production CI/CD Development Enterprise production OIDC deployments that require direct cluster API access

Warning

Enabling OIDC does not disable bearer-token authentication. The flag only applies to requests that OIDC does not authenticate. For CI/CD alternatives, see Managed Cluster Tokens and OIDC ServiceAccount fallback.

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
OIDC-authenticated requests can be restricted with GroupBinding resources. ServiceAccount tokens use Kubernetes RBAC instead; when ServiceAccount fallback is enabled, those tokens bypass GroupBinding entirely.

The Server supports anonymous access for public registries. When OIDC is enabled and server.anonymousAuth: false, browse API requests require a valid bearer token. See OIDC for the exact enforcement behavior.

docs.title: Base64-Encoded Kubeconfig
docs.text:
Use a base64-encoded kubeconfig for local development or environments where an environment variable is not practical. This method is not recommended for production because the credential is long-lived and manually rotated.

Note

This method requires server.useBearerToken: false in your Helm values.

docs.title: Encode Your Kubeconfig
docs.text: kubectl config view --raw | base64 | tr -d '\n' > /tmp/kubeconfig.b64

docs.title: Create the Credentials File
docs.text:
Create ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json and replace the placeholder with the contents of /tmp/kubeconfig.b64:

{
  "credentials": {
    "opendepot.defdev.io": {
      "token": "<contents-of-kubeconfig.b64>"
    }
  }
}

Restrict the file permissions:

chmod 600 ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json

OpenTofu and Terraform read this file automatically when they contact the registry.

docs.title: Managed Cluster Tokens
docs.text: Use a token issued by the managed Kubernetes provider when a CI job already has access to the cluster API. OpenDepot forwards the token to Kubernetes; if the API server accepts it, registry reads and module downloads work without Dex credentials.

docs.title: Required Server Configuration
docs.text:
Use one of these modes:

  • server.useBearerToken: true for pure bearer-token authentication.
  • server.oidc.allowServiceAccountFallback: true when OIDC is primary but non-OIDC tokens should be forwarded to Kubernetes.

If OIDC is enabled without ServiceAccount fallback, managed-cluster tokens are rejected because they are not Dex-issued JWTs.

docs.title: Registry Token Variable
docs.text:
OpenTofu and Terraform derive the environment variable name from the registry hostname. Replace dots with underscores and convert the result to uppercase.

opendepot.defdev.io becomes TF_TOKEN_OPENDEPOT_DEFDEV_IO.

Amazon EKSAzure AKSGoogle GKE 
export TF_TOKEN_OPENDEPOT_DEFDEV_IO=$(aws eks get-token \
  --cluster-name my-cluster \
  --region us-west-2 \
  --output json | jq -r '.status.token')

tofu init
tofu plan

export TF_TOKEN_OPENDEPOT_DEFDEV_IO=$(az account get-access-token \
  --resource 6dae42f8-4368-4678-94ff-3960e28e3630 \
  --query accessToken -o tsv)

tofu init
tofu plan

export TF_TOKEN_OPENDEPOT_DEFDEV_IO=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

tofu init
tofu plan

Provider-issued tokens are short-lived. This is the preferred option for CI/CD jobs when the cluster accepts the provider-issued token.

docs.title: CI/CD Example
docs.text:
name: Apply Infrastructure

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  apply:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/github-actions-role
          aws-region: us-west-2

      - name: Setup OpenTofu
        uses: opentofu/setup-opentofu@v1

      - name: Set registry token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(aws eks get-token --cluster-name my-cluster --region us-west-2 \
            --output json | jq -r '.status.token')
          echo "TF_TOKEN_OPENDEPOT_DEFDEV_IO=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - run: tofu init
      - run: tofu plan

For a pipeline-specific comparison with Dex Client Credentials and ServiceAccount tokens, see CI/CD Pipelines.

docs.title: OIDC via Dex
docs.text:
OIDC authentication enables single sign-on through an existing identity provider without distributing credentials or kubeconfigs. Dex is bundled as a Helm subchart and federates upstream providers such as Entra ID, Okta, GitHub, and LDAP.

For Helm values, Dex connectors, static clients, and the tofu login flow, see OIDC Helm Configuration.

docs.title: Browse Endpoint Authentication Enforcement
docs.text:
When server.oidc.enabled: true and server.anonymousAuth: false, browse API endpoints under /opendepot/ui/v1/* require a valid Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Requests without a valid token return 401 Unauthorized, including requests with an invalid or expired JWT.

A valid token with no matching GroupBinding is accepted and receives public-only visibility. The gate blocks callers with no token or a token that fails all verification paths. When server.anonymousAuth: true, or OIDC is not configured, browse endpoints remain accessible without authentication.

Warning

Set server.anonymousAuth: false together with server.oidc.enabled: true in production to prevent unauthenticated access to the browse API.

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop OIDC
docs.text:
When ui.oidc.enabled: true, the UI uses a dedicated Dex client, normally opendepot-ui, separate from the tofu login client opendepot. Set the UI client ID so the Server accepts UI-issued tokens:

ui:
  oidc:
    enabled: true
    clientId: opendepot-ui
    clientSecretName: opendepot-ui-oidc-secret

The Dex opendepot-ui client must include trustedPeers: [opendepot] so Dex includes the Server audience in UI-issued tokens:

dex:
  config:
    staticClients:
      - id: opendepot-ui
        name: OpenDepot UI
        secret: <ui-client-secret>
        trustedPeers:
          - opendepot
        redirectURIs:
          - https://<ui-host>/auth/callback

The UI requires an HTTPS issuer and an HTTPS ui.baseUrl when ui.oidc.enabled: true. The chart fails to render otherwise. Discovered authorization, token, and JWKS endpoints must share the issuer origin unless an explicit ui.oidc.authzUrl browser override is set. Insecure HTTP is allowed only when global.developmentMode: true. OIDC state and nonce cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Session cookies are Secure when the base URL uses HTTPS.

Note

Without the Server's UI client ID configured, the Stats page and browse endpoints may return empty results for users authenticated through the UI's OIDC client.

docs.title: GroupBinding Access Control
docs.text:
After OIDC authentication, the Server extracts the JWT groups claim and matches it against GroupBinding expressions. The groups claim is required. Requests with no claim receive 403 Forbidden. For the module and provider APIs, a claim that matches no GroupBinding also returns 403 Forbidden. Browse endpoints return public resources only instead.

Warning

With no GroupBinding resources in the Server namespace, module and provider API requests from OIDC users are denied. Deploy at least one GroupBinding before enabling OIDC in production.

See Fine-Grained Access Control with GroupBinding for expression syntax and setup instructions.

docs.title: CI/CD with ServiceAccount Fallback
docs.text:
GroupBinding is bypassed for ServiceAccount tokens

When ServiceAccount fallback is enabled, ServiceAccount tokens skip GroupBinding entirely. Kubernetes RBAC is the only access control applied to those tokens. This creates a separate access-control path alongside OIDC.

Before enabling fallback, consider the GitOps workflow for publishing modules or Dex Client Credentials for registry reads that continue to respect GroupBinding.

See CI/CD with ServiceAccount Fallback for setup details and required RBAC.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Cause Fix missing Authorization header .tofurc has no credentials block Add a credentials "host" { token = "..." } block unauthorized JWT expired or invalid Run tofu login again Browser redirects to localhost but fails Dex redirect URI is not registered Add the expected localhost ports to redirectURIs Stats shows zeroes for UI-authenticated users UI client ID was not propagated to the Server Enable ui.oidc and set a non-empty ui.oidc.clientId

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop Authentication
docs.text:
OpenDepot Workshop has a browser-based authentication flow separate from the tofu login CLI flow. The UI registers its own OIDC client and issues its own access tokens.

For UI deployment, routing, session secrets, and client registration, see the OpenDepot Workshop guide.

docs.title: Sign In and Sign Out
docs.text:
When ui.oidc.enabled: true, the Sidebar displays a Sign in button. It redirects the browser to /auth/login, which starts the OIDC authorization code flow. After the identity provider redirects back, the UI stores the access token in an encrypted server-side session cookie.

The Sidebar footer shows the authenticated user's display name from the name or preferred_username JWT claim and a Sign out button. Sign-out calls /auth/logout and clears the session cookie.

docs.title: Session Token Forwarding
docs.text:
The UI is a Next.js application with server components. On each page render, the server component reads the access token from the session cookie and forwards it as an Authorization: Bearer <token> header to browse API calls under /opendepot/ui/v1/*.

The Server evaluates the token against GroupBinding resources. Unauthenticated users receive only publicly labelled resources.

docs.title: Provider Unavailability
docs.text: If the OIDC provider is unreachable when a user attempts to sign in, /auth/login returns HTTP 503. Load balancers and health checks can tell provider outages apart from other failures.

docs.title: Developer Token Input
docs.text:
Local development only

Set ui.auth.devTokenInput.enabled: false in every production environment.

When enabled, the Sidebar shows a Dev Bearer Token input. A developer can paste a raw Kubernetes ServiceAccount token, such as the output of kubectl create token, into the field. The UI posts it to /auth/dev-token and stores it as devToken in the encrypted session. Subsequent server renders prefer it over the OIDC access token. Submit an empty value to clear it.

See Developer Token Input for Helm configuration details.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure OpenDepot for your environment. All configuration is done through Helm chart values — no config files to manage.

  • Authentication

    Choose OIDC, managed cluster tokens, kubeconfig credentials, or Registry Explorer UI authentication for your deployment.

  • Storage Backends

    Configure S3, Azure Blob, GCS, filesystem storage, and pre-signed provider downloads.

  • OIDC Helm Configuration

    Deploy Dex as a bundled OIDC identity provider to enable tofu login and single sign-on via Entra ID, Okta, GitHub, LDAP, and other upstream IdPs.

  • Vulnerability Scanning

    Enable Trivy-based vulnerability scanning for provider binaries and source dependencies, with optional policy enforcement to block critical or high findings.

  • GPG Signing

    Set up GPG signing for provider SHA256SUMS files so OpenTofu can cryptographically verify provider archives.

  • GitHub Authentication

    Configure a GitHub App to authenticate API requests and increase rate limits when using the Depot controller with private repositories.

  • Namespace-Scoped Mode

    Restrict OpenDepot to a single namespace using Role and RoleBinding instead of cluster-wide ClusterRole resources.

  • TLS

    Terminate TLS on the OpenDepot server using a Kubernetes Secret, or delegate to an Ingress controller or service mesh.

  • Assembly Line

    Enable and configure browser-based OpenTofu root-module composition and server-side validation.

docs.title: Assembly Line Configuration
docs.text: Assembly Line lets users compose onboarded modules and providers into a validated OpenTofu root module. It is disabled by default and requires the UI to be enabled.

docs.title: Enable Assembly Line
docs.text:
Set the following Helm values:

ui:
  enabled: true

assembly:
  enabled: true

Assembly Line requires OpenTofu, which is not bundled in the default server and version images. Point both images at the -assembly tag variant of your release, which includes the OpenTofu binary:

server:
  image:
    tag: "<release>-assembly"

version:
  image:
    tag: "<release>-assembly"

The server refuses to start with Assembly Line enabled if the OpenTofu binary is missing from its image.

See the Helm Chart Reference for the complete assembly.* value table, including request, node, timeout, output, and workspace limits.

ui.baseUrl must be a valid external HTTP(S) URL. OpenDepot uses its host for generated module source addresses and the Provider Network Mirror URL. The server must also be able to reach that origin during export, unless you set a separate assembly.validationRegistryUrl.

docs.title: Validation Connectivity
docs.text:
Assembly Line validates exports by running OpenTofu initialization in a temporary server-side workspace. If the public UI origin is not reachable from the server pod, configure an internal HTTPS origin and its CA bundle:

assembly:
  validationRegistryUrl: https://registry.internal.example.com
  validationCACertPath: /etc/opendepot/ca/registry.pem

These values affect only server-side initialization transport. They do not change generated module sources, provider identities, or the files returned to the user.

The validation workspace is isolated per export. OpenTofu runs with bounded output and a configured timeout. The workspace is removed after the request, including failed requests. The chart mounts only assembly.workDir as a writable, size-limited volume; consider setting ephemeral-storage requests and limits for production workloads.

docs.title: Provider and Module Requirements
docs.text:
Before a resource appears in the Assembly Line palette:

  • A module version must have a synced, derived contract.
  • A provider version must have a synced, extracted configuration schema.
  • The provider must use the registry.opentofu.org upstream registry.

Provider schema extraction runs OpenTofu in a temporary scrubbed workspace. The controller validates provider-controlled source, version, and workspace components before starting extraction.

Assembly Line does not support Terraform-origin providers, even though the general provider registry can mirror both OpenTofu and Terraform origins.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Anonymous export does not write credentials. Authenticated export forwards the caller’s bearer token through a temporary mode-0600 OpenTofu credentials file. The token is not included in command arguments, logs, generated HCL, diagnostics, or the ZIP archive.

Legacy kubeconfig authentication cannot be forwarded through the registry protocol. Authenticated exports therefore require a bearer token.

docs.title: Export Behavior
docs.text:
The server re-authorizes every resource and reloads the selected versions, module contracts, and provider schemas from Kubernetes. It does not trust metadata supplied by the browser. The server rejects stale, unavailable, unauthorized, or unsupported provider resources before returning a ZIP.

Successful exports contain only:

main.tf
variables.tf

The archive excludes .terraform, lock files, state, CLI configuration, temporary files, and command output.

For the browser workflow, see Using Assembly Line.

docs.title: GitHub Authentication
docs.text:
For private repositories and to avoid GitHub API rate limits, create a GitHub App and store its credentials as a Kubernetes Secret:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: opendepot-github-application-secret
  namespace: opendepot-system
type: Opaque
data:
  githubAppID: <base64-encoded-app-id>
  githubInstallID: <base64-encoded-install-id>
  githubPrivateKey: <base64-encoded-private-key>

Warning

githubPrivateKey is base64-encoded twice. First encode the PEM file, then place that value in data. Kubernetes decodes the data layer on read, and the controller decodes the remaining layer.

Then enable authenticated access in your module config:

githubClientConfig:
  useAuthenticatedClient: true

docs.title: Provider Source Scanning
docs.text:
