A skill or agent source can set ref to follow a Git branch instead of publishing from tags. Branch sourcing is enabled only when the chart is installed with branchSourcing.enabled: true.

  • Polling is opt-in. Set pollingIntervalMinutes to pick up new commits on a schedule. When it is unset, the Depot picks up new commits only when it reconciles for another reason, such as a spec change, an annotation change, or a resync.
  • One pending entry at a time. While the newest entry is pending, the Depot adds no new entry. Commits that arrive between polls collapse into one Version.
  • Tags are the stable choice. Tags are usually more immutable than branches. A branch head moves with every push, and each new commit becomes a new Version pinned to its sourceCommit.
  • Migration only. Branch sources are intended as a one-time migration. After that, manage the source definitions through GitOps.

See Branch sourcing for branchPolicy, the naming and status flow, and the Jev bump rules.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Polling interval: pollingIntervalMinutes sets how often the Depot re-queries GitHub and upstream registries. If omitted, the Depot reconciles once and does not poll.

For branch sources (ref), polling is what picks up new commits on a schedule. When pollingIntervalMinutes is unset, a branch source picks up new commits only when the Depot reconciles for another reason, such as a spec change, an annotation change, or a resync. Branch sources are intended as a one-time migration, managed through GitOps afterward. See Branch sourcing.

Per-module storage override: Any module can override the global storage config:

moduleConfigs:
  - name: terraform-aws-eks
    provider: aws
    repoOwner: terraform-aws-modules
    versionConstraints: ">= 21.10.1"
    storageConfig:
      azureStorage:
        accountName: opendepotmodules
        accountUrl: https://opendepotmodules.blob.core.windows.net
        subscriptionID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
        resourceGroup: opendepot-rg

Version history limit: the first value set wins, in this order:

  1. versionHistoryLimit on the moduleConfigs or providerConfigs entry.
  2. spec.global.moduleConfig.versionHistoryLimit for modules, or spec.global.providerConfig.versionHistoryLimit for providers.
  3. spec.global.versionHistoryLimit for both kinds.

The Depot keeps the newest N matching versions and writes only those to each generated resource's spec.versions. The Module and Provider controllers then delete the Version resources that were removed. Trimmed versions do not return on later polls.

GitHub client config: An entry inherits githubClientConfig in the same order as the version history limit: the entry, then spec.global.moduleConfig or spec.global.providerConfig, then spec.global. A provider inherits spec.global.githubClientConfig when neither the entry nor spec.global.providerConfig sets githubClientConfig. An entry that sets githubClientConfig keeps its own value.

Provider source scans use the GitHub App token by default

When a provider inherits useAuthenticatedClient: true from spec.global.githubClientConfig, the Version controller uses the GitHub App token for source scans of that provider's Versions. This can read go.mod data from private repositories, and the Trivy findings are stored in each Version's status. This is intentional. The combined example above sets this flag, so its aws provider uses the App token. To keep a provider unauthenticated, set githubClientConfig.useAuthenticatedClient: false on that entry. If the opendepot-github-application-secret Secret is missing, the scan falls back to an unauthenticated client.

docs.title: GitOps with Argo CD
docs.text:
Recommended for OIDC organizations

With OIDC enabled, GitOps is the recommended way to publish modules. Developers push to Git, pipelines hold no cluster credentials, and no ServiceAccount token bypasses GroupBinding.

For teams that manage infrastructure declaratively through Git, OpenDepot fits naturally into a GitOps workflow with Argo CD. Instead of running kubectl apply from a CI pipeline, you check your Module manifests into a Git repository and let Argo CD sync them to the cluster.

How it works:

  1. A developer opens a PR against their OpenTofu module repository with the code changes
  2. The same PR includes an update to the OpenDepot Module manifest, adding the new version to spec.versions
  3. The team reviews both the module code and the registry manifest in a single PR
  4. On approval and merge, Argo CD detects the change and syncs the Module resource to the cluster
  5. OpenDepot takes over — the Module controller creates a Version resource, and the Version controller fetches the archive from GitHub and uploads it to storage

This gives you a complete audit trail: every module version published to your registry maps to an approved, merged pull request.

Example repository structure:

opendepot-manifests/
├── modules/
│   └── terraform-aws-eks.yaml
└── kustomization.yaml

Module manifest (modules/terraform-aws-eks.yaml):

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: Module
metadata:
  name: terraform-aws-eks
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  moduleConfig:
    name: terraform-aws-eks
    provider: aws
    repoOwner: my-org
    repoUrl: https://github.com/my-org/terraform-aws-eks
    fileFormat: zip
    immutable: true
    storageConfig:
      s3:
        bucket: my-org-opendepot-modules
        region: us-west-2
    githubClientConfig:
      useAuthenticatedClient: true
  versions:
    - version: "21.10.1"
    - version: "21.11.0"
    - version: "21.12.0"
    - version: "21.13.0"   # added in PR #42

Argo CD Application:

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: my-org-opendepot-modules
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/my-org/opendepot-manifests
    targetRevision: main
    path: modules
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: opendepot-system
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: false
      selfHeal: true

Tip

Set prune: false so that Argo CD does not delete Module resources removed from Git — this prevents accidental module deletion. Use selfHeal: true so that any manual drift on the cluster is corrected back to the Git-declared state.

Why this works well with OpenDepot:

  • Single PR, full visibility — module code and registry manifest are reviewed together
  • No cluster credentials in CI — Argo CD handles authentication to the cluster; developers only push to Git
  • Immutable audit trail — Git history records exactly who added each version and when
  • Declarative all the way down — Git declares the desired state, Argo CD syncs it, and OpenDepot reconciles it to storage
  • GroupBinding fully enforced — all human access still flows through OIDC and GroupBinding; no bypass path is introduced
  • Blast radius is Git, not the cluster — a compromised pipeline runner can push a PR at worst; it cannot directly modify Kubernetes resources or reach the cluster API

docs.title: Least Privilege in Regulated Environments
docs.text:
When OIDC is enabled, the alternative to GitOps is enabling ServiceAccount fallback so pipelines can authenticate alongside human users. That approach has a material trade-off: SA tokens bypass GroupBinding entirely. The SA's Kubernetes RBAC governs its access instead of the centralized, identity-aware GroupBinding model. In practice this means:

  • You operate two separate access control systems — OIDC + GroupBinding for humans, RBAC for pipelines — which increases audit surface and operational overhead.
  • A compromised pipeline token grants direct cluster API access, not just registry access.
  • Access granted to an SA does not appear in GroupBinding audit logs.

For organizations that must enforce least privilege and separation of duties, GitOps keeps cluster credentials out of pipelines entirely.

docs.title: Fine-Grained Access Control with GroupBinding
docs.text:
GroupBinding is a namespaced CRD that restricts which modules and providers an OIDC-authenticated user may access, based on the groups present in their JWT. It requires OIDC authentication to be enabled.

GroupBinding controls Registry and browse authorization only. ScanPolicy administration uses the separate SecurityGroupBinding resource; changing a GroupBinding does not grant policy access.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When a user authenticates via OIDC, the server extracts the configured groups claim from their JWT and evaluates all GroupBinding resources in the server namespace in alphabetical order by name. The first GroupBinding whose expression evaluates to true for the user's groups is applied. If an expression fails to compile or evaluate, the request is denied with 403 Forbidden rather than skipping to the next binding. The user may then access only the modules whose names match the moduleResources glob patterns and the providers whose type names are listed in providerResources on that GroupBinding.

flowchart TD
    A[OIDC JWT received] --> B{Groups claim present?}
    B -- No --> C[403 Forbidden]
    B -- Yes --> D[Evaluate GroupBindings in alphabetical order]
    D --> E{Expression matches?}
    E -- No more bindings --> F[403 Forbidden]
    E -- Yes --> G[Check resource name against allowed list]
    G --> H{Name matches?}
    H -- Yes --> I[200 OK]
    H -- No --> J[403 Forbidden]

docs.title: First-Match Semantics
docs.text: Only the first binding (alphabetically by name) whose expression is true is applied — later bindings are not evaluated. Use ordered name prefixes (e.g., 01-platform-team, 02-app-teams) when evaluation order matters.

docs.title: Required Groups Claim
docs.text:
The groups claim is required for interactive OIDC users. A valid JWT that does not carry the configured claim is denied with 403 Forbidden. Every OIDC user must have a groups claim in their JWT and match a GroupBinding to access any resource.

The one exception is client credentials tokens. When server.oidc.allowClientCredentials is enabled, the server synthesizes a virtual group from the token's sub claim ("client:<sub>"), so a groups claim is not required in the JWT itself.

Confirm that your Dex connector emits the groups claim. Connector configuration varies; see the Dex connector documentation for your IdP.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: GroupBinding
metadata:
  name: platform-team-binding
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"platform-team" in groups'
  moduleResources:
    - "aws-*"
    - "gcp-networking"
  providerResources:
    - "aws"
    - "google"

docs.title: Spec Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description expression string Yes An expr-lang boolean expression evaluated against the user's groups. Must return true or false. moduleResources []string No Glob patterns for module names the group may access. Empty list denies access to all modules. providerResources []string No Exact provider type names the group may access, or ["*"] to allow all providers. Empty list denies access to all providers.

docs.title: Expression Syntax
docs.text:
The expression field uses expr-lang syntax. The evaluation environment exposes one variable:

Variable Type Description groups []string Groups extracted from the user's JWT groups claim.

Examples:

"platform-team" in groups
"platform-team" in groups || "platform-readonly" in groups
len(groups) > 0

Client credentials identities

When server.oidc.allowClientCredentials is enabled, the token's sub claim is mapped to the virtual group "client:<sub>". For Dex client credentials tokens the sub equals the Dex client id (e.g. ci-pipeline → "client:ci-pipeline"). Use this in expressions to grant machine clients scoped access: 

"client:ci-pipeline" in groups
Inspect the JWT to confirm the sub value before writing the expression.

See Client Credentials (Machine-to-Machine) for full setup details.

Warning

A GroupBinding with an invalid or failing expression fails closed. The server logs an ERROR entry and denies the request with 403 Forbidden instead of skipping to the next binding. Check server logs to diagnose expression errors.

docs.title: Module Resource Glob Patterns
docs.text:
moduleResources uses path.Match semantics, supporting the * wildcard:

Pattern Matches Does not match aws-* aws-vpc, aws-eks, aws-s3-bucket gcp-gke terraform-aws-* terraform-aws-eks, terraform-aws-vpc terraform-google-gke * every module name — my-module exactly my-module my-module-v2

providerResources takes exact provider type names (e.g., aws, google, azurerm) or the literal "*" to allow all providers. No partial wildcard matching is applied to provider names.

An empty moduleResources or providerResources list denies access to all resources of that type. To allow access to all modules, use ["*"]; to allow access to all providers, use ["*"].

docs.title: Configuring the Groups Claim Name
docs.text:
The server reads the groups JWT claim by default. If your IdP uses a different claim name, set server.oidc.groupsClaim in your Helm values:

server:
  oidc:
    groupsClaim: "cognito:groups"

This sets the --oidc-groups-claim server flag.

docs.title: Example: Team-Based Access
docs.text:
Two GroupBindings restricting access by team:

Platform team — full access to AWS and Google resources:

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: GroupBinding
metadata:
  name: 01-platform-team
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"platform" in groups || "platform-readonly" in groups'
  moduleResources:
    - "terraform-aws-*"
    - "terraform-google-gke"
  providerResources:
    - "aws"
    - "google"

App teams — access to shared modules only:

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: GroupBinding
metadata:
  name: 02-app-teams
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"developers" in groups'
  moduleResources:
    - "shared-*"
  providerResources:
    - "aws"

Apply both:

kubectl apply -f groupbindings.yaml

Note

GroupBindings must be created in the same namespace as the OpenDepot server (default: opendepot-system). The server ServiceAccount is granted get, list, and watch on groupbindings in that namespace by the Helm chart.

docs.title: Access Logging
docs.text:
The server emits structured JSON log entries for every authorization decision. These provide a full audit trail for OIDC access:

Event Level Key Fields JWT verified DEBUG subject, groups_claim, groups Missing groups claim WARN subject, groups_claim GroupBinding matched INFO subject, groups, binding_name, expression Expression invalid or failed ERROR binding_name, expression, error Resource access allowed INFO subject, binding_name, resource_type, resource_name, namespace Resource access denied WARN subject, binding_name, resource_type, resource_name, namespace

View server logs:

kubectl logs -n opendepot-system -l app=server --follow

ScanPolicy writes add structured ScanPolicy created, ScanPolicy updated, and ScanPolicy deleted events with the subject, namespace, and policy name. These events complement Kubernetes API-server audit records; they do not replace them. Use SecurityGroupBinding to grant policy administration without changing Registry access.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• OIDC Helm Configuration — enable OIDC before deploying GroupBindings
  • API Reference — GroupBinding — full field reference
  • Kubernetes RBAC — cluster-level access control

docs.title: Migrating to OpenDepot
docs.text:
Tip

Migration is one of several Depot use cases. For ongoing mirroring and tracking, see Pull-Based Workflow: Using the Depot. Deleting a Depot does not delete the Modules or Providers it created.

Migrating modules — Use the Depot to bulk-import existing modules into OpenDepot:

  1. Create a Depot with broad version constraints (e.g., ">= 0.0.0") to pull in the full release history
  2. Wait for all versions to sync (check Module and Version status resources)
  3. Update your OpenTofu/Terraform configurations to source modules from OpenDepot
  4. Delete the Depot — all Module and Version resources remain untouched
  5. Going forward, publish new versions via the GitOps workflow

Migrating providers — Use spec.providerConfigs in your Depot to mirror providers from upstream registries into your own storage backend:

  1. Create a Depot with providerConfigs listing each provider, your target OS/architecture matrix, and a version constraint (the upstream registry defaults to registry.opentofu.org; set upstreamRegistry: registry.terraform.io explicitly if needed)
  2. Wait for all Provider and Version resources to sync
  3. Update your configurations to reference providers by their canonical identity (e.g., hashicorp/aws) and configure OpenDepot as the installation source via provider_installation.network_mirror in your .tofurc or .terraformrc (see Consuming Providers for full CLI configuration examples)
  4. Delete the Depot — all Provider and Version resources remain untouched

This pattern lets you adopt OpenDepot incrementally. For version-specific steps, see Upgrading.

docs.title: Consuming Modules
docs.text:
Once modules are synced, reference them in your OpenTofu configuration:

module "eks" {
  source  = "opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot-system/terraform-aws-eks/aws"
  version = "~> 21.0"
}

module "aks" {
  source  = "opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot-system/terraform-azurerm-aks/azurerm"
  version = ">= 10.0.0"
}

The source format is <registry-host>/<namespace>/<name>/<provider>:

  • <namespace> is the Kubernetes namespace of the Module resource.
  • <name> is the name of the Module resource.
  • <provider> is the provider name, such as aws.

docs.title: Authenticate
docs.text:
tofu login requires OIDC enabled on the server (server.oidc.enabled: true). See OIDC via Dex.

tofu login opendepot.defdev.io
tofu init

If OIDC is not enabled, see Authentication.

Host mapping fallback

OpenTofu discovers the module API from /.well-known/terraform.json. Only add this host block to your .tofurc if discovery does not resolve for your host.

host "opendepot.defdev.io" {
  services = {
    "modules.v1" = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/modules/v1/"
  }
}

docs.title: Module Fields
docs.text: For Module spec fields such as moduleConfig, versions, and forceSync, see the API Reference.

docs.title: Next Steps for Admins
docs.text:
• Registry Operations: create Module resources, add inline Version config, and force re-sync.
  • Vulnerability Scanning: scan configuration and policy controls.

docs.title: Registry Operations
docs.text: Operational runbooks for managing module and provider lifecycles after initial setup.

docs.title: Adding versions to an existing module
docs.text:
To publish a new version of a module that already exists in OpenDepot, append the version to the spec.versions list. Existing versions are preserved - the Module controller only creates Version resources for entries it has not seen before.

Using kubectl patch (quick):

kubectl patch module terraform-aws-eks -n opendepot-system \
  --type json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/versions/-","value":{"version":"21.13.0"}}]'

Using kubectl apply (declarative):

Include all existing versions alongside the new one. The Module controller is idempotent and does not re-create versions that already exist.

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: Module
metadata:
  name: terraform-aws-eks
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  moduleConfig:
    name: terraform-aws-eks
    provider: aws
    repoOwner: terraform-aws-modules
    repoUrl: https://github.com/terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-eks
    fileFormat: zip
    storageConfig:
      s3:
        bucket: opendepot-modules
        region: us-west-2
  versions:
    - version: "21.10.1"
    - version: "21.11.0"
    - version: "21.12.0"
    - version: "21.13.0"

GitHub Actions Example (Append on Release):

- name: Add version to existing module
  run: |
    VERSION=${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
    kubectl patch module my-module -n opendepot-system \
      --type json \
      -p "[{\"op\":\"add\",\"path\":\"/spec/versions/-\",\"value\":{\"version\":\"${VERSION}\"}}]"

Removing a version: remove the entry from spec.versions and re-apply. The controller garbage-collects the removed Version resources. With versionHistoryLimit set, the controller also trims spec.versions to the newest N entries and garbage-collects the rest.

docs.title: Force re-sync
docs.text:
If a Module or Version fails to sync (for example, due to a transient network error), you can force a re-sync by setting forceSync: true on the resource.

# Force a Module to re-sync all its versions
kubectl patch module terraform-aws-eks -n opendepot-system \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceSync":true}}'

# Force a single Version to re-sync
kubectl patch version.opendepot.defdev.io terraform-aws-eks-21.18.0 -n opendepot-system \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceSync":true}}'

The controller resets forceSync to false after reconciliation completes.

docs.title: Module READMEs
docs.text:
For module Version resources, the Version controller resolves the README on a best-effort basis. It tries the GitHub API first, then falls back to a README.md extracted from the downloaded archive. An unresolved README does not fail the sync, and OpenDepot Workshop omits the README card.

The README is stored base64-encoded in a ConfigMap named <version-name>-readme. The Version owns the ConfigMap, so deleting the Version removes it. The reference is recorded in status.readmeConfigMapRef. The README is fetched on the first sync, when status.readmeConfigMapRef is unset, and again when forceSync: true is set. Provider Version resources do not get a README.

docs.title: Inline module configuration (Version CR)
docs.text:
moduleConfigRef.name is optional. When it is omitted, or when no Module with that name exists in the namespace, the Version controller uses the fields on moduleConfigRef directly and generates a UUID filename as the storage key. Use this to run the Version controller without the Module controller, or for one-off testing.

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: Version
metadata:
  name: terraform-aws-s3-bucket-4-3-0
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  type: Module
  version: "4.3.0"
  moduleConfigRef:
    repoOwner: terraform-aws-modules
    repoUrl: "https://github.com/terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-s3-bucket"
    githubClientConfig:
      useAuthenticatedClient: false
    storageConfig:
      fileSystem:
        directoryPath: /data/modules

Note

When name is omitted the Version CR is completely self-contained. No Module CR needs to exist in the namespace.

docs.title: Adding a new provider version
docs.text:
To publish a new version, append it to spec.versions:

kubectl patch provider aws -n opendepot-system \
  --type json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/versions/-","value":{"version":"5.81.0"}}]'

The Provider controller creates new Version resources for every OS/architecture combination, and the Version controller fetches and stores the binaries automatically.

docs.title: Force re-sync
docs.text:
kubectl patch provider aws -n opendepot-system \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceSync":true}}'

docs.title: Force re-sync a specific provider version
docs.text:
Version resources also support forceSync. Use it to force a re-download and re-scan of a specific OS/architecture binary - for example, when status.binaryScan is empty because scanning was enabled after the version was first synced.

kubectl patch version <version-name> -n <namespace> \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceSync":true}}'

The <version-name> follows the pattern <provider>-<version-dashes>-<os>-<arch> - for example, aws-5-80-0-linux-amd64.

The controller bypasses the provider fast-path, re-downloads the artifact, runs the binary scan, and resets forceSync to false once reconciliation completes.

Note

On restart, a provider Version with a stored checksum that still matches storage skips the download. Stored scan findings are re-evaluated against the current ScanPolicy, but Trivy does not run again. Use forceSync: true on that Version for a one-time re-download and re-scan.

docs.title: Provider source repository
docs.text: For registry.opentofu.org providers, OpenDepot looks up the source repository through api.opentofu.org. For registry.terraform.io providers, it builds https://github.com/{namespace}/terraform-provider-{name}. Set spec.providerConfig.namespace when the provider is not published under hashicorp, or set sourceRepository to pin the URL. The resolution order and examples are in Provider Source Repository Resolution.

docs.title: Authenticated source scanning
docs.text: For private source repositories, or to avoid GitHub API rate limits, set githubClientConfig.useAuthenticatedClient: true on the ProviderConfig. The Version controller uses the opendepot-github-application-secret that modules use. See Authenticated Source Scanning and GitHub Authentication.

docs.title: Vulnerability Scanning Runbooks
docs.text:
When scanning is enabled, the Version controller runs Trivy and stores findings on Kubernetes resources.

Module IaC scan results (Version.status.sourceScan):

kubectl get version terraform-aws-key-pair-2-0-0 -n opendepot-system \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.sourceScan}' | jq .

Provider binary scan results (Version.status.binaryScan):

kubectl get version aws-5-81-0-linux-amd64 -n opendepot-system -o jsonpath='{.status.binaryScan}' | jq .

Provider source scan results (Version.status.sourceScan):

kubectl get version aws-5-81-0-linux-amd64 -n opendepot-system -o jsonpath='{.status.sourceScan}' | jq .

For complete scanning configuration, thresholds, and policy behavior, see Vulnerability Scanning.

docs.title: Pre-signed URL Redirect Operations
docs.text:
By default, provider binary downloads are proxied through the OpenDepot server. Enabling pre-signed URLs causes the server to redirect OpenTofu directly to the storage backend with a time-limited signed URL, reducing server-side bandwidth costs for large provider binaries.

Add a presign block to the storageConfig on provider Version resources (or on Depot.spec.global.storageConfig to apply globally):

spec:
  providerConfig:
    name: aws
  storageConfig:
    s3:
      bucket: opendepot-providers
      region: us-east-1
    presign:
      enabled: true
      ttl: "15m"
      fallbackToProxy: true

When presign.enabled is true, the /opendepot/providers/v1/download/{namespace}/{type}/{version}/{os}/{arch} endpoint responds with 307 Temporary Redirect to the signed URL. If pre-signing fails and fallbackToProxy is true (the default), the server automatically falls back to streaming the binary itself. Set fallbackToProxy: false to make pre-signing strictly required. Storage initialization, checksum lookup, and presign failures then return 502 Bad Gateway. A checksum mismatch returns 500 Internal Server Error.

Pre-signed URLs are supported on S3, GCS, and Azure Blob Storage. Filesystem storage cannot pre-sign, so with fallbackToProxy: false its downloads fail with 502. See Pre-signed URL Redirects for IAM requirements and field reference.

docs.title: Consuming Providers
docs.text:
OpenDepot implements the Provider Network Mirror Protocol, which OpenTofu and Terraform share. Configurations reference providers by their canonical identity (for example, hashicorp/aws), and the CLI installs binaries from OpenDepot. The lockfile keeps the canonical identity, so configurations stay portable.

OpenDepot supports providers from registry.opentofu.org and registry.terraform.io. Set the origin per Provider with spec.providerConfig.upstreamRegistry. It defaults to registry.opentofu.org.

docs.title: Default workflow: Network Mirror
docs.text:
Once providers are synced, declare them in your configuration using their canonical source identity:

terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.80"
    }
    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = ">= 4.0.0"
    }
  }
}

The source field uses <provider-namespace>/<provider-type>, or the fully-qualified form <upstream-registry>/<provider-namespace>/<provider-type>. It names the upstream identity, not your OpenDepot hostname.

CLI configuration: namespace-scoped mirror URL

Configure OpenDepot as the installation source in .tofurc (OpenTofu) or .terraformrc (Terraform) with a provider_installation block.

The network_mirror.include and direct.exclude patterns must use the same hostname as the upstreamRegistry on your Provider resources. For example, upstreamRegistry: registry.terraform.io requires registry.terraform.io/*/* in both patterns.

OpenTofu (registry.opentofu.org)Terraform (registry.terraform.io)Non-default port

Anonymous access

provider_installation {
  network_mirror {
    url     = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/opendepot-system/"
    include = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }

  direct {
    exclude = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }
}

The direct.exclude entry prevents OpenTofu from falling back to registry.opentofu.org if a mirrored provider is missing a version, ensuring all installations come from OpenDepot.

Authenticated access (OIDC)

credentials "opendepot.defdev.io" {
  token = "<oidc-access-token>"
}

provider_installation {
  network_mirror {
    url     = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/opendepot-system/"
    include = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }

  direct {
    exclude = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }
}

Obtain a token: 

tofu login opendepot.defdev.io
Or retrieve it directly from your OIDC provider and place it in .tofurc.

Anonymous access

provider_installation {
  network_mirror {
    url     = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/opendepot-system/"
    include = ["registry.terraform.io/*/*"]
  }

  direct {
    exclude = ["registry.terraform.io/*/*"]
  }
}

The direct.exclude entry prevents Terraform from falling back to registry.terraform.io if a mirrored provider is missing a version, ensuring all installations come from OpenDepot.

Authenticated access (OIDC)

credentials "opendepot.defdev.io" {
  token = "<oidc-access-token>"
}

provider_installation {
  network_mirror {
    url     = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/opendepot-system/"
    include = ["registry.terraform.io/*/*"]
  }

  direct {
    exclude = ["registry.terraform.io/*/*"]
  }
}

Obtain a token: 

terraform login opendepot.defdev.io
Or retrieve it directly from your OIDC provider and place it in .terraformrc.

When your OpenDepot instance runs on a non-default port, include the port in both the credentials hostname and the network_mirror.url:

credentials "opendepot.localtest.me:8080" {
  token = "<oidc-access-token>"
}

provider_installation {
  network_mirror {
    url     = "https://opendepot.localtest.me:8080/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/opendepot-system/"
    include = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }

  direct {
    exclude = ["registry.opentofu.org/*/*"]
  }
}

Key details

  • Credentials and namespace: Credentials match the OpenDepot hostname, including the port if it is non-default. The mirror URL is scoped to a Kubernetes namespace (/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/<kubernetes-namespace>/).
  • Lockfile identity: .terraform.lock.hcl records the canonical upstream identity, not the OpenDepot hostname.
  • Mirror-only installs: direct.exclude is required. Without it, the CLI can fall back to the upstream registry for a version the mirror lacks, bypassing OpenDepot's scanning and access controls.
  • Both origins: Providers from registry.opentofu.org and registry.terraform.io can share one cluster-scoped installation. If the same provider namespace and type is mirrored from both registries, place them in separate Kubernetes namespaces. Otherwise their Version resource names collide. With rbac.scopeToNamespace: true, controllers only watch global.namespace, so multi-namespace serving needs broader cluster scope or separate namespace-scoped installations.

Note

The mirror metadata endpoints (index.json and the per-version files) check the caller's access. Archive downloads are served by OpenDepot or redirected to a presigned URL, depending on storage configuration. See Pre-signed URL Redirects.

docs.title: Advanced: Direct OpenDepot provider identity
docs.text:
For private or internal providers that are not mirrored from an upstream registry, use the Provider Registry Protocol with direct OpenDepot identity. The source names your OpenDepot hostname and Kubernetes namespace:

terraform {
  required_providers {
    customapi = {
      source  = "opendepot.defdev.io/my-team/customapi"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
  }
}

The source format is <registry-host>/<namespace>/<name>. <namespace> is the Kubernetes namespace of the Provider resource. <name> is spec.providerConfig.name, or the Provider resource name if name is omitted.

Discovery at /.well-known/terraform.json advertises providers.v1, so the CLI needs no extra configuration. Use this host block only if discovery fails:

Host mapping fallback

host "opendepot.defdev.io" {
  services = {
    "providers.v1" = "https://opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot/providers/v1/"
  }
}

Authenticate with a credentials "opendepot.defdev.io" block, as in the mirror examples. Use direct identity only for private or internal providers. Use the Network Mirror workflow for providers from registry.opentofu.org or registry.terraform.io.

docs.title: Next Steps for Admins
docs.text: For publishing and lifecycle operations, see Registry Operations. For scanning, see Vulnerability Scanning. For redirects and storage, see Pre-signed URL Redirects.

docs.title: ScanPolicy Access with SecurityGroupBinding
docs.text:
SecurityGroupBinding is a namespaced CRD for ScanPolicy administration. It is separate from GroupBinding, which controls Registry and browse access to Modules and Providers. A user may be authorized for one workflow without being authorized for the other.

SecurityGroupBindings are created in the OpenDepot server namespace, normally opendepot-system. The server sorts bindings by name and applies the first binding whose expression matches the authenticated user's OIDC groups. It does not combine grants from multiple bindings.

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: SecurityGroupBinding
metadata:
  name: 10-platform-scan-policy-admins
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"platform-security" in groups'
  namespaces:
    - platform
  moduleResources:
    - terraform-aws-*
  providerResources:
    - aws
  namespaceWidePolicyManagement: false

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Field Description expression Required expr-lang boolean expression evaluated against groups []string. namespaces Policy namespace allow-list. An empty list allows no namespaces; "*" allows namespaces reachable by the server ServiceAccount. moduleResources Allowed Module names using path.Match glob semantics. An empty list allows no Module targets. providerResources Allowed Provider names. Names are exact; "*" allows all onboarded Providers. An empty list allows no Provider targets. namespaceWidePolicyManagement When true, allows selector-based policies and policies without targetRefs in an allowed namespace. Defaults to false.

The server discovers the effective binding independently for every request. Malformed expressions, expression evaluation errors, missing matches, and failed binding discovery fail closed. A later binding cannot bypass an invalid earlier binding.

For a scoped operator, a policy must have no selector, at least one targetRef, and every target must be an allowed Module or Provider. The UI offers only existing, authorized resources in the selected namespace. The server remains authoritative and does not trust names or scope supplied by the UI.

Selectors and empty targetRefs are allowed only when namespaceWidePolicyManagement: true. Updates authorize both the persisted and proposed policy, so an authorized targeted policy cannot be widened into an unauthorized selector or namespace-wide policy. Deletes reauthorize the persisted policy before removing it.

docs.title: Catalog and UI
docs.text:
The policy UI obtains its namespace and target choices from the server-authorized catalog:

GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/catalog

The response contains writesEnabled and sorted namespace items. Each item contains canRead, canWrite, canManageNamespaceWidePolicies, and sorted modules and providers lists. Unauthorized namespaces, resources, bindings, and patterns are not disclosed. The UI does not use the public browse namespace endpoint for policy discovery and does not accept arbitrary target names.

The global server.policyManagement.enabled value is a separate write gate and defaults to false. Enabling it adds write permissions to the server ServiceAccount; it does not grant an OIDC user access. Writes are also disabled when server.anonymousAuth is true. Keep it disabled when policies are managed only through GitOps. Kubeconfig and bearer-token requests continue to rely on the caller's Kubernetes RBAC, while OIDC requests use the SecurityGroupBinding scope described above.

docs.title: Migration and Rollout
docs.text:
Create and test SecurityGroupBindings before enabling UI writes. A least-privilege rollout is:

  1. Apply the SecurityGroupBinding CRD and create a binding with explicit namespaces and resource lists.
  2. Confirm the catalog exposes only the intended namespaces and onboarded targets.
  3. Deploy the chart with server.policyManagement.enabled: false and verify existing Registry and scan behavior.
  4. Enable policy writes only after authorized and unauthorized preview, create, update, and delete requests have been tested.

To roll back, disable server.policyManagement.enabled first. Existing ScanPolicy objects remain available to the controller and are not deleted by disabling the UI write gate. Keep the CRD installed until policy objects have been removed through the chosen declarative workflow.

See the API reference and Kubernetes RBAC for the resource and ServiceAccount permissions.

docs.title: OpenDepot CLI
docs.text:
The opendepot CLI installs Agent Skills and Agents from an OpenDepot registry into a project. It records each installed item in opendepot.lock.hcl with a hash, and it checks those hashes before anything is written.

Use this skill to find approved skills and agents, install them, and verify them. Do not treat the CLI as a way to edit installed skills or agents.

docs.title: Find skills and agents
docs.text:
Search the registry before you build a capability from scratch. If a task needs something you do not already have, such as a tool workflow, a review checklist, or domain guidance, check whether an approved skill or agent already exists. Searching is read-only and cheap, so search whenever you are unsure. Do not wait for a person's permission to search. Installing an approved item also does not need permission.

  1. Search the catalog. Run opendepot list skills --registry <host> --json and opendepot list agents --registry <host> --json. The JSON includes full descriptions, so match the task's keywords against them. Add --namespace <name> to narrow the search.
  2. Check the candidates. Run opendepot describe skill <namespace/name> --registry <host>, or opendepot describe agent for agents. Read the description, latest version, risk level, and assessment.
  3. Use only approved items. An item can be installed when list shows a version and the status available. Do not install an item with any other status, such as assessment failed, or one that describe shows as blocked or rejected.
  4. Install through the lock file. Add a block to opendepot.hcl, then run opendepot plan, opendepot apply --no-prompt, and opendepot verify:
agent_skill "gh-actions-debug" {
  source  = "demo.opendepot.defdev.io/opendepot-system/gh-actions-debug"
  version = "0.9.0"
  path    = ".github/skills/gh-actions-debug"
}

Use agent "<name>" instead of agent_skill for agents. The source is <host>/<namespace>/<name>. For a skill, set path to a directory inside the project. 5. Use the item. Read the installed SKILL.md or agent file and follow it for the task. In your reply, name the registry item and version you used.

If no approved item fits the task, say so in your reply and continue with your own approach. Do not fill the gap by copying a skill from GitHub, a web page, or another project.

docs.title: Rules for agents
docs.text:
• Never edit an installed skill or agent file. Installed files are owned by the lock file. Make changes in the source repository and publish a new version.
  • Run opendepot verify before you finish a task that touched installed items, and after any step that might have changed them.
  • Run opendepot plan before opendepot apply so you can read what will change.
  • Do not pass --force, --trust-new-key, or --allow-yanked without explicit approval from a person. --force overwrites AGENTS.md blocks that were edited by hand, --trust-new-key accepts a rotated signing key, and --allow-yanked installs a yanked version.
  • Use --no-prompt in automation. The command then fails instead of asking a question.
  • Run the CLI from the project root. The lock file is read from the current directory.
  • If verify fails because an installed skill or agent changed, run opendepot apply with no flags to restore it from the lock file, then run opendepot verify again. Do not restore the file by hand.
  • If apply refuses because an AGENTS.md block was edited by hand, stop and report it. Do not pass --force yourself.
  • Do not edit opendepot.lock.hcl by hand.
  • Get new skills and agents only from a registry through this CLI. Do not copy them from GitHub, a web page, or another project, even when they look useful.
  • Do not pass --allow-older-versions without approval from a person. It installs an older version after the newest one was blocked, rejected, or failed assessment.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Purpose opendepot login <host> Sign in to a registry host. opendepot plan Show what apply would install, upgrade, or change. Writes nothing. opendepot apply Install or update items from the lock file. Writes files. opendepot list skills List skills. Use --registry and --namespace to filter, and --json for full descriptions. opendepot list agents List agents. Use --registry and --namespace to filter, and --json for full descriptions. opendepot describe skill <namespace/name> Show details for one skill. Use --registry to choose a host. opendepot describe agent <namespace/name> Show details for one agent. Use --registry to choose a host. opendepot validate [path] Check a local skill or agent source before you publish it. opendepot verify Check that installed items still match the lock file. Read-only and does not use the network.

docs.title: Flags for apply and plan
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --upgrade Re-resolve version constraints instead of using the locked versions. --allow-yanked Allow yanked versions. --allow-older-versions Install an older matching version when the newest one is blocked, rejected, or failed assessment. --trust-new-key Re-pin a rotated signing key. --no-prompt Never prompt. Fail instead. --force Overwrite AGENTS.md blocks that were edited by hand. apply only.

plan accepts the same flags except --no-prompt.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm the project has opendepot.hcl or opendepot.lock.hcl. If it has neither, ask a person which registry to use. To add a new item, follow Find skills and agents first, then run steps 3 to 5.
  2. Run opendepot verify. If an installed item changed, restore it as described in the rules. If the lock file is invalid, report it.
  3. Run opendepot plan to see any pending changes.
  4. Run opendepot apply only when the plan is expected.
  5. Run opendepot verify again.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hooks can run opendepot verify before every tool call. When a check fails, the hook blocks the call and tells you to run opendepot apply. It allows that restore through, so you can recover without a person. See Verify with Agent Hooks for Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot configuration. Do not add, remove, or change hooks.

docs.title: Raw version
docs.text: Agents can read this skill as raw Markdown at https://opendepot.defdev.io/docs/guides/opendepot-cli/SKILL.md.

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop
docs.text:
OpenDepot Workshop is a browsable, searchable frontend for OpenDepot. The Workshop includes the Registry Explorer, resource details, Depots, Stats, Assembly Line, and Security Policies. Enable it by setting ui.enabled: true in the Helm chart.

Note

The UI is disabled by default. Existing server-only deployments are unaffected when ui.enabled remains false.

docs.title: Workshop components
docs.text:
OpenDepot Workshop brings the following user-facing workflows together:

  • Registry Explorer — discover modules and providers, then open their versions and resource details.
  • Module Details and Provider Details — inspect README content, contracts, schemas, artifacts, versions, and scan findings.
  • Agent Details and Skill Details — inspect client configuration, definitions, versions, Jev assessments, and scan findings.
  • Depots — review where resources are managed and how they are discovered.
  • Stats — compare synchronization health, resource counts, storage, and security findings.
  • Assembly Line — compose onboarded modules and providers into a validated, downloadable root module.
  • Security Policies — review and manage scan policies when policy management is enabled and you have the required permissions.

The components follow the same authentication and visibility rules. If a resource or workflow is not visible, check the current authentication mode, public labels, and any applicable GroupBinding.

docs.title: Navigate OpenDepot Workshop
docs.text:
Use the Workshop components as the starting point for a focused workflow:

  1. Select a module in the Registry Explorer to open Module Details. Review its README and usage block, then inspect its normalized contract, configuration, versions, and scan findings.
  2. Select a provider in the Registry Explorer to open Provider Details. Review provider identity and synchronization status, then drill into platform versions and source or binary findings.
  3. Select an agent or skill in the Registry Explorer to open Agent Details or Skill Details. Copy the client configuration, review the definition, and inspect versions and Jev assessments.
  4. Select a version from any details page to inspect the exact archive, checksum, scan timestamp, and findings associated with that version.
  5. Open a Depot to understand which storage backend and discovery settings manage its modules and providers.
  6. Open Stats to compare synchronization health and security posture across the resources visible to you.
  7. Open Assembly Line to compose onboarded modules and providers into a validated, downloadable root module.
  8. Open Security Policies to review or manage scan policies when policy management is enabled and you have the required permissions.

docs.text:

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop Administration
docs.text: This page covers deployment, authentication, routing, and visibility controls for OpenDepot Workshop. For the user-facing Workshop and its Registry Explorer and resource details, see the OpenDepot Workshop guide.

docs.title: Routing Architecture
docs.text:
When ui.enabled: true, OpenDepot deploys a Next.js frontend alongside the server. NGINX runs inside the UI pod and splits traffic between the registry protocol server and the browser UI:

Path Destination /opendepot/* Server — registry protocol and browse API /.well-known/terraform.json Server — service discovery /dex/* Server — Dex proxy, when server.oidc.dexProxy.enabled: true / (all other paths) Next.js UI at port 3000

When ui.ingress.enabled: true, the Ingress sends every configured path to the ui Service. The UI pod's NGINX applies the split above.

When server.ingress.istio.enabled: true and ui.enabled: true, the Istio VirtualService routes /opendepot, /.well-known, and /dex (when the Dex proxy is enabled) to the server and all other paths to the UI.

Warning

When ui.enabled: true, the server-ingress.yaml template is automatically disabled. If you were previously routing directly through the server Ingress, migrate to ui.ingress before enabling the UI.

docs.title: Local Quick Start with Tilt
docs.text:
The fastest way to try OpenDepot Workshop is the repository's Tilt environment. It creates or reuses a local Kind cluster, builds the complete stack, configures Dex OIDC, generates development secrets, and enables live updates.

Install the local quickstart prerequisites, then run from the repository root:

export OPENDEPOT_DEV_PASSWORD='choose-a-local-password'
tilt/scripts/up.sh

Wait for the ui resource to become ready in the Tilt dashboard, then open https://opendepot.localtest.me:8443. Sign in as dev@example.com with the value of OPENDEPOT_DEV_PASSWORD.

Create sample resources from the Tilt dashboard or run:

tilt trigger seed-sample-resources

The sample GroupBinding grants the local user access to the seeded resources. Refresh OpenDepot Workshop to browse version metadata, READMEs, and scan findings.

Stop Tilt with Ctrl+C, then remove the deployed resources while preserving the local cluster and image registry:

tilt down

docs.title: Create the session secret
docs.text:
The UI uses encrypted server-side session cookies. Provide a secret of at least 32 characters before deploying:

kubectl create secret generic ui-session-secret \
  --from-literal=sessionPassword=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  -n opendepot-system

docs.title: Register an OIDC client
docs.text:
When ui.oidc.enabled: true, the UI uses the OIDC authorization code flow to authenticate users. The groups claim from the resulting token is matched against GroupBinding resources. Skip this step if you only need anonymous browsing.

Add a staticClient to your Dex configuration:

dex:
  config:
    staticClients:
      - id: opendepot-ui
        name: OpenDepot UI
        secretEnv: OPENDEPOT_UI_CLIENT_SECRET
        redirectURIs:
          - https://opendepot.example.com/auth/callback
        responseTypes:
          - code
        grantTypes:
          - authorization_code

Create the client secret. The UI reads the clientSecret key, and Dex reads OPENDEPOT_UI_CLIENT_SECRET. Both keys must hold the same value:

kubectl create secret generic ui-oidc-secret \
  --from-literal=clientSecret=<your-client-secret> \
  --from-literal=OPENDEPOT_UI_CLIENT_SECRET=<your-client-secret> \
  -n opendepot-system

Dex loads this Secret through dex.envFrom. Helm replaces list values, so keep the default entry:

dex:
  envFrom:
    - secretRef:
        name: opendepot-dex-client-secret
        optional: true
    - secretRef:
        name: ui-oidc-secret

docs.title: Set Helm values
docs.text:
At minimum:

ui:
  enabled: true
  sessionPasswordSecretName: ui-session-secret
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    className: nginx
    annotations:
      nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    hosts:
      - host: opendepot.example.com
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
    tls:
      - secretName: opendepot-tls
        hosts:
          - opendepot.example.com

To enable OIDC login, add:

ui:
  oidc:
    enabled: true
    issuerUrl: https://dex.example.com/dex
    clientId: opendepot-ui
    clientSecretName: ui-oidc-secret
    scopes: "openid profile email groups"
    callbackPath: /auth/callback

Developer token input — never enable in production

ui.auth.devTokenInput.enabled: true renders a token input field in the Sidebar for testing the UI against a live cluster. The default is false.

See Helm Chart — UI Configuration for the full ui.* Helm values reference.

docs.title: Apply the chart
docs.text:
helm upgrade opendepot opendepot/opendepot \
  --namespace opendepot-system \
  -f values.yaml

docs.title: Public Visibility Labels
docs.text:
By default, browse endpoints return only resources explicitly marked as public:

Label Applied to Effect opendepot.defdev.io/public: "true" Kubernetes Namespace Marks the namespace as publicly discoverable opendepot.defdev.io/public: "true" Module or Provider Marks the resource as publicly viewable

A resource is public only when both its namespace and the resource carry the label.

kubectl label namespace opendepot-system opendepot.defdev.io/public=true

docs.title: Browse Visibility Rules
docs.text:
Caller Resources visible Unauthenticated in OIDC mode with anonymous access disabled 401 Unauthorized Unauthenticated in non-OIDC or anonymous mode Public namespace and public resources OIDC-authenticated without a matching GroupBinding Public namespace and public resources OIDC-authenticated with a matching GroupBinding Public resources plus resources allowed by the binding anonymousAuth: true All resources; public_only=true still filters to public resources Non-OIDC bearer token Public resources only

Namespace list is always label-filtered

The namespace endpoint always enforces the opendepot.defdev.io/public=true label. System namespaces are never returned regardless of auth mode.

docs.title: GroupBinding for Browse Access
docs.text:
GroupBinding resources grant OIDC-authenticated users access beyond the public set. They use an expr-lang expression against the OIDC groups claim.

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: GroupBinding
metadata:
  name: platform-team-binding
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"platform-team" in groups'
  moduleResources:
    - "terraform-aws-*"
    - "terraform-gcp-vpc"
  providerResources:
    - "aws"
    - "google"

See GroupBinding Access Control for full expression syntax, client credentials, and first-match semantics.

docs.title: Related Guides
docs.text:
• OpenDepot Workshop
  • Module Details
  • Provider Details
  • Agent Details

docs.title: Agent Details
docs.text: The Agent Details page shows one Agent: its latest version, the opendepot.hcl snippet for each supported client, its frontmatter and AGENT.md definition, tools and model metadata, versions, and scan findings.

docs.title: Agent identity and status
docs.text: The breadcrumb shows the namespace and kind. The header shows the agent name, the latest synchronized version, the source ref and commit, and sync status. When Jev is enabled, the header also shows the risk level from the latest Jev assessment.

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text:
The opendepot.hcl section provides a copyable agent block for the agent. Choose a tab to match your client:

  • Claude
  • Copilot
  • OpenAI
  • Generic

Copy the snippet into your opendepot.hcl file. See Consuming Agents and Skills for how the block is used.

docs.title: Jev Assessment
docs.text: When Jev is enabled and the latest version has an assessment, the Jev Assessment section shows the risk level, risk score, confidence, a probability for each risk category, and the files that were assessed. See Jev Assessment for how to read the results.

docs.title: Frontmatter and definition
docs.text:
The Frontmatter section shows the metadata parsed from the top of AGENT.md, including the name, description, and tools fields.

The AGENT.md section renders the agent definition from the latest version.

docs.title: Tools and Model
docs.text: The Tools and Model section appears only when the agent declares a model or tools. It lists the tools from the frontmatter as chips. When the agent sets a model, the section also shows the model.

docs.title: Overview, storage, GitHub, and Depot settings
docs.text:
The Overview section lists the provider, repository owner, source path, version history limit, and version constraints.

The Storage Configuration section shows the backend and its location fields. The GitHub Configuration section shows the authenticated client used for source metadata, if one is configured.

The Depot section appears only when the agent is managed by a Depot. It names the Depot that manages the agent. Agents that you manage through GitOps do not have a Depot section.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The Versions view lists the synchronized versions of the agent with their sync status, resource name, archive filename, commit, checksum, last scan time, and findings. Use the search field and Sync status filter to narrow the list, and use the pagination controls to move between pages.

docs.title: Scan Findings
docs.text: The Scan Findings section lists the source scan findings for the selected version, with the count in the heading. Use the version selector to view findings for another version.

docs.title: Related views
docs.text:
• Workshop
  • Skill Details
  • Browse resources and dashboards
  • Consuming Agents and Skills
  • Workshop authentication

docs.title: OpenDepot Workshop Browse API
docs.text: The browse endpoints power OpenDepot Workshop and can also be called directly for integrations and automation. In OIDC mode with anonymous access disabled, requests require an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

docs.title: List Namespaces
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/namespaces

Returns namespaces carrying the opendepot.defdev.io/public=true label. System namespaces are never returned.

{
  "items": [
    { "name": "opendepot-system", "public": true }
  ]
}

docs.title: List Resources
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources

Returns a paginated list of visible Module and Provider resources.

Parameter Type Description namespace string (repeatable) Namespace filter kind string module or provider q string Name search synced bool Synced or unsynced resources os / arch string Provider platform filters severity string Minimum finding severity public_only bool Public resources only sort_by / sort_dir string Sort field (name, namespace, latest_version, kind, source, status, risk) and direction (asc, desc) page / page_size int Pagination controls

docs.title: Resource Detail
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}

Returns full detail for one resource, including versions and latest-version scan findings. The readmeContent field is present for modules when a README was resolved.

docs.title: List Resource Versions
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/versions

Returns a paginated, filtered version list. Supported query parameters include page, page_size, q, synced, os, and arch. Provider responses also include availableOS and availableArch for filter controls.

docs.title: Resource Scan Findings
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/scan-findings

Returns findings for the latest scanned version. Use ?version=<semver> for a specific source scan or ?binaryVersion=<semver> for a provider binary scan. See the API Reference for the full response schema.

docs.title: Depot Relationship Graph
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/depots/graph

Returns visible Depot, Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources with edges connecting each depot to the resources it manages. OpenDepot Workshop uses this endpoint to render the Depots page.

docs.title: Module Contract
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/contract

Returns the Assembly Line input contract for a module version. Only module is supported. See the API Reference for query parameters and responses.

docs.title: Provider Configuration Schema
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/provider/{name}/provider-schema

Returns the provider configuration schema for a version. Available only when Assembly Line is enabled. See the API Reference.

docs.title: Assembly Line Export
docs.text:
POST /opendepot/ui/v1/assembly/export

Validates a canvas and returns a root module as a ZIP archive, or as a stream of progress events when the request sends Accept: application/x-ndjson. Available only when Assembly Line is enabled. See the API Reference for the request schema and error codes.

docs.title: List Depots
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/depots

Returns visible Depot resources. For the connected view, use the Depot Relationship Graph. See the API Reference.

docs.title: Registry Stats
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/stats

Returns the aggregate data behind the Stats page. See the API Reference.

docs.title: Scan Policies
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/catalog Authorized namespaces and onboarded targets GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace} List policies in a namespace GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Get one policy GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/capabilities Write support for the namespace POST /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/preview Validate without saving POST /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace} Create a policy PUT /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Replace a policy (requires If-Match) DELETE /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Delete a policy (requires If-Match)

Write routes require policy management to be enabled and anonymous access to be off. See the API Reference.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text: Stats provides an operational view of synchronization health, security posture, storage, and resource usage across the OpenDepot Workshop resources visible to you.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The dashboard (/stats) shows:

Section Description Summary Modules, providers, skills, agents, depots, versions, storage used, and downloads Sync health Synced, unsynced, and failed version counts Security posture Finding counts by severity, plus exempted findings Storage distribution Version counts by storage backend Most downloaded Resources with download totals and last-download timestamps

Summary counts come from Kubernetes resources. Download counts come from Prometheus over the lookback window set by server.stats.lookback (default 90d).

Visibility

The dashboard uses the same visibility rules as OpenDepot Workshop. OIDC users with a matching GroupBinding see the resources allowed by that binding.

docs.title: Download Tracking
docs.text:
The Server exposes download metrics at /metrics on the metrics port (9090 by default). The chart creates a ServiceMonitor when metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled is true, which is the default.

When server.stats.prometheusURL is empty, the chart points the Server at the bundled Prometheus service. Set the URL to query an existing Prometheus instead.

docs.title: Depots
docs.text:
The Depots page (/depots) renders an interactive graph of visible Depot resources and the Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources each depot manages. Every Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent with versions fans out to one node per version.

graph LR
  D[Depot] -->|manages| M1[Module A]
  D -->|manages| P[Provider]
  D -->|manages| S[Skill]
  D -->|manages| A[Agent]
  M1 --> V1[v3.19.0]
  S --> SV[v0.9.0]
  A --> AV[v0.9.0]

Select a depot from the filter to narrow the graph. Each node opens a detail panel with its namespace, name, storage backend and configuration, presigned URL settings, and sync status. Skill and Agent versions without a version string are labeled with their short commit SHA.

The graph is served by GET /opendepot/ui/v1/depots/graph and applies the same visibility rules as the rest of the Workshop.

docs.title: Module Details
docs.text: The Module Details page shows one module: its current version, README, usage, contract, storage and GitHub configuration, versions, and scan findings.

docs.title: Module identity and status
docs.text: The breadcrumb shows the namespace and kind. The header shows the module name, the latest synchronized version, sync status, and scan counts. A link to the upstream source appears when one is configured.

docs.title: Usage and README
docs.text:
The Usage section comes first and provides a copyable module block with the OpenDepot source address and version constraint.

The README section renders the module README when one is available.

docs.title: Module contract
docs.text:
The Contract section shows the normalized interface extracted from the module source: inputs and outputs with their types, required status, defaults, and descriptions.

Use Show more to expand long input or output lists. A contract appears only when Assembly Line is enabled and the version has a derived contract.

Note

Enable Assembly Line with assembly.enabled: true in the Helm values, and set server.image.tag and version.image.tag to a -assembly image tag. The UI must also be enabled with ui.enabled: true. See Assembly Line Configuration.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Overview section lists the provider, repository owner (when set), version history limit (when greater than zero), and version constraints.

docs.title: Storage Configuration
docs.text:
The Storage Configuration section shows the backend, its location fields, and Presign Enabled. When Presign Enabled is Yes, downloads use pre-signed redirects instead of streaming through the server.

When the module has no storage settings of its own, the section shows the backend inherited from its managing Depot with an Inherited From row.

docs.title: GitHub Configuration
docs.text: The GitHub Configuration section shows Authenticated Client. The value is Yes when the module uses an authenticated GitHub client for source metadata.

docs.title: Depot
docs.text: The Depot section appears when a Depot manages the module. It names that Depot as namespace / name.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
The Versions view lists synchronized module archives with their sync status, resource name, filename, checksum, scan timestamp, and findings.

Use the search field and Sync status filter to narrow the list. Each row shows the version, resource name, archive filename, checksum, last scan timestamp, and severity counts. Select a version to inspect its scan results.

docs.title: Scan Findings
docs.text:
The Scan Findings view lists findings for a selected module version. Use the Version, search, Severity, Sort by, and Order controls to filter the list.

Each finding shows its rule ID, severity, title, affected package or resource, message, and recommended resolution. Findings are deduplicated by rule ID, and only the highest-severity instance of each rule appears.

docs.title: Provider identity and status
docs.text: The breadcrumb shows the namespace and kind. The header shows the provider name, the latest version, sync status, and scan counts. A link to the upstream source appears when one is configured.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The Usage section comes first and provides copyable network mirror configuration for .tofurc or .terraformrc. The mirror URL includes the deployment and namespace shown on the page.

Field Description Provider Namespace Registry namespace, such as hashicorp. Defaults to hashicorp Upstream Registry Registry used for discovery and downloads. Defaults to registry.opentofu.org Repo Owner Repository owner. Appears when set Version History Limit Number of versions retained. Appears when greater than zero Version Constraints Constraint used to select versions

The Storage Configuration section shows the backend, its location fields, and Presign Enabled. When Presign Enabled is Yes, downloads use pre-signed redirects instead of streaming through the server.

When the provider has no storage settings of its own, the section shows the backend inherited from its managing Depot with an Inherited From row.

docs.title: Versions and findings
docs.text:
The Versions view lists each synchronized provider artifact by platform. Use the search field and the Sync status, OS, and Arch filters to narrow the list.

Each row shows the version, sync status, resource name, OS, architecture, schema extraction status (Extracted or Failed), archive filename, checksum, last scan time, and finding counts. A version appears once per OS and architecture artifact. Select a row to inspect its scan results.

docs.text:
The Scan Findings view lists the provider's source findings and binary findings in separate sections.

Use the search field and the Severity, Sort by, and Order controls to filter the source findings. Each finding shows its identifier, severity, title, message, and recommended resolution. Findings are deduplicated by rule ID.

docs.title: Registry Explorer
docs.text: The Registry Explorer is OpenDepot Workshop's discovery surface. It gives users an overview of the modules, providers, skills, and agents available to them and lets them open resource details, versions, and security information.

docs.title: Sidebar
docs.text:
The sidebar groups the Registry Explorer under a Registry item. The children filter the explorer by kind:

Item Shows Registry All kinds: agents, skills, modules, and providers. Agents Only agents. Skills Only skills. Modules Only modules. Providers Only providers.

Each item has an icon. When the sidebar is collapsed, only the icons appear. Hover over an icon to see its name in a tooltip. The search icon in the collapsed sidebar expands it and places the cursor in the search field.

docs.title: Reading the Registry Explorer
docs.text:
The explorer lists one resource per row and summarizes its latest available version. Select a row to open the resource details.

Column Meaning Kind The resource kind: Module, Provider, Skill, or Agent. Modules and providers also show the icon of their provider ecosystem, such as AWS. Name The Kubernetes namespace that owns the resource, then the resource name. A globe icon marks a public resource. Version The latest version currently shown for the resource. Source For a Skill or Agent that follows a Git ref, the tracked branch or commit. The column is hidden when no resource on the page has one. Status Whether the latest version synchronized. A healthy resource shows Synced. A failure, or a version that Jev blocked, is shown in red with its reason in a tooltip. Risk For a Skill or Agent, the Jev risk level as a five-step meter from Minimal to Critical. For a Module or Provider, the number of scan findings by severity: C critical, H high, M medium, L low, U unknown, and E exempted.

Above the list, the Sort menu orders resources by name, namespace, latest version, or last scan, and the arrow next to it reverses the order. Selecting the Name or Version column heading sorts by that column. Active namespace and search filters appear next to the resource count and can be removed there. The view toggle switches between the table and a card grid. Narrow screens always use cards.

The footer shows the resource count, the Per page setting, and pagination controls. The page size defaults to 12.

The browser saves your Per page choice, sort field and direction, and table or card view in local storage, so they persist across visits. Preferences are stored per browser, not per account.

docs.title: What users see
docs.text:

  • Providers: versions, platform artifacts, checksums, schema extraction status, and scan findings.

  • Providers with versions, platform artifacts, checksums, extracted schemas, and source or binary scan findings.
  • Skills and Agents with versions, the SKILL.md or AGENT.md definition, tools and model metadata, scan findings, and Jev assessments when enabled. See Consuming Agents and Skills.

The Registry Explorer shows the resources the current user can access. If a resource is not visible, check the current authentication mode, public labels, and any applicable GroupBinding.
