docs.title: Security Policies
docs.text:
OpenDepot Workshop provides a Security Policies view for managing ScanPolicy rules and exemptions. Open it at /security-policies to review the policies that apply to resources in a selected namespace.

Keep policies in source control

Creating policies in OpenDepot Workshop is provided for convenience, such as when you need to react to a threat immediately. Always copy the generated YAML and commit it to source control. OpenDepot Workshop assumes a GitOps workflow, where Git is the audit trail.

docs.title: Policy overview
docs.text:
The summary cards show:

  • Non-superseded — policies in effect. The caption shows the total policy count.
  • Matching resources — number of policies that match at least one version.
  • Active exemptions — exemptions currently applied to findings.
  • Expired exemptions — exemptions past their expiry. Their findings block again.

Each policy card shows its name, priority, and severity threshold (Baseline when unset). It also shows the matched version count, the active exemption count, and a Superseded by chip when another policy takes precedence. Select a policy to review its targets and exemptions.

docs.title: Find and create policies
docs.text:
Use the namespace selector to change the scope of the policy list. Use Search policies to filter by policy name, severity, or status.

Select Create policy to define a new ScanPolicy in the selected namespace.

docs.title: Create a policy
docs.text: The guided form creates a namespaced ScanPolicy and updates a live YAML preview as you work.

docs.title: Define policy identity
docs.text: Enter a lowercase DNS-compatible Name, select an authorized Namespace, and optionally set a numeric Priority. When policies overlap, the policy with the higher priority wins outright.

docs.title: Set matching and scan behavior
docs.text:
Choose a Severity threshold to control which findings block matching resources. Leave the value empty to use the controller baseline, or choose NONE to disable blocking for the policy.

Use Target labels to restrict matching to resources with exact label pairs. Enter the labels as a JSON object, for example:

{"environment":"sandbox"}

You can also add explicit Target resources. Each target has a kind (Module, Provider, Skill, or Agent), a resource name, and an optional Version constraint, such as >= 1.0.0, < 2.0.0. Select from authorized onboarded resources. Use * as the name to match every resource of that kind. When no explicit targets are configured, the policy relies on its other matching criteria.

docs.title: Add finding exemptions
docs.text:
Use Add exemption to exempt a finding from the policy. Every exemption must include a reason. Leave its expiry empty for an indefinite exemption.

Each exemption can be narrowed with these fields:

  • Vulnerability IDs — enter one or more vulnerability identifiers, such as CVE-2026-0001 or AWS-0057. Use * to match any vulnerability ID.
  • Package names — enter one or more package names, such as stdlib or golang.org/x/net. Use * to match any package.
  • Severities — select the finding severity or leave the filter at All.
  • Scan types — select the scan type or leave the filter at All.
  • Reason — required documentation for why the finding is exempted.
  • Expires — optional date after which the exemption no longer applies.

Use the trash button to remove an exemption before saving. The live YAML preview adds each configured exemption under spec.exemptions.

docs.title: Validate and create
docs.text: Review the generated scanpolicy.yaml in the live preview. Use the copy button to copy the manifest, Validate policy to check the configuration, or Create policy to submit it. Use Cancel to return to the policy list without creating a resource.

docs.title: Review active exemptions
docs.text:
After you create a policy with an exemption, the Security Policies page shows the active exemption in the summary card and on the policy card. The exemption count is separate from matched-version counts. Open the policy to review the finding filters, reason, and expiry date.

OpenDepot Workshop also reflects active exemptions on affected resource cards. The card keeps its normal sync status and finding-severity badges, and adds an E badge for exempted findings. For example, the terraform-aws-s3 v1.2.0 card shows H 4, M 1, L 2, and E 1. These badges indicate four high-severity findings, one medium-severity finding, two low-severity findings, and one exempted finding.

On a module's Scan Findings section, an exempted finding remains in the findings table with its original severity. Its Resolution column displays an Exempted badge, while findings without exemptions show a dash (—).

The findings count still includes the displayed finding. Use the version selector, search, severity filter, and sorting controls to inspect the findings for a specific module version.

docs.title: Blocked versions
docs.text:
After you create a policy with a blocking threshold, a blocked version appears in the module's Versions section with a warning that some versions are out of sync. The affected version's sync status reports the policy violation, including the blocking severity, vulnerability ID, and resource location.

The blocked version remains listed with its findings badges, while unaffected versions can continue to show Successfully synced version. This differs from an exemption: an exempted finding is marked in the Scan Findings Resolution column, whereas a blocked version reports the policy violation in its Sync Status column.

docs.title: Superseded policies
docs.text:
When policies overlap, the higher-priority policy wins outright. The lower- priority policy remains visible in the list, but it is marked Superseded by <policy-name> so users can see which policy takes precedence.

The summary card shows the Non-superseded count with the total policy count beneath it. In the screenshot above, four policies exist and one of them is superseded, so the card reads 3 of 4 policies. A superseded policy can still be opened to review its configuration and matching resources; its status explains why it is not the effective policy when the rules overlap.

docs.title: Skill Details
docs.text: The Skill Details page shows one Skill: its latest version, the opendepot.hcl snippet for each supported client, its frontmatter and SKILL.md definition, versions, and scan findings.

docs.title: Skill identity and status
docs.text: The breadcrumb shows the namespace and kind. The header shows the skill name, the latest synchronized version, the source ref and commit, and sync status. When Jev is enabled, the header also shows the risk level from the latest Jev assessment.

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text:
The opendepot.hcl section provides a copyable agent_skill block for the skill. Choose a tab to match your client:

  • Claude
  • Copilot
  • OpenAI
  • Generic

Copy the snippet into your opendepot.hcl file. See Consuming Agents and Skills for how the block is used.

docs.title: Jev Assessment
docs.text: When Jev is enabled and the latest version has an assessment, the Jev Assessment section shows the risk level, risk score, confidence, a probability for each risk category, and the files that were assessed. See Jev Assessment for how to read the results.

docs.title: Frontmatter and definition
docs.text:
The Frontmatter section shows the metadata parsed from the top of SKILL.md, such as name, description, license, compatibility, and metadata.

The SKILL.md section renders the skill definition from the latest version.

docs.title: Overview, storage, GitHub, and Depot settings
docs.text:
The Overview section lists the provider, repository owner, source path, version history limit, and version constraints. The source path is the location of the skill within its repository.

The Storage Configuration section shows the backend and its location fields. The GitHub Configuration section shows the authenticated client used for source metadata, if one is configured.

The Depot section appears only when the skill is managed by a Depot. It names the Depot that manages the skill. Skills that you manage through GitOps do not have a Depot section.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The Versions view lists the synchronized versions of the skill with their sync status, resource name, archive filename, commit, checksum, last scan time, and findings. Use the search field and Sync status filter to narrow the list, and use the pagination controls to move between pages.

docs.title: Scan Findings
docs.text: The Scan Findings section lists the source scan findings for the selected version, with the count in the heading. Use the version selector to view findings for another version.

docs.title: agents.v1 Protocol
docs.text:
The server exposes skills and agents under the agents.v1 protocol at /opendepot/agents/v1/. {kind} is skills or agents.

Method Path Purpose GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/versions List available versions. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/download Return the archive location and checksums. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/archive Download the packaged archive. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/SHA256SUMS Return the checksums for the archive. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/SHA256SUMS.sig Return the GPG signature for SHA256SUMS. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/catalog List the skills and agents the caller can see.

When OIDC is enabled, GroupBinding authorization gates the artifact handlers. These include the agent and skill metadata, the versions, SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.sig, and archive requests. The skillResources and agentResources fields of a GroupBinding control which skills and agents a group can read. A denied request returns 403 Forbidden.

The archive endpoint authorizes the request before it serves the archive. For a private agent, the request needs a bearer token and a GroupBinding that allows the agent. A request without a token returns 401 Unauthorized. With server.anonymousAuth enabled, the archive downloads without a token.

When presign is enabled for the agent source, the archive endpoint returns a 307 Temporary Redirect to a presigned URL from the storage backend. The download source is the Agent Version. The controller keeps the Version's presign in sync with the source storageConfig.presign on each reconcile, so a change applies to every owned Version in one reconcile. The response has Cache-Control: private, no-store. The URL TTL defaults to 15m. Revoking a GroupBinding stops new redirects. A URL that was already issued stays valid until it expires. This is an accepted window.

If presign fails and fallbackToProxy is false, the endpoint returns 500 Internal Server Error and does not redirect. This applies to a checksum mismatch too. If fallbackToProxy is true, the server streams the archive bytes instead. The FileSystem backend always fails the presign step, so it streams only when fallback is on. fallbackToProxy defaults to false for new Agent objects. Existing Agent objects keep the value they were stored with. See Pre-signed URL Redirects.

Archive extraction enforces a decompressed-size budget of 2 GiB and a cap of 10,000 entries. An archive that exceeds either limit fails. Symbolic links and hard links are refused. The total decompressed stream, including tar headers, is capped at the 2 GiB budget plus a 64 MiB allowance for headers. The CLI verifies the SHA256SUMS signature against the pinned signing key before it installs anything.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/agents/v1/catalog lists the skills and agents the caller can see. Each item is one skill or agent, not one version. The opendepot list command uses this endpoint.

Parameter Default Rules namespace None Limits the results to one namespace. Must be a valid DNS label. page 1 Must be 1 or greater. page_size 20 Must be from 1 to 100.

An invalid parameter returns 400. A page past the end returns 200 with an empty items array. The response has items, totalCount, page, and pageSize. Items are sorted by namespace, kind, and name. If the server cannot list the resources, it returns 500 and no partial catalog.

Each item has kind (skill or agent), namespace, name, status, latestVersion, riskLevel, riskScore, unavailableCandidate, and description. latestVersion is omitted when no version is installable. unavailableCandidate is the newest unavailable candidate, in the same shape as the unavailableCandidates entries. It is omitted when there is none. description is omitted when the latest installable version has none. See Descriptions.

Status Meaning blocked The newest unavailable candidate is blocked. This applies even when an older version is installable. rejected The newest unavailable candidate is rejected. This applies even when an older version is installable. available A latest installable version exists, and the newest candidate, if any, is neither blocked nor rejected. assessmentFailed No version is installable, and the newest candidate failed assessment. pending No version is installable, and the newest candidate is pending. Also used when the resource has no versions.

An assessmentFailed or pending candidate does not change an available status. riskLevel and riskScore describe latestVersion only. They are omitted when the risk is unknown. An omitted risk field means unknown, not safe.

Auth follows the same policy as the UI browse endpoints. With anonymous auth enabled, every resource is visible. With OIDC not configured, only public resources are listed. With OIDC configured, a missing or invalid Bearer token returns 401. A valid token shows public resources and the resources its GroupBindings allow. Unlike the artifact endpoints above, the catalog does not return 403.

docs.title: Descriptions
docs.text: Each item can include description. It is the description from the frontmatter of the latest installable version, the same version named by latestVersion. The field is omitted when that version has no description, and when no version is installable. It is author-declared text and is untrusted. Clients must not render it as markup, and must treat it as plain text. The parser limits descriptions to 1024 bytes. Versions synced before the description was recorded have no description until they are synced again.

docs.title: Detail fields for describe
docs.text: opendepot describe skill and opendepot describe agent read the UI browse detail endpoint, GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}, not the catalog. The table and --json output show the same fields, under the same visibility rules. The detail includes latestVersion, synced, syncStatus, hasUnsyncedVersions, public, blocked, blockReasons, jevRiskLevel, sourceRef, sourceCommit, sourcePath, repoUrl, repoOwner, scanCounts, lastScanned, totalDownloads, lastDownloadedAt, definitionFileName, definitionContent, agentMetadata (name, description, tools, model), storageConfig (backend, bucket, region, key, directoryPath, accountName, accountUrl, subscriptionID, resourceGroup, presignEnabled, presignTTL), githubConfig (useAuthenticatedClient), and sourceScanFindings. Each finding has vulnerabilityID, pkgName, installedVersion, fixedVersion, severity, title, exempted, exemptionReason, and exemptedBy. The table shows the storage, GitHub, and finding fields in rows and writes finding text through the same sanitizer as the rest of the table. Unset storage and GitHub settings are null in --json, and sourceScanFindings is [] when there are none. Each entry in versions has name, version, synced, syncStatus, branchPhase, blocked, blockReasons, fileName, checksum, archiveSizeBytes, downloadCount, lastDownloadedAt, lastScanned, scanCounts, schemaState, schemaMessage, and schemaAttemptedAt. The detail also includes jevAssessment, jevExemptionGovernance, jevUnblock, and jevThresholds. Policy names in the governance and unblock fields are omitted for OIDC callers. The table omits empty fields, and definitionContent appears only in --json. description is untrusted author text and is shown as plain text.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Name collisions. Version names use a prefix-name-version pattern without escaping. A Skill and an Agent that produce the same Version name can collide. A collision returns 404 and never serves the wrong object.
  • Checksum source. On S3, the archive checksum check uses the object's SHA-256 checksum metadata. It does not hash the archive bytes.
  • Anonymous download. On an OIDC-only server, a public agent still needs a bearer token. Anonymous download is available only when server.anonymousAuth is enabled.
  • Revocation window. A revoked GroupBinding does not invalidate a presigned URL that was already issued. The URL stays valid until its TTL expires.

docs.text:

docs.text: For breaking changes between versions, see Upgrading.

docs.title: Service Discovery
docs.text:
GET /.well-known/terraform.json

Response:

{
  "modules.v1": "/opendepot/modules/v1/",
  "providers.v1": "/opendepot/providers/v1/",
  "login.v1": {
    "client": "opentofu-cli",
    "grant_types": ["authz_code", "device_code"],
    "authz": "https://opendepot.example.com/dex/auth",
    "token": "https://opendepot.example.com/dex/token",
    "ports": [10000, 10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006, 10007, 10008, 10009, 10010]
  }
}

The authz and token URLs above assume the recommended server-proxied Dex setup, so they share the same host as the rest of the registry API. Without the proxy, they point at wherever Dex itself is exposed.

The login.v1 field is only present when OIDC authentication is enabled. It advertises the OIDC endpoints and ports that the tofu login command uses to obtain a JWT.

docs.title: OIDC Device Authorization
docs.text:
POST {login.v1.authz}

Initiates the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow. Used by tofu login on headless systems (servers, CI runners) to obtain a device code and user code.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Description client_id From login.v1.client scope Space-separated scopes (e.g. openid profile email groups)

Response:

{
  "device_code": "AQABAGF...",
  "user_code": "WXYZ-ABCD",
  "verification_uri": "https://opendepot.example.com/dex/device",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "interval": 5
}

docs.title: OIDC Token Exchange
docs.text:
POST {login.v1.token}

Exchanges an authorization code (authz_code flow) or device code (device_code flow) for a JWT. Used by tofu login to obtain the bearer token returned to the client.

Request (authz_code grant):

POST https://opendepot.example.com/dex/token
grant_type=authorization_code&code=<AUTH_CODE>&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=http://localhost:10000/login

Request (device_code grant):

POST https://opendepot.example.com/dex/token
grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code&device_code=<DEVICE_CODE>&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>

Response:

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "id_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs..."
}

The id_token (JWT) is returned to tofu login and subsequently passed to OpenDepot as a bearer token in the Authorization: Bearer <id_token> header.

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
All endpoints that require authentication accept the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. The server operates in one of the following modes, configured at startup:

Mode Value Token accepted K8s calls use Anonymous --anonymous-auth None Server SA Kubeconfig (default) Base64-encoded kubeconfig Caller's kubeconfig identity Bearer token --use-bearer-token SA bearer token Caller's SA RBAC OIDC --oidc-issuer-url + --oidc-client-id Dex JWT Server SA (GroupBinding controls access) OIDC + SA fallback above + --oidc-allow-sa-fallback Dex JWT or SA token Dex JWT → Server SA; SA token → Caller's SA RBAC OIDC + client credentials above + --oidc-allow-client-credentials + --oidc-client-credentials-audiences Dex client credentials token whose aud is allowlisted Server SA (GroupBinding matches client:<sub>)

docs.title: List Module Versions
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/modules/v1/{namespace}/{name}/{system}/versions

Returns all available versions of a module. Requires authentication.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the Module resource name Module name system Provider (e.g., aws, azurerm)

docs.title: Download Module
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/modules/v1/{namespace}/{name}/{system}/{version}/download

Returns 204 No Content with an X-Terraform-Get header pointing to the storage-specific download URL. Requires authentication.

docs.title: Storage Download Endpoints (Modules)
docs.text:
These endpoints are called by OpenTofu/Terraform after receiving the X-Terraform-Get redirect. They validate the SHA256 checksum and stream the module archive.

GET /opendepot/modules/v1/download/s3/{bucket}/{region}/{name}/{fileName}?fileChecksum={checksum}
GET /opendepot/modules/v1/download/azure/{subID}/{rg}/{account}/{accountUrl}/{name}/{fileName}?fileChecksum={checksum}
GET /opendepot/modules/v1/download/gcs/{bucket}/{name}/{fileName}?fileChecksum={checksum}
GET /opendepot/modules/v1/download/fileSystem/{directory}/{name}/{fileName}?fileChecksum={checksum}

docs.title: List Provider Versions
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/v1/{namespace}/{type}/versions

Returns all available versions of a provider and the platforms each version supports. Requires authentication.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the Provider resource type Provider name (e.g., aws, azurerm)

Response:

{
  "versions": [
    {
      "version": "5.80.0",
      "protocols": ["6.0"],
      "platforms": [
        { "os": "linux", "arch": "amd64" },
        { "os": "linux", "arch": "arm64" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Provider Package Metadata
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/v1/{namespace}/{type}/{version}/download/{os}/{arch}

Returns the download URL, SHA256 checksum, and GPG signing key for a specific provider binary. Requires authentication.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the Provider resource type Provider name version Provider version os Operating system (e.g., linux, darwin) arch CPU architecture (e.g., amd64, arm64)

Response:

{
  "protocols": ["6.0"],
  "os": "linux",
  "arch": "amd64",
  "filename": "terraform-provider-aws_5.80.0_linux_amd64.zip",
  "download_url": "https://.../opendepot/providers/v1/download/opendepot-system/aws/5.80.0/linux/amd64",
  "shasum": "<hex-sha256>",
  "shasums_url": "https://.../opendepot/providers/v1/opendepot-system/aws/5.80.0/SHA256SUMS/linux/amd64",
  "shasums_signature_url": "https://.../opendepot/providers/v1/opendepot-system/aws/5.80.0/SHA256SUMS.sig/linux/amd64",
  "signing_keys": {
    "gpg_public_keys": [
      {
        "key_id": "<KEY_ID>",
        "ascii_armor": "-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----\n..."
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Provider Binary Download
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/v1/download/{namespace}/{type}/{version}/{os}/{arch}

Streams the provider binary archive (.zip) directly from storage. Does not require client authentication — the server uses its own ServiceAccount per the Terraform Provider Registry Protocol, which both OpenTofu and Terraform implement.

docs.title: Provider SHA256SUMS
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/v1/{namespace}/{type}/{version}/SHA256SUMS/{os}/{arch}

Returns the SHA256SUMS text file for the specified provider version and platform. Does not require client authentication.

docs.title: Provider SHA256SUMS Signature
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/v1/{namespace}/{type}/{version}/SHA256SUMS.sig/{os}/{arch}

Returns the detached GPG signature over the SHA256SUMS file, signed with the key configured in server.gpg.secretName. Does not require client authentication.

docs.title: Provider Network Mirror Protocol
docs.text:
OpenDepot implements the Provider Network Mirror Protocol (shared by both OpenTofu and Terraform) so configurations can reference providers by their canonical upstream identity (e.g., registry.opentofu.org/hashicorp/aws or registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws) while installing from OpenDepot. The mirror URL is namespace-scoped:

https://<host>/opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/<namespace>/

Clients configure this URL in their .tofurc via the provider_installation.network_mirror block. See Consuming Providers for full usage examples.

docs.title: Mirror: List Provider Versions
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/{namespace}/{hostname}/{providerNamespace}/{type}/index.json

Returns all available versions of a provider from the specified origin registry. Requires authentication when anonymous mode is disabled.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the Provider resource hostname Origin registry hostname (registry.opentofu.org or registry.terraform.io) providerNamespace Provider namespace at the origin (e.g., hashicorp, datadog) type Provider name (e.g., aws, azurerm)

Response:

{
  "versions": {
    "5.80.0": {},
    "5.81.0": {}
  }
}

The version keys are normalized semver strings without a leading v. The values are empty objects per the Network Mirror Protocol specification.

docs.title: Mirror: Provider Version Metadata
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/{namespace}/{hostname}/{providerNamespace}/{type}/{version}.json

Returns archive URLs and checksums for all OS/architecture combinations of a specific provider version. Requires authentication when anonymous mode is disabled.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the Provider resource hostname Origin registry hostname (registry.opentofu.org or registry.terraform.io)

Response:

{
  "archives": {
    "linux_amd64": {
      "url": "5.80.0/linux/amd64/terraform-provider-aws_5.80.0_linux_amd64.zip",
      "hashes": ["zh:abc123..."]
    },
    "linux_arm64": {
      "url": "5.80.0/linux/arm64/terraform-provider-aws_5.80.0_linux_arm64.zip",
      "hashes": ["zh:def456..."]
    }
  }
}

The url field is a relative path from the mirror base URL. The hashes array uses the zh: prefix for packed ZIP checksums as required by the Network Mirror Protocol.

docs.title: Mirror: Provider Archive Download
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/providers/mirror/v1/{namespace}/{hostname}/{providerNamespace}/{type}/{version}/{os}/{arch}/{filename}

Streams the provider binary archive (.zip) directly from storage. Does not require client authentication when using anonymous mirror access — the server uses its own ServiceAccount. Archive URLs are discovered via the version metadata endpoint above.

docs.title: Browse API
docs.text: The browse endpoints power OpenDepot Workshop and can also be called directly. All endpoints are accessible without authentication; providing an Authorization: Bearer <token> header extends visibility per the browse visibility rules.

docs.title: List Namespaces
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/namespaces

Returns only namespaces that carry the opendepot.defdev.io/public=true label. The label selector is sent directly to the Kubernetes API, so system namespaces (kube-system, default, kube-public) are never included in the response regardless of auth mode. The public field is always true because unlabeled namespaces are excluded before the response is built.

An admin must label a namespace before it appears in the sidebar:

kubectl label namespace <ns> opendepot.defdev.io/public=true

Response:

{
  "items": [
    { "name": "opendepot-system", "public": true }
  ]
}

docs.title: List Resources
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources

Returns a paginated, filtered list of visible Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description namespace string (repeatable) Filter by one or more namespaces kind string module, provider, skill, or agent. Omit to return all four kinds. q string Search string matched against resource name synced bool Filter to synced (true) or unsynced (false) resources os string Filter providers by operating system arch string Filter providers by CPU architecture severity string Filter to resources with findings at or above this level (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) public_only bool When true, return only publicly-labelled resources sort_by string Sort field: name, namespace, latest_version, kind, source, status, or risk sort_dir string asc or desc page int Page number (1-based) page_size int Results per page

Response:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "kind": "module",
      "namespace": "opendepot-system",
      "name": "terraform-aws-vpc",
      "latestVersion": "3.19.0",
      "synced": true,
      "provider": "aws",
      "repoUrl": "https://github.com/terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-vpc",
      "scanCounts": { "critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 0, "unknown": 0, "exempted": 0 },
      "public": true,
      "hasUnsyncedVersions": true,
      "totalDownloads": 4821,
      "lastDownloadedAt": "2026-05-25T14:32:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "pageSize": 20
}

hasUnsyncedVersions is present and true when at least one Version CR under the resource has status.synced: false or a status.syncStatus containing "failed" or "error" (case-insensitive). The field is omitted from the response when all versions are healthy.

For skill and agent resources, the item includes jevRiskLevel and blocked from the Jev assessment of the Version that matches latestVersion. For a Skill or Agent with only an unversioned, blocked branch Version, blocked and blockReasons come from that Version. blockReasons is set only when blocked is true. Fields with no value are omitted.

scanCounts reflects vulnerability findings from the latest version only. The field is omitted when no version has been scanned. exempted counts findings currently exempted by a ScanPolicy and is excluded from the critical/high/medium/low/unknown counters.

docs.title: Resource Detail
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}

Returns full detail for a single resource including all versions and scan findings. The sourceScanFindings and binaryScanFindings fields contain findings from the latest version only.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the resource kind module, provider, skill, or agent name Resource name

Response:

{
  "kind": "module",
  "namespace": "opendepot-system",
  "name": "terraform-aws-vpc",
  "latestVersion": "3.19.0",
  "synced": true,
  "public": true,
  "versions": [
    { "version": "3.19.0", "synced": true },
    { "version": "3.18.0", "synced": true }
  ],
  "sourceScanFindings": [
    {
      "vulnerabilityID": "CVE-2024-12345",
      "pkgName": "some-dep",
      "installedVersion": "1.0.0",
      "fixedVersion": "1.0.1",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "title": "Example vulnerability"
    }
  ],
  "binaryScanFindings": {
    "linux/amd64": []
  },
  "readmeContent": "# terraform-aws-vpc\n\nTerraform module..."
}

readmeContent is the decoded (plain markdown) README for the module's latest version. It is only present for module resources, and only when a README could be resolved — see VersionStatus.readmeConfigMapRef. The field is omitted for providers and for modules with no resolvable README.

skill and agent resources do not return readmeContent. They return the definition file of the latest version instead:

  • definitionContent is the decoded definition file (SKILL.md or the agent file). It is read from VersionStatus.definitionConfigMapRef.
  • definitionFileName is the source file name, such as SKILL.md or code-reviewer.agent.md.
  • agentMetadata is the frontmatter of the latest version. jevAssessment is the Jev result for the newest Version that Jev assessed, when one exists. That Version can be blocked or Rejected, so a Skill with no servable Version still shows its Jev result. jevThresholds is the source's jevPolicy.
  • sourceRef, sourceCommit, and sourcePath describe the source. sourceRef is set only for branch sources, and sourceCommit is set only when sourceRef is set. sourceCommit is the commit of the latest version.

docs.title: List Resource Versions
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/versions

Returns a paginated, filtered list of versions for a single resource. Used by the OpenDepot Workshop detail page to populate the versions table. Authentication follows the same rules as the other browse endpoints.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the resource kind module, provider, skill, or agent name Resource name

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description page int 1 Page number (1-based) page_size int 20 Items per page (max 100) q string — Case-insensitive substring filter on the version string synced string — true = healthy versions only, false = failed or error versions only; omit for all os string — Exact OS filter (case-insensitive); providers only arch string — Exact architecture filter (case-insensitive); providers only

Response:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "version": "3.19.0",
      "synced": true,
      "scanCounts": { "critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 0, "unknown": 0, "exempted": 0 },
      "downloadCount": 1243,
      "lastDownloadedAt": "2026-05-25T14:32:00Z",
      "archiveSizeBytes": 2097152
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": 42,
  "page": 1,
  "pageSize": 20,
  "availableOS": ["darwin", "linux", "windows"],
  "availableArch": ["amd64", "arm64"]
}

availableOS and availableArch are populated from the full (pre-filter) version set so filter dropdowns remain populated while a filter is active. Both fields are omitted for modules; they are only present for providers. Versions are sorted newest-first.

downloadCount and lastDownloadedAt are omitted when no downloads have been recorded. archiveSizeBytes is omitted when VersionStatus.archiveSizeBytes has not been set by the version controller.

For skill and agent resources, the list includes every Version that has a version. It also includes branch Versions that Jev blocked or that have the Rejected phase, even though they have no version. Pending and Held branch Versions without a version are not listed. Each item has these additional fields:

Field Description commit The commit SHA of the Version. Uses VersionStatus.sourceCommit and falls back to VersionSpec.sourceCommit. Omitted when neither is set. branchPhase VersionStatus.branchPhase: Pending, Held, Assigned, or Rejected. Omitted for tag-sourced Versions. blocked true when Jev blocked the Version. Omitted otherwise. blockReasons The Jev block reasons. Only set when blocked is true.

fileName, checksum, and archiveSizeBytes are omitted for a Skill or Agent Version that is not servable, such as one that is unsynced or blocked.

docs.title: Resource Scan Findings
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/scan-findings

Returns scan findings for one resource. ?version= selects the scanned version. Without it, the most recently scanned version is returned. A leading v and surrounding whitespace are stripped, so v1.2.3, 1.2.3, and 1.2.3 match. Authentication follows the other browse endpoints.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Description namespace Kubernetes namespace of the resource kind module or provider name Resource name

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description version string Selects the source scan entry for this exact version. Applies to both modules and providers. Leading v and surrounding whitespace are stripped automatically. Omit to return findings from the latest scanned version. binaryVersion string Providers only. Selects the binary scan entries for this exact version. When omitted, binary findings from the latest scanned version per platform are returned. Leading v is stripped automatically.

Response (BrowseScanFindings):

{
  "sourceScanFindings": [
    {
      "vulnerabilityID": "CVE-2024-12345",
      "pkgName": "some-dep",
      "installedVersion": "1.0.0",
      "fixedVersion": "1.0.1",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "title": "Example vulnerability"
    }
  ],
  "binaryScanFindings": {
    "linux/amd64": [],
    "darwin/arm64": []
  },
  "selectedVersion": "3.2.3",
  "scannedVersions": ["3.2.3", "3.2.0"],
  "binaryVersions": ["3.2.3", "3.2.0"]
}

sourceScanFindings contains IaC (module) or go.mod (provider) vulnerability findings. binaryScanFindings is a map of os/arch → findings; it is only populated for providers. Both fields are omitted when empty.

selectedVersion is the version whose source findings are returned. scannedVersions lists every version with source scan results, sorted by semver descending. The UI uses it for the source scan version selector. binaryVersions is the equivalent list for binary scans and appears only for providers. All three fields are omitted when no scan results exist.

This endpoint is used by the OpenDepot Workshop refresh button to re-fetch findings without a full page reload.

docs.title: Module Contract
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/contract

Returns the Assembly Line contract for a module version. The contract is the input schema that the Assembly Line canvas uses to render module inputs. It is derived when the Version is synced. This endpoint is available whether or not Assembly Line is enabled.

Only module is supported. Requests for provider return 400.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description version string Exact module version. Omit to use the module's latest version.

Responses:

Status Description 200 The contract JSON, served as application/json. 400 The resource is not a module. 404 The resource or version was not found, or no contract has been derived for it. An unavailable contract returns {"error": "contract_unavailable", "message": "...", "version": "..."}.

The decompressed payload is capped at 32 MiB.

docs.title: Provider Configuration Schema
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/resources/{namespace}/provider/{name}/provider-schema

Returns the configuration schema for a provider version, extracted from the provider binary. Assembly Line must be enabled with --assembly-enabled (server.assembly.enabled in the chart). When it is disabled, the route is not registered and the request returns 404.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description version string Exact provider version. Omit to use the provider's latest version.

Response (providerConfigurationSchemaResponse):

{
  "namespace": "opendepot",
  "name": "example",
  "providerNamespace": "hashicorp",
  "providerName": "aws",
  "version": "5.0.0",
  "schemaVersion": "1",
  "configuration": {}
}

The decompressed payload is capped at 128 MiB.

docs.title: Assembly Line Export
docs.text:
POST /opendepot/ui/v1/assembly/export

Validates an Assembly Line canvas and packages it as a root module. This endpoint is registered only when Assembly Line is enabled. Authentication follows the browse rules. The export needs a bearer token, so OpenTofu can download the artifacts that the generated module references.

Request Body (assembly.export.v1):

{
  "schemaVersion": "assembly.export.v1",
  "variables": [],
  "modules": [],
  "providers": []
}
Field Type Required Description schemaVersion string Yes Must be assembly.export.v1. variables array Yes Root module input variables. modules array Yes Module nodes from the canvas. providers array No Provider nodes from the canvas.

The request body is limited to 2 MiB by default (--assembly-max-request-bytes). The total node count across variables, modules, and providers is limited to 100 by default (--assembly-max-nodes). Unknown fields and trailing data after the JSON object are rejected.

Response formats:

The format depends on the Accept header.

  • Default: 200 OK with application/zip and Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="assembly-line.zip". The archive is the root module.
  • Accept: application/x-ndjson: 200 OK with a stream of newline-delimited JSON events. The stream emits started, then zero or more output events, then either complete or error.
Event type Fields Description started phase Validation or packaging began. output phase, output Progress output from tofu init and validation. complete archive The base64-encoded ZIP archive. error error An error object with error and message fields.

Errors:

Errors use the ErrorResponse shape: {"error": "<code>", "message": "...", "diagnostics": [], "output": "..."}. The diagnostics and output fields appear only when they apply.

Status error code Description 400 invalid_request The body is not valid JSON, contains unknown fields, or has trailing data. 413 too_many_nodes The canvas exceeds the node limit. 413 request_too_large The body exceeds the request size limit. 422 invalid_canvas The canvas failed validation. diagnostics lists the problems. 500 internal_error The export failed on the server. 500 streaming_unavailable The client requested NDJSON but the response writer cannot stream.

docs.title: List Depots
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/depots

Returns a flat list of all visible Depot resources with their storage backend, polling interval, and managed resource counts.

Visibility: public depots are always included. Non-public depots are included when the server is in anonymous-auth mode or when the caller has a matching GroupBinding. An optional ?namespace= query parameter filters results to a single namespace.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description namespace string Filter by namespace

Response:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "namespace": "opendepot-system",
      "name": "platform-depot",
      "modules": ["terraform-aws-vpc", "terraform-aws-s3-bucket"],
      "providers": ["aws"],
      "pollingIntervalMinutes": 30,
      "storageBackend": "s3"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Depot Relationship Graph
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/depots/graph

Returns a graph of all visible Depot, Module, Provider, Skill, and Agent resources with directed edges connecting each depot to its managed modules, providers, skills, and agents. Each node carries only its latestVersion; the Depots page loads each resource's versions from the Resource Detail endpoint to draw version nodes. Used by the Depots page in OpenDepot Workshop to render the interactive relationship diagram.

Visibility: same rules as List Depots.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description namespace string Filter the graph to a single namespace

docs.title: Registry Stats
docs.text:
GET /opendepot/ui/v1/stats

Returns aggregate registry statistics as JSON. All counts are scoped to the resources visible to the caller (same visibility rules as the other browse endpoints).

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description namespace string Scope statistics to a single namespace. Omit for all accessible namespaces.

Response:

{
  "totalModules": 12,
  "modulesSynced": 11,
  "totalProviders": 3,
  "providersSynced": 3,
  "totalSkills": 14,
  "skillsSynced": 12,
  "totalAgents": 10,
  "agentsSynced": 9,
  "totalVersions": 87,
  "versionsSynced": 82,
  "totalStorageBytes": 5368709120,
  "totalDownloads": 24601,
  "syncHealth": {
    "syncedVersions": 82,
    "unsyncedVersions": 3,
    "failedVersions": 2
  },
  "securityPosture": {
    "critical": 0,
    "high": 4,
    "medium": 11,
    "low": 7,
    "unknown": 1,
    "totalAffectedResources": 6
  },
  "jev": {
    "assessedVersions": 12,
    "blockedVersions": 1,
    "needsReviewVersions": 2,
    "exemptedVersions": 0,
    "failedVersions": 0,
    "assessedChunks": 348,
    "inputTokens": 1893204,
    "riskLevels": {
      "minimal": 5,
      "low": 4,
      "moderate": 2,
      "high": 1,
      "critical": 0
    }
  },
  "storageDistribution": [
    { "backend": "s3", "count": 10 },
    { "backend": "filesystem", "count": 5 }
  ],
  "mostDownloaded": {
    "modules": [
      {
        "namespace": "opendepot-system",
        "kind": "module",
        "name": "terraform-aws-vpc",
        "version": "3.19.0",
        "downloadCount": 4821,
        "lastDownloadedAt": "2026-05-25T14:32:00Z"

    "providers": [],
    "skills": [],
    "agents": []
