}

totalStorageBytes is the sum of VersionStatus.archiveSizeBytes across all visible versions; it is 0 when no archive sizes have been recorded. totalDownloads and mostDownloaded are queried from Prometheus over the configured lookback window; both are 0 / empty until a matching metric has been scraped. Skill and Agent downloads are included in totalDownloads. Download counts are cross-referenced against the caller's visibility set — private resource names do not appear in mostDownloaded for unauthenticated callers.

mostDownloaded is split by kind so each list ranks only its own resources. Each list holds up to 10 resources, ranked by total downloads across all versions. Each entry reports the resource's most-downloaded version, with ties broken by the higher version. Resources with zero downloads are omitted, so an empty list means no visible downloads for that kind.

docs.title: Kubernetes Resource Types
docs.text: All resources are in the opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1 group. Fields marked controller-managed are written by OpenDepot, not by you.

docs.title: Module
docs.text: Field Type Description spec.moduleConfig ModuleConfig Required. Settings for the module and for each Version it creates. spec.versions []ModuleVersion Required. Versions to sync. A leading v is trimmed. spec.forceSync bool Forces a re-sync. The controller resets it to false. Default false. status.latestVersion string Controller-managed. Latest available version. status.synced bool Controller-managed. Whether the module reached its desired state. status.syncStatus string Controller-managed. Reconciliation status. status.fileName string Controller-managed. Generated archive file name. status.moduleVersionRefs map[string]ModuleVersion Controller-managed. Versions the controller created.

docs.title: ModuleConfig
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Name used when naming Version resources. Defaults to the Module resource name. provider string Main OpenTofu provider the module requires (for example, aws). repoOwner string Owner of the GitHub source repository. repoUrl string Full URL of the GitHub source repository. fileFormat string zip produces .zip archives. Any other value produces .tar.gz. Inherited from global.moduleConfig when unset in a Depot. immutable bool When true, the archive checksum must match the stored checksumSHA256 on every sync. Inherited from global.moduleConfig when unset in a Depot. versionConstraints string Comma-separated constraints such as >= 1.0.0, < 2.0.0. Used only by the Depot controller. versionHistoryLimit int Keeps the newest N versions. The controller trims spec.versions to the N highest semantic versions and deletes the removed Version resources. Unset, <= 0, or greater than the number of versions keeps all versions. Falls back to spec.global.moduleConfig.versionHistoryLimit, then spec.global.versionHistoryLimit. githubClientConfig GithubClientConfig GitHub client settings. See GithubClientConfig. storageConfig StorageConfig Storage backend for the archives. See StorageConfig.

docs.title: ModuleVersion
docs.text:
Items in spec.versions and status.moduleVersionRefs.

Field Type Description version string Semantic version to sync. A leading v is trimmed. name string Controller-managed. Name of the generated Version resource. fileName string Controller-managed. Archive file name. synced bool Controller-managed. Whether the Version has synced.

docs.title: Provider
docs.text: Field Type Description spec.providerConfig ProviderConfig Required. Settings for the provider and for each Version it creates. spec.versions []ProviderVersion Required. Versions to sync. A leading v is trimmed. spec.forceSync bool Forces a re-sync. The controller resets it to false. Default false. status.latestVersion string Controller-managed. Latest available version. status.synced bool Controller-managed. Whether the provider reached its desired state. status.syncStatus string Controller-managed. Reconciliation status. status.resolvedSourceRepository string Controller-managed. See ProviderStatus fields.

docs.title: ProviderConfig
docs.text:
The namespace, upstreamRegistry, and sourceRepository fields are described in ProviderConfig fields.

Field Type Description name string Provider name. Defaults to the Provider resource name. operatingSystems []string Operating systems the provider supports, used as the os constraint. architectures []string Architectures the provider supports, used as the arch constraint. githubClientConfig GithubClientConfig GitHub client settings for source scanning. Inherited from global.providerConfig, then global.githubClientConfig, when unset in a Depot. See GithubClientConfig. storageConfig StorageConfig Storage backend for the binaries. See StorageConfig. versionHistoryLimit int Keeps the newest N versions. The controller trims spec.versions to the N highest semantic versions and deletes the removed Version resources. Unset, <= 0, or greater than the number of versions keeps all versions. Falls back to spec.global.providerConfig.versionHistoryLimit, then spec.global.versionHistoryLimit. versionConstraints string Comma-separated constraints such as ~> 1.0.0. Used only by the Depot controller.

docs.title: ProviderVersion
docs.text:
Items in spec.versions.

Field Type Description version string Semantic version to sync. A leading v is trimmed. architecture string Architecture for this provider version. operatingSystem string Operating system for this provider version. name string Controller-managed. Provider name. synced bool Controller-managed. Whether the Version has synced.

docs.title: Version
docs.text:
Version resources are created by the Module and Provider controllers. Edit the parent resource instead of creating them by hand.

Field Type Description spec.type string Required. Module or Provider. spec.version string Required. Semantic version. spec.architecture string Provider architecture. spec.operatingSystem string Provider operating system. spec.fileName string Archive file name. Controller-managed. spec.forceSync bool Forces this version to re-sync. spec.moduleConfigRef ModuleConfig Copy of the parent module's config. Set by the Module controller. spec.providerConfigRef ProviderConfig Copy of the parent provider's config. Set by the Provider controller. status VersionStatus Sync state, checksum, and scan results. See VersionStatus fields.

docs.title: Depot
docs.text: Field Type Description spec.global GlobalConfig Defaults for the entries the Depot manages. Requires storageConfig. See GlobalConfig. spec.moduleConfigs []ModuleConfig Modules to create and manage. spec.providerConfigs []ProviderConfig Providers to create and manage. spec.pollingIntervalMinutes int Minutes between checks for new versions. Unset or 0 disables periodic polling. status.modules []string Controller-managed. Names of the Module resources the Depot manages. status.providers []string Controller-managed. Names of the Provider resources the Depot manages.

docs.title: GlobalConfig
docs.text:
spec.global sets defaults for each entry that does not set its own value. Identity fields such as name, sourceRepository, and repoOwner are not allowed in a global block. Set them on each entry.

Field Type Description storageConfig StorageConfig Required. Storage backend for each module and provider that does not set its own. See StorageConfig. githubClientConfig GithubClientConfig GitHub client settings for each module, provider, skill, and agent that does not set its own. See GithubClientConfig. versionHistoryLimit int Keeps the newest N versions of each module and provider that does not set its own. Minimum 0. moduleConfig ModuleDefaults Defaults for moduleConfigs entries. See ModuleDefaults below. providerConfig ProviderDefaults Defaults for providerConfigs entries. See ProviderDefaults below.

Precedence

An entry value always wins. The kind-level block (moduleConfig or providerConfig) is checked next, then the top-level global block. A list inherits only when it is empty. A pointer inherits only when it is nil, so an explicit 0 or an explicit githubClientConfig on an entry stops inheritance.

Setting Applies to Order versionHistoryLimit Modules, providers Entry, moduleConfig or providerConfig, global storageConfig Modules, providers Entry, moduleConfig or providerConfig, global githubClientConfig Modules, providers Entry, moduleConfig or providerConfig, global fileFormat Modules Entry, moduleConfig immutable Modules Entry, moduleConfig operatingSystems Providers Entry, providerConfig architectures Providers Entry, providerConfig

ModuleDefaults (global.moduleConfig)

Field Type Description fileFormat string Archive format for entries that do not set one. See ModuleConfig. immutable bool Checksum enforcement for entries that do not set one. See ModuleConfig. githubClientConfig GithubClientConfig Used when the entry does not set one. Falls back to global.githubClientConfig. storageConfig StorageConfig Used when the entry does not set one. Falls back to global.storageConfig. versionHistoryLimit int Used when the entry does not set one. Minimum 0. Falls back to global.versionHistoryLimit.

ProviderDefaults (global.providerConfig)

Field Type Description operatingSystems []string Used when the entry lists none. architectures []string Used when the entry lists none. githubClientConfig GithubClientConfig Used when the entry does not set one. Falls back to global.githubClientConfig. storageConfig StorageConfig Used when the entry does not set one. Falls back to global.storageConfig. versionHistoryLimit int Used when the entry does not set one. Minimum 0. Falls back to global.versionHistoryLimit.

global.moduleConfig does not accept name, namespace, sourceRepository, versionConstraints, provider, repoOwner, or repoUrl. global.providerConfig does not accept the same identity fields, and it does not accept upstreamRegistry. Set upstreamRegistry on each providerConfigs entry. The API server removes unknown fields when it decodes a Depot. See Upgrading.

docs.title: GithubClientConfig
docs.text: Field Type Description useAuthenticatedClient bool Authenticates GitHub requests with a GitHub App to avoid rate limits. Requires a Secret named opendepot-github-application-secret in the resource's namespace with githubAppID, githubInstallID, and a base64 encoded githubPrivateKey.

docs.title: StorageConfig
docs.text:
Each field selects a storage backend. presign configures pre-signed downloads.

Field Type Description s3 AmazonS3Config Amazon S3 bucket. azureStorage AzureStorageConfig Azure Storage account. gcs GoogleCloudStorageConfig Google Cloud Storage bucket. fileSystem FileSystemConfig Local filesystem path. presign PresignConfig Pre-signed download URLs. See PresignConfig fields.

AmazonS3Config

Field Type Description bucket string Required. Bucket name. region string Required. AWS region of the bucket. key string Key prefix (for example, my/bucket/prefix). The file name is generated.

AzureStorageConfig

Field Type Description accountName string Required. Storage account name. accountUrl string Required. Storage account URL. subscriptionID string Required. Subscription that contains the account. resourceGroup string Required. Resource group that contains the account.

GoogleCloudStorageConfig

Field Type Description bucket string Required. Bucket name.

FileSystemConfig

Field Type Description directoryPath string Directory where archives are stored.

docs.title: SecurityFinding
docs.text:
Represents a single vulnerability finding from a Trivy scan.

Field Type Description vulnerabilityID string CVE or GHSA identifier for the vulnerability, or a Trivy rule ID (e.g. AWS-0057) for module IaC findings pkgName string Name of the package containing the vulnerability installedVersion string Version of the package currently in use fixedVersion string Minimum version that resolves the vulnerability, if known severity string CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or UNKNOWN title string Short description of the vulnerability exempted bool Whether a ScanPolicy exempted this finding from blocking reconciliation. Exempted findings are still reported so they remain visible and auditable; only the per-severity counters, highestSeverity, and totalAffectedResources treat them differently. Omitted when false. exemptionReason string The reason recorded on the ScanExemption that covered this finding. Only set when exempted is true. exemptedBy string The name of the ScanPolicy that exempted this finding. Only set when exempted is true.

docs.title: BinaryScan
docs.text:
Holds Trivy binary scan (trivy rootfs) results for a specific provider artifact. Stored in Version.status.binaryScan. Each OS/architecture binary is scanned independently because Go stdlib versions and runtime dependencies may differ between compiled artifacts.

Note

Trivy requires the execute bit to be set on the binary for gobinary detection. Provider binaries are written with 0500 permissions before scanning; binaries without execute permission are silently skipped by Trivy and findings will be empty.

Field Type Description scannedAt string RFC3339 timestamp at which the binary scan completed findings []SecurityFinding Vulnerabilities found in the compiled provider binary

docs.title: SourceScan
docs.text:
Holds Trivy source scan results. Used for both provider go.mod dependency scans and module IaC (HCL filesystem) scans. Stored in Version.status.sourceScan for every Version resource when scanning is enabled.

Field Type Description scannedAt string RFC3339 timestamp at which the scan completed findings []SecurityFinding Findings produced by the scan. For provider Version resources these are go.mod dependency vulnerabilities (CVE identifiers). For module Version resources these are HCL misconfigurations (vulnerabilityID contains a Trivy rule ID such as AWS-0057).

docs.title: ScanPolicy
docs.text:
ScanPolicy is a namespaced resource that lets you exempt specific scan findings, or override the severity threshold that blocks reconciliation, for a subset of Version resources without touching the cluster-wide scanning.blockOnCritical/scanning.blockOnHigh flags. See Policy Enforcement for the full semantics — precedence, exact-match rules, RBAC boundary, and information-disclosure considerations.

The server also exposes the optional policy-management API for UI clients:

Method Path Behavior GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace} Lists policies in the namespace. GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/catalog Lists authorized policy namespaces and currently onboarded Module/Provider targets. GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Gets one policy. GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/capabilities Returns writesEnabled, canRead, canWrite, supported methods, and supportsPreview. POST /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/preview Validates a ScanPolicy JSON object without persisting it; returns { "valid": true, "policy": ... }. POST /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace} Creates a policy from a JSON ScanPolicy object. PUT /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Replaces a policy. Requires If-Match and matching metadata.resourceVersion; missing preconditions return 428, stale versions return 409 Conflict. DELETE /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/{namespace}/{name} Deletes a policy. Requires If-Match; missing preconditions return 428, stale versions return 409 Conflict.

POST, PUT, and DELETE return 404 until server.policyManagement.enabled is true. Anonymous callers can read policies but get 403 on mutations. In OIDC mode, access is default-deny and uses the effective SecurityGroupBinding. GroupBinding and Registry visibility do not grant policy access. Unauthorized namespace or item reads return 404. A disallowed mutation in an authorized namespace returns 403. Kubeconfig and bearer-token requests use Kubernetes RBAC. Status codes: 400 validation, 401 authentication, 403 authorization, 409 Kubernetes conflict.

The server logs each successful create, update, and delete with the operation, namespace, policy name, and authenticated subject. Kubernetes audit logging remains the authoritative record of the underlying CRD writes.

The server logs every successful create, update, and delete with the operation, namespace, policy name, and subject. For a durable record of the CRD write, configure the Kubernetes API server audit policy. UI access and a successful preview do not authorize writes.

ScanPolicySpec fields:

Field Type Description priority int The precedence of this policy. When more than one ScanPolicy matches a Version, the policy with the highest priority wins outright and supplies both the severity threshold and the exemption set; lower priority policies are ignored entirely rather than merged. Ties are broken by the oldest creation timestamp, then by name ascending. Default: 0 selector metav1.LabelSelector Matched against the labels of the Version resources this policy applies to. A Version matches when the selector matches it or when any entry in targetRefs matches it. When both selector and targetRefs are omitted, the policy applies to every Version in its namespace. targetRefs []ScanPolicyTargetRef An explicit list of Module or Provider resources this policy applies to. severityThreshold string The minimum severity that blocks reconciliation for the matched Versions: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or NONE. Overrides the version controller's --scan-block-on-critical/--scan-block-on-high flags for matched Versions. NONE disables blocking entirely for the match. When omitted, the controller flags remain in effect as the baseline. exemptions []ScanExemption The findings that must not block reconciliation for the matched Versions. jevExemptions []JevExemption The Jev blocks that must not block reconciliation for the matched Versions. Each entry matches one exact archive by its contentDigest. Lists are keyed by contentDigest. See JevExemption fields.

ScanPolicyStatus fields:

Field Type Description matchedVersions int The number of Version resources in this namespace currently matched by this policy. activeExemptions int The number of exemptions currently in effect. expiredExemptions int The number of exemptions whose expires has passed and no longer apply. activeJevExemptions int The number of Jev exemptions currently in effect. Entries without an expires count as active. Omitted when 0. expiredJevExemptions int The number of Jev exemptions whose expires has passed and no longer apply. Omitted when 0. supersededBy string The name of the higher priority ScanPolicy that shadows this policy for every Version it matches. Empty when this policy wins for at least one Version, or when it matches no Versions at all. conditions []metav1.Condition Observed conditions. Reasons: Active, NoMatchingVersions, Superseded, InvalidSelector.

docs.title: ScanPolicyTargetRef
docs.text:
Identifies a Module or Provider resource a ScanPolicy applies to.

Field Type Description kind string Module or Provider. name string The name of the Module or Provider resource. Matching is exact; the single literal * matches every resource of the given kind in the namespace. versions string An optional hashicorp/go-version constraint string, e.g. "1.2.1", ">= 1.0.0, < 2.0.0", or "~> 1.0.0". Constraints use AND semantics. When omitted, matches every version of the resource.

docs.title: ScanExemption
docs.text:
Declares a set of scan findings that must not block reconciliation. A finding is exempted when it matches every populated field of the exemption. All list fields below support only exact matches or the single literal "*" — there is no glob or regex support.

Field Type Description vulnerabilityIDs []string Vulnerability or misconfiguration identifiers this exemption covers, e.g. CVE-2024-1234 or AWS-0057. ["*"] matches every identifier. Omitted covers every identifier. pkgNames []string Package names this exemption covers, e.g. stdlib or golang.org/x/net. ["*"] matches every package. Omitted covers every package. scanTypes []string Scan types this exemption applies to: binary, source, module. Omitted covers every scan type. severities []string Severities this exemption covers. Matching is exact and case-insensitive. ["*"] matches every severity. Omitted covers every severity. reason string Required. Justification for the exemption, so every exemption remains auditable. Must be non-empty. expires string RFC3339 timestamp at which this exemption stops applying. Once passed, the covered findings block again with no user action required. Omitted means the exemption never expires.

Preview accepts the same object as create and update, and returns the normalized policy without writing it. It rejects unknown JSON fields, invalid DNS names, unsupported thresholds or target kinds, missing exemption reasons, and a namespace that differs from the URL. Preview does not reserve a name or check authorization for a later write.

docs.title: JevExemption fields
docs.text:
Declares a Jev exemption. An entry clears every Jev block reason for one exact archive. Only the winning ScanPolicy for a Version supplies its jevExemptions. See Jev exemptions with ScanPolicy.

Field Type Description contentDigest string Required. The lowercase hex SHA-256 of the Version archive, copied from status.jevAssessment.contentDigest. Must match ^[0-9a-f]{64}$. The exemption applies only while the archive has this digest. reason string Required. Justification for the exemption, so every exemption remains auditable. Must be non-empty. expires string RFC3339 timestamp at which this exemption stops applying. Once passed, the Version blocks again. Omitted means the exemption never expires and stays valid until the archive content changes.

The server rejects a contentDigest that is not 64 lowercase hex characters, a duplicate contentDigest in one policy, and a blank reason.

docs.title: ProviderConfig fields
docs.text: Field Type Description namespace string The organisation namespace in the upstream registry (e.g. hashicorp, integrations, DataDog). Defaults to hashicorp. Used for binary download and source repository lookup. Existing Provider resources without this field continue to work unchanged. upstreamRegistry string The canonical registry used to discover and download this provider. Controls upstream version discovery, archive acquisition, and the canonical provider identity exposed via the Network Mirror Protocol and UI snippets. Allowed values: registry.opentofu.org, registry.terraform.io. Defaults to registry.opentofu.org when omitted. Providers from different origins with the same namespace/type should be placed in separate Kubernetes namespaces to avoid Version resource-name collisions. See Consuming Providers for examples. sourceRepository string Full GitHub URL of the provider's source repository (e.g. https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws). When omitted for an OpenTofu Registry provider, OpenDepot queries api.opentofu.org and falls back to https://github.com/{namespace}/terraform-provider-{name} if the lookup fails. Terraform Registry providers use the fallback directly because that registry does not expose equivalent source metadata. Set this field to override an incorrect or unavailable result.

docs.title: ReadmeConfigMapRef
docs.text:
References the ConfigMap and data key holding a module Version's base64 encoded README content. Stored in Version.status.readmeConfigMapRef. The ConfigMap is owned by the Version resource (via ownerReferences), so it is garbage collected automatically when the Version is deleted.

This reference applies to module Version resources only. Skill and Agent definitions do not fill README content. A Skill or Agent Version does not use readmeConfigMapRef, and the version controller clears any existing reference on it. Their definition files are stored in DefinitionConfigMapRef instead.

Field Type Description name string Name of the ConfigMap holding the README content. key string Key within the ConfigMap's data holding the base64 encoded README content.

docs.title: DefinitionConfigMapRef
docs.text:
References the ConfigMap and data key holding a Skill or Agent Version's base64 encoded definition file. Stored in Version.status.definitionConfigMapRef. The ConfigMap is owned by the Version resource (via ownerReferences), so it is garbage collected automatically when the Version is deleted. The OpenDepot UI shows the file as SKILL.md for skills and AGENT.md for agents.

Field Type Description name string Name of the ConfigMap holding the definition file. key string Key within the ConfigMap's data holding the base64 encoded definition file. fileName string Name of the source entry file, such as SKILL.md, code-reviewer.agent.md, or code-reviewer.md. Maximum 255 characters.

The base64 encoded definition must be at most 1,000,000 bytes. This keeps the ConfigMap below the 1 MiB Kubernetes object limit. A larger definition is not synced. The Version gets synced: false, and syncStatus records the file name, its size, the encoded size, and the limit. The Version stays unsynced until the definition changes.

docs.title: VersionStatus fields
docs.text: Field Type Description binaryScan BinaryScan Binary vulnerability scan result for this specific provider artifact. Populated only for provider Version resources when scanning is enabled. sourceScan SourceScan Scan result for this version. Contains IaC misconfigurations for module Version resources and go.mod dependency vulnerabilities for provider Version resources. Populated when scanning is enabled. archiveSizeBytes int64 Compressed archive size in bytes stored in the backend. Set automatically by the version controller after a successful upload. Omitted until the archive has been synced. readmeConfigMapRef ReadmeConfigMapRef Reference to the ConfigMap holding this version's base64 encoded README content. Only populated for module Version resources when a README could be resolved from GitHub or the module archive. See Module READMEs. definitionConfigMapRef DefinitionConfigMapRef Reference to the ConfigMap holding this version's base64 encoded definition file. Only populated for Skill and Agent Version resources. See DefinitionConfigMapRef. jevAssessment JevAssessment The Jev assessment of this Version. Only populated when Jev is enabled and the source sets jevSecretRef. See JevAssessment fields.

docs.title: ProviderStatus fields
docs.text: Field Type Description resolvedSourceRepository string The VCS source URL resolved by the Version controller. Set automatically on first scan; spec.providerConfig.sourceRepository takes precedence if set. See Provider Source Repository Resolution.

docs.title: Branch source fields
docs.text:
These fields apply to AgentSourceConfig, which is used by Depot skillConfigs and agentConfigs, by Skill.spec, Agent.spec, and by Version.spec.agentSourceRef. Branch sourcing is enabled only when the chart sets branchSourcing.enabled: true. See Branch sourcing.

Field Type Description ref string A Git branch to follow instead of tags. Must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._+/-]+$ and is validated in the controller. Mutually exclusive with versionConstraints and tagPrefix. branchPolicy BranchPolicy Branch-mode thresholds. Requires ref. Applies to branch sources only.

The following rules are enforced by CEL on the type:

  • ref and versionConstraints are mutually exclusive: "ref and versionConstraints are mutually exclusive".
  • tagPrefix is not used with ref: "tagPrefix is not used with ref".
  • branchPolicy requires ref: "branchPolicy requires ref".

versionConstraints applies to tag mode only.

docs.title: BranchPolicy fields
docs.text:
BranchPolicy classifies each new commit and never blocks a Version. Defaults apply when a field or the whole policy is omitted.

Field Type Default Description minVersionInterval Duration 10m The minimum time between Versions for a source. 0s disables the interval. Negative values are rejected. majorThreshold float64 0.5 MAJOR when the major-change probability is at least this value. Between 0 and 1. minorThreshold float64 0.5 MINOR when the major-change probability plus the minor-change probability is at least this value. Between 0 and 1. minConfidence float64 0.5 A Version whose confidence is below this value is marked needsReview. Informational only. Between 0 and 1.

For the classification rules, see Version bump classification.

docs.title: SkillVersion and AgentVersion fields
docs.text:
These types are used by spec.versions and status.versionRefs on the Skill and Agent resources.

Field Type Description name string The name of the Version resource. version string The semver for the entry. Empty for a branch entry until it is assigned. commit string The 40-character commit SHA for a branch entry. Must match ^[0-9a-f]{40}$. discoveredAt Time When the commit was discovered. Used to order branch entries. state string Pending, Assigned, or Rejected. Set in the spec for branch entries.

docs.title: VersionSpec branch fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description sourceCommit string The 40-character commit SHA the Version is pinned to. Must match ^[0-9a-f]{40}$. Immutable once set.

For a branch Version, version is empty until the version controller assigns a semver, and then it cannot change. A Version without a version must set sourceCommit, and sourceCommit requires agentSourceRef.ref.

docs.title: VersionStatus branch fields
docs.text: Field Type Description sourceCommit string The commit SHA that was actually downloaded. branchPhase string Pending, Held, Assigned, or Rejected. bumpAssessment BumpAssessment The bump decision for this Version. Never contains the Jev token or prompt content.

docs.title: BumpAssessment fields
docs.text: Field Type Description commit string The commit this assessment is for. previousCommit string The commit of the previous Version. previousVersion string The semver of the previous Version. category string Major, Minor, or Patch. source string Initial, Default, Jev, Withheld, or Manual. reason string The reason for the decision. model string The Jev model that produced the answer, when Jev was used. evaluatedAt string RFC3339 time of the decision. majorProbability, minorProbability, patchProbability float64 Optional. The Jev probabilities for each bump size. confidence float64 Optional. The Jev confidence. needsReview bool Set when the confidence is below minConfidence. Informational only. attempts int The number of Jev attempts. error string The redacted error message, when a Jev call failed.

docs.title: JevPolicy fields
docs.text:
jevPolicy is set on the same sources as jevSecretRef. Each threshold is optional. A threshold that is not set never blocks a Version. Each threshold is checked against every part of the content, and a breach in any part blocks the Version. See Thresholds.

Field Type Description minSafeProbability float64 Blocks when the safe probability is below this value. maxInjectionProbability float64 Blocks when the prompt injection probability is above this value. maxExfiltrationProbability float64 Blocks when the data exfiltration probability is above this value. maxDestructiveProbability float64 Blocks when the destructive action probability is above this value. maxHiddenInstructionsProbability float64 Blocks when the hidden instructions probability is above this value. maxScopeMismatchProbability float64 Blocks when the scope mismatch probability is above this value. maxRemoteExecutionProbability float64 Blocks when the remote execution probability is above this value. maxRiskScore float64 Blocks when the risk score is above this value. minConfidence float64 Blocks when the risk confidence is below this value, and sets needsReview.

docs.title: JevAssessment fields
docs.text:
jevAssessment is set on VersionStatus. It is combined from the scored parts. See How content is split.

Field Type Description evaluatedAt string The time at which the assessment was evaluated. contentDigest string Optional. The lowercase hex SHA-256 of the archive that Jev assessed. It equals the hex form of status.checksum. Used as the jevExemptions key. A legacy assessment without a digest cannot match an exemption until one forceSync. model string Optional. The Jev model that produced the assessment. safeProbability float64 Optional. The lowest part value. injectionProbability, exfiltrationProbability, destructiveProbability, hiddenInstructionsProbability, scopeMismatchProbability, remoteExecutionProbability float64 Optional. The highest part value for each probability. riskScore float64 Optional. The highest part value. riskLevel string Optional. The worst part value. One of Minimal, Low, Moderate, High, or Critical. riskConfidence float64 Optional. The lowest part value. needsReview bool Set when a part's risk confidence is below minConfidence, or when the risk level is Critical on a fully scored assessment. An exemption does not change it, but the Workshop Needs review queue and the Stats Needs review count hide the Version while the exemption is active. blocked bool Whether Jev blocks the Version: a threshold, a Critical risk level, a part below minConfidence, content Jev could not read, Jev disabled on the controller, or an assessment that could not complete. false when a matching jevExemptions entry cleared every block reason. blockReasons []string Optional. The Jev block reasons. When the assessment is exempted, this lists the reasons that were cleared. The field is kept when blocked is false. exempted bool Optional. Whether a jevExemptions entry cleared the block reasons for this assessment. Omitted when false. This does not mean the Version is synced. When the Jev call failed, status.synced stays false until a Jev run completes without an error. exemptedBy string Optional. The name of the ScanPolicy whose jevExemptions entry cleared the block reasons. exemptionReason string Optional. The reason given by the jevExemptions entry that cleared the block reasons. exemptionExpires string Optional. The expires of the jevExemptions entry that cleared the block reasons. Omitted when the entry never expires. error string Optional. A redacted error that prevented the assessment from completing, or why it is incomplete. chunkCount int32 Optional. The planned number of parts. Above 16, no Jev call is made and the Version is blocked. assessedChunks int32 Optional. The number of part entries that Jev scored. At most 16. chunks []JevChunkResult Optional. One entry per scored or attempted part. At most 16 entries. skippedFiles []JevSkippedFile Optional. Files that Jev could not read. Any entry blocks the Version. At most 32 entries are listed. skippedFileCount int32 Optional. The total number of skipped files. retryCount int32 Optional. The number of counted failed attempts since the last ForceSync, which resets it to 0. The count starts at 0 and rises by one for each counted failure. 401 and 403 failures are not counted. Automatic retries stop once it exceeds jevMaxRetries, which defaults to 3. See Retries.

docs.title: JevChunkResult fields
docs.text:
Each entry describes one part of a Version's content.

Field Type Description index int32 The 1-based planned part number, from 1 to 16. A halved part keeps the index of the part it came from. label string The part index plus any halving suffix, such as 3, 3a, or 3ab. At most 4 characters. files []string Optional. The paths whose content, or part of it, is in this part. The entry file is in part 1. At most 32 entries. Each path is cut to 256 bytes at a rune boundary, with no suffix. fileCount int32 The exact number of files in this part. status string Scored, Failed, TokenLimitExceeded, or NotSent. riskLevel string Optional. Set when the part is Scored. riskScore float64 Optional. Set when the part is Scored. riskConfidence float64 Optional. Set when the part is Scored. safeProbability float64 Optional. Set when the part is Scored. error string Optional. The redacted reason the part failed or was not sent. Cut to 512 bytes.

docs.title: JevSkippedFile fields
docs.text: Field Type Description path string The path of the skipped file. Cut to 256 bytes at a rune boundary, with no suffix. reason string Withheld for a file flagged for a secret, or Binary for a binary file.

docs.title: GroupBinding
docs.text:
GroupBinding is a namespaced resource that grants a group of OIDC users access to specific modules, providers, skills, and agents. The server evaluates all GroupBindings in alphabetical order by name and applies the first one whose expression matches the user's groups claim. If an expression fails to compile or evaluate, the request is denied with 403 Forbidden. Requires OIDC authentication to be enabled.

See the GroupBinding guide for usage examples.

GroupBindingSpec fields:

Field Type Required Description expression string Yes An expr-lang boolean expression evaluated against the user's groups. The evaluation environment exposes groups []string. Must return true or false. Example: '"platform-team" in groups' moduleResources []string No Glob patterns (path.Match semantics) for module names the group may access. Empty list denies access to all modules. Example: ["aws-*", "gcp-networking"] providerResources []string No Exact provider type names the group may access, or ["*"] to allow all providers. Empty list denies access to all providers. Example: ["aws", "google"] skillResources []string No Glob patterns (path.Match semantics) for skill names the group may access. Empty list denies access to all skills. Example: ["code-review-*"] agentResources []string No Glob patterns (path.Match semantics) for agent names the group may access. Empty list denies access to all agents. Example: ["release-*"]

Example manifest:

apiVersion: opendepot.defdev.io/v1alpha1
kind: GroupBinding
metadata:
  name: platform-team-binding
  namespace: opendepot-system
spec:
  expression: '"platform-team" in groups'
  moduleResources:
    - "aws-*"
    - "gcp-networking"
  providerResources:
    - "aws"
    - "google"

docs.title: SecurityGroupBinding
docs.text:
SecurityGroupBinding is a namespaced resource for ScanPolicy administration. It is independent of GroupBinding, which remains responsible for Registry and browse authorization. The server reads bindings from its configured namespace, sorts them by name, and applies the first matching expression. Invalid expressions, evaluation errors, and no matching binding deny policy access.

SecurityGroupBindingSpec fields:

Field Type Required Description expression string Yes expr-lang boolean expression evaluated against groups []string. namespaces []string No Policy namespace allow-list. Empty denies access; "*" allows all namespaces reachable by the server ServiceAccount. moduleResources []string No Allowed Module names using path.Match glob semantics. Empty denies Module targets. providerResources []string No Allowed Provider names by exact match, or "*" for all onboarded Providers. Empty denies Provider targets. namespaceWidePolicyManagement bool No Allows selector-based and empty-target policies in allowed namespaces. Defaults to false.

The policy catalog is:

GET /opendepot/ui/v1/scan-policies/catalog

It returns { "writesEnabled": bool, "items": [...] }. Each item contains namespace, canRead, canWrite, canManageNamespaceWidePolicies, and sorted modules and providers arrays whose entries contain name. The catalog contains only authorized namespaces and currently onboarded resources. It does not disclose binding expressions, patterns, or denied resources.

For OIDC policy requests, a targeted policy is authorized only when it has no selector, has at least one targetRef, and every target is allowed by the effective SecurityGroupBinding. Selectors and policies without targetRefs require namespaceWidePolicyManagement: true. The server applies the same scope check to reads, previews, creates, updates, and deletes; updates check both the persisted and proposed object.

docs.title: PresignConfig fields
docs.text:
Controls pre-signed URL generation for provider and agent downloads. Set on StorageConfig.presign. For Agent and Skill sources, the controller copies this setting to each owned Version, and archive downloads use the Version's copy. A change on the source reaches the Versions on the next reconcile.

Field Type Default Description enabled bool false When true, download requests are redirected to the storage backend via a pre-signed URL instead of proxied through the server. ttl duration 15m How long the pre-signed URL remains valid (e.g. "15m", "1h"). fallbackToProxy bool true When true, if pre-sign generation fails the server falls back to proxying the download. Set to false to make pre-signing strictly required. For Agent objects, the default is false. See agents.v1 Protocol.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The opendepot CLI installs skills and agents from OpenDepot registries into a project. It resolves each entry against the registry, verifies the signature and hashes, and writes the files into the project's install targets. The lock file records exactly what was installed so that verify can check it later without network access.

docs.title: Download the binary
docs.text:
The registry server serves prebuilt opendepot binaries, so users can install the CLI without a Go toolchain. The UI exposes them on the Download CLI page, and the same files are available directly from the server at the following public paths:

Path Returns /opendepot/cli/v1/{os}/{arch} The binary for one platform. /opendepot/cli/v1/SHA256SUMS SHA-256 checksums for every binary.

Supported platforms are darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and windows/amd64. Windows binaries end in .exe. Any other platform returns 404.

The example below runs on macOS and Linux. Set REGISTRY to your registry's base URL. Use -o to name the file. curl -O saves the binary as amd64, which breaks the checksum check. On Linux, replace shasum -a 256 -c with sha256sum -c.

REGISTRY=https://<registry-host>
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64 | amd64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
  arm64 | aarch64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "Unsupported architecture" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
BIN="opendepot_${OS}_${ARCH}"

curl -fsSL "$REGISTRY/opendepot/cli/v1/$OS/$ARCH" -o "$BIN"
curl -fsSL "$REGISTRY/opendepot/cli/v1/SHA256SUMS" -o SHA256SUMS
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing && \
  chmod +x "$BIN" && \
  sudo install -m 0755 "$BIN" /usr/local/bin/opendepot && \
  opendepot --version

On Windows, download opendepot_windows_amd64.exe from the same paths and verify it with Get-FileHash.

The server image bundles the binaries at /opt/opendepot/cli/. The image build sets the version with --build-arg CLI_VERSION=<version>, which defaults to dev. The server reads that directory from the -cli-dist-dir flag. If the directory has no binary for a platform, that platform returns 404, so local development without bundled binaries still works. The binaries are not GPG-signed. Use the checksum file to verify them.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose opendepot login <host> Log in to a registry with the login.v1 flow and store the token. <host> is a hostname such as registry.example.com. The registry must advertise login.v1. opendepot apply Resolve, verify, and install every entry in opendepot.hcl. opendepot plan Show what apply would change, comparing the project and lock file with the registry. Downloads and verifies content, then writes nothing. Never prompts. opendepot validate [path] Validate a SKILL.md, a skill directory, or an agent .md file. Defaults to the current directory when path is omitted. Frontmatter keys are checked against the union of all platform key sets. The command has no platform option. opendepot verify Check the installed targets against opendepot.lock.hcl without network access. opendepot list skills or opendepot list agents List the skills or agents on a registry. Read-only. See List skills and agents. opendepot describe skill <namespace/name> or opendepot describe agent <namespace/name> Show every detail for one resource. --json prints them as JSON.

Command failures are written to standard error in a distinct error section, with the source when available and the underlying details. Jev assessment output includes an Error row; none reported means the assessment did not report an error.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flags apply to opendepot apply unless noted. opendepot plan accepts --upgrade, --allow-yanked, --allow-older-versions, --trust-new-key, and --force with the same meaning, and it never prompts. A changed signing key appears as an error in the plan instead of a prompt.

Flag Purpose --upgrade Re-resolve version constraints instead of reusing the versions in the lock file. --allow-yanked Allow yanked versions. Without this flag, the CLI skips yanked versions for new resolution. --allow-older-versions Install an older matching version when a newer one is blocked, rejected, or failed assessment. See Allow older versions. --trust-new-key Re-pin a rotated signing key. Without this flag, a changed signing key fails the install. --no-prompt Never prompt. Fail instead of asking for confirmation. Use this in CI. --force Overwrite AGENTS.md blocks that were edited by hand.

docs.title: opendepot.hcl
docs.text:
opendepot.hcl declares the skills and agents a project uses. It has one optional opendepot block and any number of agent_skill and agent blocks.

opendepot {
  targets  = ["copilot", "claude"]
  registry = "registry.example.com"
}

agent_skill "release-notes" {
  source  = "registry.example.com/my-org/release-notes"
  version = "~> 1.2"
}

agent "code-reviewer" {
  source      = "registry.example.com/my-org/code-reviewer"
  version     = ">= 2.1.0, < 3.0.0"
  signing_key = "3E9A1F0C2B7D4E5A6F8091A2B3C4D5E6F7A8B9C0"
  path        = "tools/agents/code-reviewer.md"
}
Field Required Purpose source Yes The registry address of the skill or agent. version Yes A version constraint. signing_key No Pins the expected GPG signing key fingerprint. A mismatch fails the install and never prompts. path No Installs to this path instead of the default targets. A custom path replaces targets for that entry. targets In the opendepot block The install targets for entries that do not set path. registry No, in the opendepot block The registry host that opendepot list queries, such as registry.example.com. Use a bare host, not a URL. apply and plan ignore it.

Each block label is the local name of the entry. Names must be unique within the file. An entry needs at least one install target, from targets or from path.

docs.title: Install targets
docs.text:
The copilot and claude targets install into folders in your home directory, so they are shared by every project on the machine:

Target Skill Agent copilot ~/.copilot/skills/{name}/ ~/.copilot/agents/{name}.agent.md claude ~/.claude/skills/{name}/ ~/.claude/agents/{name}.md codex ~/.agents/skills/{name}/ ~/.codex/agents/{name}.toml agents-md A block in AGENTS.md A block in AGENTS.md

Agent files are copied as published. Claude agents use the .md format, and Copilot agents keep the .agent.md suffix.

Each agent format installs only to the targets that read it:

  • A Codex TOML agent ({name}.toml) installs only to codex, or to a custom path. It is never written to AGENTS.md, because that target would store the raw TOML in Markdown.
  • A Markdown agent ({name}.agent.md or {name}.md) installs to copilot, claude, and agents-md. It never installs to codex.

If an agent has no target that accepts its format, the install fails before anything is written. Add codex to targets for a TOML agent, or add copilot or claude for a Markdown agent.

To install into a project instead, set path on the entry, for example path = ".github/skills/release-notes". A custom path is relative to the project and replaces targets for that entry.

The agents-md target writes each entry into AGENTS.md between markers:

<!-- opendepot:begin release-notes -->
...installed content...
<!-- opendepot:end release-notes -->

The CLI refuses to overwrite a block that was edited by hand unless you pass --force.

docs.title: opendepot.lock.hcl
docs.text:
apply writes opendepot.lock.hcl next to opendepot.hcl. It records what was installed:

agent_skill "registry.example.com/my-org/release-notes" {
  version        = "1.2.4"
  constraints    = "~> 1.2"
  signing_key    = "3E9A1F0C2B7D4E5A6F8091A2B3C4D5E6F7A8B9C0"
  signature_hash = "h1:..."
  hashes         = ["h1:...", "zh:..."]

  installed "copilot" {
    path = "/Users/you/.copilot/skills/release-notes"
    hash = "h1:..."
  }
}
Field Purpose version The resolved version. constraints The constraint from opendepot.hcl that produced the version. signing_key The pinned GPG signing key fingerprint. signature_hash The hash of the signed SHA256SUMS file. hashes The h1: directory hash and the zh: archive hash of the package. installed One block per install target, labeled with the target name. Each records the path and the h1: hash of the installed content.

Commit this file. Paths for the copilot and claude targets are absolute home-directory paths, so the lock file is specific to the machine that last ran apply. Teammates on other machines get different paths after they run apply. Use path on an entry when the install must live in the repository.

Use opendepot verify in CI to confirm that the installed files match the lock file. To run it before each agent tool call, see Verify with Agent Hooks.

docs.title: File safety
docs.text:
The CLI does not follow symlinks. It refuses to read opendepot.hcl, opendepot.lock.hcl, and AGENTS.md when any of them is a symlink. It also refuses install targets that are symlinks. The error is refusing to follow symlink <path>. Writes and removals use the same check.

Archive extraction is limited to 2 GiB of decompressed data and 10,000 entries. An archive that exceeds either limit fails the install.

docs.title: agents.v1 protocol
docs.text:
For the full protocol reference, see agents.v1 Protocol.

The registry serves skills and agents under /opendepot/agents/v1/. {kind} is skills or agents. The CLI uses these endpoints:

Method Path Purpose GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/versions List available versions. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/download Return the archive location and checksums. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/archive Download the packaged archive. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/SHA256SUMS Return the checksums for the archive. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{version}/SHA256SUMS.sig Return the GPG signature for SHA256SUMS. GET /opendepot/agents/v1/catalog List the skills and agents the caller can see. Used by opendepot list.

The service discovery document advertises the base path as agents.v1. Requests are subject to GroupBinding authorization. Archive requests return a 307 redirect to a presigned URL when presign is enabled for the agent source. Otherwise the server streams the archive. A presigned URL remains valid until it expires, even after GroupBinding access is revoked. See agents.v1 protocol for details.

docs.title: Signing key trust
docs.text:
The first install pins the signing key that signed the package (trust on first use). Later installs must match the pinned key.

  • If signing_key is set in opendepot.hcl, the signer must match it. A mismatch fails and never prompts.
  • If the signer changes, the install fails until you re-run with --trust-new-key to re-pin the new key.
  • With --no-prompt, a changed key always fails.

docs.title: Plan before apply
docs.text:
opendepot plan runs the same resolution, verification, and staging as apply, then reports the result without writing any file or the lock file. Each entry shows a header with the locked and resolved versions and one row per install target:

Symbol Meaning + The target will be created. ~ The target will be updated to the planned content. ! The target was edited by hand. apply will overwrite it only with --force. = The target already matches. - A stale path or AGENTS.md block will be removed.

When the registry has a newer version than the lock file, the plan shows it with a note to run opendepot apply --upgrade. The plan ends with a summary, and opendepot apply writes it.

docs.title: List skills and agents
docs.text:
opendepot list skills and opendepot list agents show the skills or agents on a registry. The command is read-only. It writes no files, and it prints nothing until every page of the catalog has loaded.

Flag Purpose --registry <host> The registry host to query. Overrides the project setting. --namespace <name> List only the resources in one namespace. --json Print the catalog as JSON, with the full description for each item.

The CLI picks the registry in this order:

  1. The --registry flag.
  2. The registry attribute in the opendepot block of opendepot.hcl.
  3. The single host shared by every source in opendepot.hcl.

If none of these yields one host, the command fails. The error asks you to pass --registry, or to set registry in opendepot.hcl. With several different hosts in source, the error lists them.

Each row shows one skill or agent:

Column Meaning SOURCE The namespace/name of the resource. VERSION The latest installable version, or none. RISK The risk level and score of the latest version, or unknown. STATUS Whether the displayed version is available, plus any unavailable candidate's status. DESCRIPTION The first line of the latest installable version's description, with ANSI escape sequences deleted and other control or format characters replaced by spaces, and the text cut to 80 characters. The text is author-supplied. The table shows it as plain text. --json prints the full description.

Each resource takes one line. Use opendepot describe skill <namespace/name> or opendepot describe agent <namespace/name> to inspect a single resource. The table shows its source, sync and block state, usage counts, metadata, full description, storage backend and GitHub client settings, source scan findings, every version with its status and checksum, the latest Jev assessment, and the exemption, unblock, and threshold details. Empty fields are left out of the table. Description and other author text is shown as plain text, with ANSI escape sequences deleted and other control or format characters replaced by spaces. Lines wrap to the table width. --json prints every field, including definitionContent, as one object with stable keys. Empty values are null or []. The fields are listed in Detail fields for describe. Describe accepts --registry and uses the same registry selection and UI browse access rules as list. A version marked synced is not necessarily installable. See Unavailable candidates for the statuses.

If the registry has OIDC enabled, list needs a token. Run opendepot login <host> first. The listing then shows public resources and the resources that your GroupBindings allow.

The command reports these errors:

Response Message 401 or 403 Not authorized. The message includes the HTTP status and tells you to run opendepot login <host> and retry. 404 The registry does not support the agents.v1 catalog. It may be an older OpenDepot server. 5xx The catalog could not be listed. The message says that no results were shown.

docs.title: Blocked versions
docs.text:
A version that a Jev policy blocks is not installed. The registry lists it with blocked: true and the Jev block reasons, so the CLI does not treat it as missing. Resolution skips a blocked version and picks the highest unblocked match. When the only match is blocked, the CLI explains why in the same label-column layout it uses for Jev assessments. It names the source and version, the Jev status, each policy reason, and what to do next:

✖ registry.example.com/opendepot-system/anti-ui-slop@1.0.0
  Status       blocked by a Jev policy · not installable
  Reason       overall risk score 0.80 in part 1 is above the policy limit of 0.50
  Next         installs are refused until the policy allows this version

A locked version that becomes blocked gets the same output, with a Next line that says the lock file pins the version and to re-run with --upgrade. When no version satisfies the constraint, the error lists the published versions, marked (yanked) or (blocked) where they apply. Jev scores are shown during apply and plan and are not written to the lock file.

docs.title: Allow older versions
docs.text:
Resolution can also find a newer version that matches the constraint but cannot be installed. If that version is blocked, rejected, or failed assessment, and an older matching version is installable, apply and plan stop before they write anything. The error names the newer version, its status, and its reasons, and it suggests --allow-older-versions.

Pass --allow-older-versions to install the older version instead. Both apply and plan print a warning that names the newer version that was skipped. The flag does not bypass any of these checks:

  • Signature, hash, and signing-key verification.
  • Yank checks. Use --allow-yanked for yanked versions.
  • Jev blocks on the version that would be installed.

Some cases do not refuse:

  • A pending version is not a refusal. The CLI installs the best installable version without the flag.
  • An unversioned commit is never compared against a version constraint. It can add context to a refusal, but it cannot cause one by itself.

A locked version is never re-resolved by this flag. If the lock file pins a version that is now blocked, apply fails and asks you to re-run with --upgrade. To fall back to an older version after that, pass both --upgrade and --allow-older-versions.

Registries that predate the unavailableCandidates field do not report newer blocked versions. The CLI cannot see them on those registries, so it installs the best installable version without a refusal.

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text:
opendepot login registry.example.com
opendepot validate ./skills/release-notes
opendepot plan
opendepot apply
opendepot verify

In CI, run opendepot apply --no-prompt and then opendepot verify. Use opendepot plan in review steps to see the changes before they are applied.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Consuming Agents and Skills: install skills and agents into a project.
  • Publishing Agents and Skills: configure the Depots that publish them.
  • agents.v1 Protocol: the endpoints the CLI calls.

docs.title: Version Constraints
docs.text:
OpenDepot supports all standard OpenTofu version constraint syntax:

Syntax Example Meaning Exact 1.2.0 Only version 1.2.0 Comparison >= 1.0.0, < 2.0.0 Any 1.x version Pessimistic ~> 1.2.0 >= 1.2.0, < 1.3.0 (bugfixes only) Pessimistic (minor) ~> 1.2 >= 1.2.0, < 2.0.0 Exclusion >= 1.0.0, != 1.5.0 Any 1.x except 1.5.0

docs.title: Tags and branches
docs.text:
Skill and Agent sources use versionConstraints to select Git tags, or ref to follow a Git branch. The two are mutually exclusive.

  • Tags (versionConstraints) are the recommended default for stable content. Tags are usually more immutable than branches.
  • Branches (ref) publish a new Version on every push to the branch, once all checks pass. A branch head moves with every push. Each Version is still pinned to its exact sourceCommit.

immutable works on branch sources. A re-download must match the Version's recorded status.checksum, and a moving branch creates new Versions without changing existing ones. For the full behavior, see Branch sourcing.

docs.title: Kubernetes RBAC
docs.text:
The Helm chart creates ServiceAccounts and RBAC resources for each controller automatically when rbac.create: true, which is the default.

  • Controller Permissions

    Review the resources and verbs granted to the Depot, Module, Provider, Version, and Server components.

  • Namespace-Scoped RBAC

    Reduce the controller blast radius by replacing cluster-wide roles with namespace-scoped Role and RoleBinding resources.

  • Pipeline Publisher Role

    Grant a CI ServiceAccount the least privilege needed to create or update Module resources.

  • GroupBinding and Stats Visibility

    Understand how OIDC GroupBinding rules affect OpenDepot Workshop statistics and resource visibility.

docs.title: Choosing an RBAC Model
docs.text:
Use the default cluster-wide model when controllers must reconcile resources across namespaces. Use namespace-scoped mode when all managed resources live in the installation namespace and a smaller permission boundary is more important than multi-namespace reconciliation.

See Namespace-Scoped RBAC for the required Helm values and constraints.

docs.title: Controller Permissions
docs.text: The chart creates roles for each OpenDepot component. The Server receives write permissions only for scanpolicies, and only when server.policyManagement.enabled is true. The Depot, Module, Provider, and Version controllers reconcile resources and therefore receive write permissions.

docs.title: Permission Matrix
docs.text:
Controller Resource Verbs Depot depots create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Depot depots/finalizers update Depot depots/status get, patch, update Depot modules create, get, list, patch, update, watch Depot providers create, get, list, patch, update, watch Depot secrets get Module modules create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Module modules/finalizers update Module modules/status get, patch, update Module versions create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Version modules get, list, watch Version modules/status get, patch, update Version providers get, list, watch Version providers/status get, patch, update Version versions create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Version versions/finalizers update Version versions/status get, patch, update Version pods delete (namespace-scoped) Version secrets get Version configmaps create, get, list, patch, update, watch Version events (events.k8s.io) create, patch Provider providers create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Provider providers/finalizers update Provider providers/status get, patch, update Provider versions create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch Server versions get, list, watch Server modules get, list Server providers get, list, watch Server depots get, list, watch Server groupbindings get, list, watch Server namespaces get, list, watch Server configmaps get, list, watch Server scanpolicies get, list, watch; create, delete, patch, update only when server.policyManagement.enabled is true

Note

The depots rule is added to the Server ClusterRole only when ui.enabled: true. When the UI is disabled, the Server does not call the Depots API and the rule is omitted.

Controller permissions are generated by the Helm chart. Avoid editing the resulting Role or ClusterRole objects directly; configure the deployment with rbac.create and rbac.scopeToNamespace values instead.

The Version controller's pods/delete and secrets/get permissions are limited to global.namespace. With rbac.scopeToNamespace: true, they are included in the namespace-scoped Role. Otherwise, the chart still grants them through separate namespace-scoped Roles rather than widening the controller's main ClusterRole.

docs.title: Namespace-Scoped RBAC
docs.text:
By default, OpenDepot creates ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding resources so controllers can watch the entire cluster. For a smaller permission boundary, set:

rbac:
  scopeToNamespace: true

The chart then creates Role and RoleBinding resources instead. This limits controller permissions to global.namespace and reduces the blast radius if a controller is compromised.

docs.title: Resource Placement Requirement
docs.text:
All Module, Provider, Version, and Depot resources must reside in the same namespace as the controllers. Do not enable namespace-scoped mode when managed resources span multiple namespaces.

Warning

Namespace-scoped mode is a deployment-wide constraint. It is not a way to grant different controllers access to different namespaces.

docs.title: GitHub App Secrets
docs.text: The secrets: [get] permission required for GitHub App authentication is always granted through dedicated namespace-scoped Role objects, regardless of rbac.scopeToNamespace. Controller ClusterRole objects never grant Secret access.

docs.title: Pipeline Publisher Role
docs.text:
Use a dedicated ServiceAccount and least-privilege Role when a pipeline needs to create or update Module resources. For the complete workflow, see CI/CD Pipelines.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: opendepot-ci-publisher
  namespace: opendepot-system
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: opendepot-module-publisher
  namespace: opendepot-system
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["opendepot.defdev.io"]
    resources: ["modules"]
    verbs: ["create", "update", "patch", "get", "list"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: opendepot-ci-publisher-binding
  namespace: opendepot-system
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: opendepot-module-publisher
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: opendepot-ci-publisher
    namespace: opendepot-system

This Role does not grant permission to modify providers, versions, Secrets, or controller resources.

docs.title: GroupBinding and Stats Visibility
docs.text:
The OpenDepot Workshop Stats page, GET /opendepot/ui/v1/stats, aggregates only resources visible to the authenticated user.

For OIDC users with a matching GroupBinding, module and provider counts, version counts, storage bytes, and security findings are scoped to the resources permitted by that binding.

Users without a matching GroupBinding, including users in anonymous-auth or bearer-token mode, see all resources in labelled namespaces.

See GroupBinding Access Control for the full expression syntax and setup instructions.

docs.title: Storage Backends
docs.text:
OpenDepot stores module archives and provider binaries in a configurable storage backend. Choose the backend that matches your deployment environment.

  • Amazon S3

    Production object storage using AWS SDK credentials and optional pre-signed provider downloads.

  • Azure Blob Storage

    Production object storage using Azure identity and optional user delegation SAS URLs.

  • Google Cloud Storage

    Production object storage using Application Default Credentials and optional signed provider URLs.

  • Local Filesystem

    Shared-volume storage for development, testing, and air-gapped environments.

  • Pre-signed URL Redirects

    Let clients download provider binaries directly from object storage instead of proxying them through the Server.

docs.title: Storage Configuration Scope
docs.text:
storageConfig can be set at multiple levels:

  • Depot.spec.global.storageConfig applies to resources managed by a Depot unless overridden.
  • Module.spec.moduleConfig.storageConfig configures a module.
  • Provider.spec.providerConfig.storageConfig configures a provider.
  • Inline Version.spec.moduleConfigRef.storageConfig or Version.spec.providerConfigRef.storageConfig configures a version.

docs.title: Backend Comparison
docs.text: Feature Amazon S3 Azure Blob Google Cloud Storage Filesystem Production ready Yes Yes Yes With PVC Checksum validation SHA256 (native) SHA256 (metadata) SHA256 (metadata) SHA256 (computed) Authentication AWS SDK v2 defaults DefaultAzureCredential ADC None Server download route Yes Yes Yes Yes Shared volume required No No No Yes (PVC or hostPath) Pre-signed URL redirects Yes Yes Yes No

docs.title: Azure Blob Storage
docs.text: Azure Blob Storage is recommended for production deployments. It stores module archives and provider binaries. The SHA256 checksum is stored in the container's metadata.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description accountName string Yes Azure Storage Account name accountUrl string Yes Storage Account URL subscriptionID string Yes Azure subscription ID resourceGroup string Yes Resource Group containing the Storage Account 
storageConfig:
  azureStorage:
    accountName: opendepotmodules
    accountUrl: https://opendepotmodules.blob.core.windows.net
    subscriptionID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
    resourceGroup: opendepot-rg

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OpenDepot uses Azure DefaultAzureCredential. Common Kubernetes deployments use:

  • AKS with Workload Identity: Configure federated identity credentials on the Version controller's ServiceAccount. This is the recommended option.
  • Managed Identity: Assign a managed identity to the AKS node pool or pod.
  • Environment variables: Set AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, and AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET.

docs.title: Azure RBAC Roles
docs.text:
Assign these roles on the Storage Account:

  • Storage Blob Data Contributor for read, write, and delete operations.
  • Reader for container metadata operations.
  • Storage Blob Delegator when pre-signed URLs are enabled, to obtain a User Delegation Key for SAS generation.

See Pre-signed URL Redirects for configuration.

docs.title: Local Filesystem
docs.text: Filesystem storage writes artifacts to a shared volume mounted by both the Version controller and Server. It is suitable for development, testing, and air-gapped environments when paired with a PersistentVolumeClaim.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description directoryPath string Yes with fileSystem Artifact directory; must match storage.filesystem.mountPath

The Helm values are:

Value Default Description storage.filesystem.enabled false Enable the shared filesystem volume storage.filesystem.mountPath /data/modules Container mount path and Server download guard root storage.filesystem.hostPath "" Host path for local development with kind storage.filesystem.storageClassName "" StorageClass for the PVC; must support ReadWriteMany storage.filesystem.size 10Gi PVC size

Note

The CRD directoryPath must be the same as or inside storage.filesystem.mountPath. Module downloads outside that root are rejected.

docs.title: Local Development with kind
docs.text:
helm install opendepot opendepot/opendepot \
  -n opendepot-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --set storage.filesystem.enabled=true \
  --set storage.filesystem.hostPath=/tmp/opendepot-modules

With hostPath, the chart adds an init container that runs as root to set ownership of the mount path to UID 65532, the non-root user used by the application containers. Use this for local development only.

docs.title: Download Path Enforcement
docs.text: The Server rejects module download paths that resolve outside the configured mount directory with HTTP 403. The chart passes storage.filesystem.mountPath to the Server through the --filesystem-mount-path flag.

docs.title: Production with a PVC
docs.text:
helm install opendepot opendepot/opendepot \
  -n opendepot-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --set storage.filesystem.enabled=true \
  --set storage.filesystem.storageClassName=efs-sc \
  --set storage.filesystem.size=50Gi

The PVC requires a StorageClass that supports ReadWriteMany, such as AWS EFS, Azure Files, or NFS.

storageConfig:
  fileSystem:
    directoryPath: /data/modules

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text: Google Cloud Storage stores module archives and provider binaries with checksum metadata.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description bucket string Yes GCS bucket name 
storageConfig:
  gcs:
    bucket: opendepot-modules

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OpenDepot uses Application Default Credentials (ADC). Common Kubernetes deployments use:

  • GKE with Workload Identity: Bind a Google service account to the Version controller's Kubernetes ServiceAccount. This is the recommended option.
  • Service account key: Mount a JSON key file and set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The storage identity requires:

  • storage.objects.create for uploads
  • storage.objects.get for reads and metadata lookups
  • storage.objects.delete for removals

The Storage Object Admin role includes all three.

See Pre-signed URL Redirects for signed provider download configuration.

docs.title: Pre-signed URL Redirects
docs.text:
When enabled for provider downloads, the Server returns an HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect to a time-limited URL signed by the storage backend. OpenTofu or Terraform then downloads the provider directly, reducing bandwidth and egress through the Server.

Pre-signed URLs are supported for Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage. The filesystem backend does not support them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure presign on any StorageConfig:

storageConfig:
  s3:
    bucket: opendepot-providers
    region: us-east-1
  presign:
    enabled: true
    ttl: "15m"
    fallbackToProxy: true
Field Type Default Description enabled bool false Redirect downloads to the storage backend ttl duration 15m URL validity, such as "15m" or "1h" fallbackToProxy bool true Proxy through the Server if signing fails. When false, a signing failure returns 502 Bad Gateway.

docs.title: Agent Archives
docs.text:
Agent archives are served from the Agent Version, not from the agent source. The controller copies the source presign into each Version it owns, so the archive handler reads the presign settings from the Version. The sync runs on every reconcile of the Agent or Skill, so a change to presign on the source reaches every owned Version in one reconcile, including yanked and rejected Versions. A hand-edited presign on a Version is overwritten to match the source. Removing presign from the source clears it on the Versions. Other Version fields are not synced by this path. The behavior differs in three ways:

  • fallbackToProxy defaults to false for new Agent objects. When false, a signing failure returns 500 Internal Server Error and does not redirect. Providers and modules keep the true default.
  • The FileSystem backend always fails the signing step. Agent downloads from FileSystem storage stream the archive only when fallbackToProxy is true.
  • Existing Agent objects keep the stored fallbackToProxy value. The changed default applies only to objects created after the change.

A presigned URL redirect uses 307 Temporary Redirect with Cache-Control: private, no-store. The URL TTL defaults to 15m. Revoking a GroupBinding stops new redirects, but a URL already issued stays valid until it expires. This is an accepted window. For the authorization flow, see agents.v1 Protocol.

docs.title: Amazon S3
docs.text: No additional IAM permissions are needed. s3:GetObject, already required for the proxy path, is sufficient to generate signed GET URLs.

docs.title: Azure Blob Storage
docs.text: Azure uses user delegation SAS tokens. Assign the Storage Blob Delegator role to the controller's identity in addition to Storage Blob Data Contributor.

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text: GCS signs URLs with the Go SDK's default V2 scheme. When the workload identity has no private key, the signing call goes through IAM, which requires iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob, included in the Service Account Token Creator role, in addition to the existing storage permissions.

docs.title: Amazon S3
docs.text: S3 is recommended for production deployments. It stores module archives and provider binaries with SHA256 checksum validation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description bucket string Yes S3 bucket name region string Yes AWS region, such as us-west-2 key string No Object key prefix for stored artifacts 
storageConfig:
  s3:
    bucket: opendepot-modules
    region: us-west-2

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OpenDepot uses the AWS SDK v2 default credentials chain. Common Kubernetes deployments use:

  • EKS with IRSA: Annotate the Version controller's ServiceAccount with an IAM role ARN. This is the recommended option.
  • Environment variables: Set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and optionally AWS_SESSION_TOKEN.
  • EC2 instance profile: Use the profile available to the EKS nodes.

docs.title: IAM Permissions
docs.text:
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": [
    "s3:GetObject",
    "s3:PutObject",
    "s3:DeleteObject"
  ],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::your-bucket-name/*"
}

S3 requires no additional IAM permissions for pre-signed provider downloads; s3:GetObject is sufficient. See Pre-signed URL Redirects for configuration.
